parsed_message.title: fix(text3d): stop hole bridges self-intersecting glyph counters
parsed_message.description: stop hole bridges self-intersecting glyph counters
parsed_message.body:
MergeHoles picked the bridge from a hole (e.g. an 'O' counter) to the
outline by nearest distance alone, with no check that the segment
avoided cutting back through the glyph. A wrong-side pick produced a
self-intersecting polygon, which ear clipping triangulated into a
jagged shard visible through round counters.
Bridge candidates are now ranked by distance and validated with a real
segment-crossing test against the outline and every other hole in the
glyph, taking the first candidate that doesn't cross anything.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
parsed_message.raw:
fix(text3d): stop hole bridges self-intersecting glyph counters

MergeHoles picked the bridge from a hole (e.g. an 'O' counter) to the
outline by nearest distance alone, with no check that the segment
avoided cutting back through the glyph. A wrong-side pick produced a
self-intersecting polygon, which ear clipping triangulated into a
jagged shard visible through round counters.

Bridge candidates are now ranked by distance and validated with a real
segment-crossing test against the outline and every other hole in the
glyph, taking the first candidate that doesn't cross anything.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

parsed_message.title: fix(spout): restore CPU fallback so Spout receive isn't black on non-interop GPUs
parsed_message.description: restore CPU fallback so Spout receive isn't black on non-interop GPUs
parsed_message.body:
ForceGpuInteropOnly disabled Spout's auto/CPU share, assuming ReceiveTexture
would then fail. It doesn't: with neither share path available it returns true
and copies nothing, so the node reported 'Receiving WxH' over an empty texture.
Enable auto share (GPU interop with CPU fallback) and return no frame when
Spout has no working copy path.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

parsed_message.description: drop MATERIALSWEEPTEST's dead MaterialNode(bypassed) forwarding check
parsed_message.body:
140221d removed MaterialNode::GetMaterial()'s bypass-forwarding branch as
unreachable: MaterialNode has a mesh input plus per-map texture pins, so
it fails CanBypass()'s one-input rule and can never actually be bypassed
in the live graph (stale bypassed=true gets force-cleared on load). The
pre-existing MATERIALSWEEPTEST still force-set bypassed=true on a
standalone MaterialNode to exercise that now-removed path, so it started
failing CI. There's no reachable state left where this node forwards its
input's material, so there's nothing to sweep for it.

parsed_message.title: fix(build): missing <algorithm> include and structured-binding lambda capture breaking Linux/Windows CI
parsed_message.description: missing <algorithm> include and structured-binding lambda capture breaking Linux/Windows CI
parsed_message.body:
Modulation.h used std::clamp without including <algorithm> - macOS's
libc++ pulls it in transitively via <map>/<vector>, Linux's libstdc++
does not, so it only failed on Linux/Windows CI.
INFINITE_BYPASSSWEEPTEST's fail() lambda captured a structured binding
(category/name from `for (const auto& [category, name] : types)`) by
reference - invalid before C++20, silently accepted as an extension by
Apple Clang but correctly rejected by Linux Clang/GCC and MSVC. Replaced
with named locals bound from a plain pair reference.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

parsed_message.title: feat(fx): add missing feedback/resonance to Phaser, feedback damping to Flanger
parsed_message.description: add missing feedback/resonance to Phaser, feedback damping to Flanger
parsed_message.body:
Same idea as Reverb's FDN redesign - fix structural gaps that make these
kernels sound thin, without touching their existing param surface.
Phaser had no feedback path around the allpass cascade at all: signal ran
straight through N stages and out. Every real unit (Phase 90, Small Stone)
gets its resonant swoosh by feeding the chain's own output back into its
input to sharpen the notches; without it this was closer to a mild EQ
sweep. Added a fixed internal feedback loop (per-channel, so the existing
L/R cutoff spread isn't collapsed) - stable by construction since an
allpass cascade is unity-magnitude, so any |fb| < 1 can't blow up.
Flanger's feedback tap was unfiltered in both modes, so repeats stayed
full-bandwidth - real BBD/tape flanger loops always lose some top end on
every pass (the bucket-brigade compander's own bandwidth limit). Added a
fixed ~7kHz damping filter on the feedback tap only (not the dry wet-tap
output), so repeats darken without dulling the primary signal.
Chorus and Delay were left alone - both already have multi-voice/BBD
character or Hermite interpolation, ping-pong, tone tilt, and analog wow/
flutter, so there was no equivalent structural gap to fix.
Verified: AUDIOPARAMSWEEPTEST and AUDIOTEARDOWNSWEEPTEST pass for both
nodes (the rateDiv FAIL is the pre-existing documented blind spot shared
by Chorus/Flanger/Phaser/Tremolo, not a regression), DSPTEST passes.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

would have caught, since both check modulatability and save/load - not
numeric agreement between a control and its own consumer.

parsed_message.title: fix(gesture-recorder): capture shift-drag gestures while transport is paused
parsed_message.description: capture shift-drag gestures while transport is paused
parsed_message.body:
GestureRecorder timestamped both recording and playback off the same
clock, which the previous fix (0eb00b5) made freeze while the transport
is paused so a looping recording would hold still on pause. Side effect:
recording a new gesture while paused stamped every sample with the same
frozen time, so the trace had no duration and played back as a static
value instead of the drag that was just performed.
Split it into two clocks - the playback clock (unchanged, still freezes
on pause) and a new record clock that always advances regardless of
play state. NotifyMovement/MaybeFinishArmedRecording now timestamp
against the record clock, so shift+drag captures real motion whether
the transport is playing or paused; BeginFrame/GetPlaybackValue still
use the playback clock so looping recordings still freeze on pause.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
parsed_message.raw:
fix(gesture-recorder): capture shift-drag gestures while transport is paused

GestureRecorder timestamped both recording and playback off the same
clock, which the previous fix (0eb00b5) made freeze while the transport
is paused so a looping recording would hold still on pause. Side effect:
recording a new gesture while paused stamped every sample with the same
frozen time, so the trace had no duration and played back as a static
value instead of the drag that was just performed.

Split it into two clocks - the playback clock (unchanged, still freezes
on pause) and a new record clock that always advances regardless of
play state. NotifyMovement/MaybeFinishArmedRecording now timestamp
against the record clock, so shift+drag captures real motion whether
the transport is playing or paused; BeginFrame/GetPlaybackValue still
use the playback clock so looping recordings still freeze on pause.

parsed_message.raw:
feat(reverb): redesign FDN for Valhalla Vintage Verb-grade lushness

The old kernel sounded metallic and small/roomy: delay-length modulation
only ran in "analog" mode (a static FDN rings metallically), just 2
diffusion stages before an 8-line tank left the impulse response
periodic, delay lines topped out around 42ms (room-scale, not hall), and
the whole tank ran off one mono-summed input with a sign flip standing
in for stereo width.

- 8 -> 16 lines, Hadamard mix generalized to any power-of-two line count
- Delay lengths widened to ~20-77ms (hall-scale)
- 2 -> 4-stage Schroeder diffusion, run as independent L/R chains instead
  of one mono chain, so stereo width comes from real decorrelation
- Delay-length modulation now always on, not gated behind "analog" -
  this was the main source of the metallic ringing
- Added a fixed ~13kHz pre-tank bandwidth filter to soften the injected
  transient
- Per-channel predelay so stereo content survives into the diffusers

No param/UI surface change - all of this drives the existing 5 params +
analog + mix. Exempted from the KHS-simple control-count rule per user
request (2026-09-18); see feedback_audio_node_minimalism memory.

Verified: DSPTEST's RunReverbFixture (RT60 accuracy, predelay timing,
monotonic decay, damping effect, NaN/denormal tail) and the audio param/
teardown sweeps all pass; the sweep's decay/damping/predelay FAILs are
the pre-existing documented blind spot (EffectDefs.cpp comment), not a
regression.

bullets: VST3SCANTEST's "not silent" assertion failed against Surge XT
VST3EDITORSHOTTEST crashed Xvfb with an X_ChangeProperty BadAtom
parsed_message.body:
Both fixtures picked from Platform::EnumerateVST3Plugins() by
enumeration order. That was fine when tools/linux/test-plugins.sh
only ever installed one plugin, but build.yml's --full install step
(Linux clang, push-to-main only) also installs Surge XT + Surge XT
Effects, and those can sort ahead of the small DPF "Parameters"
plugin the fixtures were actually designed and verified against:
Effects' default patch, which genuinely renders silence for a
driven 440Hz tone with no other setup - not a host bug, confirmed
by every other check (instantiate/prepare/param/state) passing
against the same instance.
opening Surge XT Effects' (JUCE) editor - a real, separate,
open host-hardening question, but not one either fixture should
block on given its actual job is verifying the app's own
scan/render/param/editor-hosting plumbing against a known-good
target.
Both now prefer a plugin named "Parameters" when present, falling
back to the previous enumeration-order behavior otherwise.

only ever installed one plugin, but build.yml's --full install step
(Linux clang, push-to-main only) also installs Surge XT + Surge XT
Effects, and those can sort ahead of the small DPF "Parameters"
plugin the fixtures were actually designed and verified against:

  Effects' default patch, which genuinely renders silence for a

  opening Surge XT Effects' (JUCE) editor - a real, separate,
  open host-hardening question, but not one either fixture should
  block on given its actual job is verifying the app's own
  scan/render/param/editor-hosting plumbing against a known-good
  target.

Both now prefer a plugin named "Parameters" when present, falling

parsed_message.title: fix(arrange): fix unsynced Sample static waveform slicing to match the actual playback ratio
parsed_message.description: fix unsynced Sample static waveform slicing to match the actual playback ratio
parsed_message.body:
ArrangeComputeSampleStaticWave always used the synced-only
SampleClipWindowSeconds(length, sampleBpm) formula to decide how much of the
decoded source file to slice for the static waveform, regardless of sync
state. That formula is only mathematically consistent with the synced ratio
(liveBpm/sampleBpm); for an unsynced clip the actual playback ratio is
sampleBpm/origBpm, entirely independent of live tempo, so the displayed
waveform did not correspond to what was actually audible - editing Sample
BPM on an unsynced clip looked like it did nothing even though the rate
override was in fact changing.
Added an unsynced branch that derives windowSeconds from the box's own
live-tempo duration times the sampleBpm/origBpm ratio, matching
AudioEngine::RunTopology's formula exactly. Also updated the two stale
Sample BPM field comments (context menu and docked Clip Settings panel)
that still claimed sync-off means "no rate override applies" - the ratio
fix from the previous commit was already live there, only the comment was
wrong.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
parsed_message.raw:

decoded source file to slice for the static waveform, regardless of sync
state. That formula is only mathematically consistent with the synced ratio
(liveBpm/sampleBpm); for an unsynced clip the actual playback ratio is
sampleBpm/origBpm, entirely independent of live tempo, so the displayed
waveform did not correspond to what was actually audible - editing Sample
BPM on an unsynced clip looked like it did nothing even though the rate
override was in fact changing.

Added an unsynced branch that derives windowSeconds from the box's own
live-tempo duration times the sampleBpm/origBpm ratio, matching

that still claimed sync-off means "no rate override applies" - the ratio

parsed_message.title: fix(arrange): fix unsynced Sample BPM ratio, give clones private nodes
parsed_message.description: fix unsynced Sample BPM ratio, give clones private nodes
parsed_message.body:
Root cause of "Sample BPM edit does nothing while sync is off": Rebuild-
AudioTopology forced ClipWindow::sampleBpm to 0 whenever syncToTempo was
false, which permanently locked RunTopology's tempoRatioLive to 1.0
(native speed) regardless of the Sample BPM field. Fixes it with a new
frozen Clip::origBpm (captured once at import, never touched by later
edits) as the reference point: synced clips keep the existing bpm/
sampleBpm ratio, unsynced clips now use sampleBpm/origBpm - tempo-
independent, but reacting to the Sample BPM field like it always should
have. origBpm round-trips through Patch (new cliporigbpm tag, migrated
from sampleBpm for old patches) and is now compared in ArrangeContentEqual
so BPM/sync edits aren't silently dropped from undo.
Also fixes a real bug behind the user's "it's still sourcing from the
canvas node" intuition: a pasted/duplicated Sample clip kept the original
clip's srcUid, so two clips could contend over one node's single WSOLA
stretcher/cursor. ArrangeRespawnCloneNode now gives every pasted/
duplicated Sample clip (audio, video, or image) its own hidden
(hiddenFromCanvas) node and kicks a fresh decode of the same file,
tracked via a new ArrangePendingImport::isClone flag so the clone's
already-correct sampleBpm/origBpm/length aren't re-estimated and
overwritten when the decode lands. Split's two halves are left sharing
one node since they never play simultaneously on the same lane.
WsolaStretcher was already extracted to its own shared header
(audio/dsp/WsolaStretcher.h, prior commit) so this and the canvas
AudioFilePlayerAudioNode use the exact same stretch algorithm.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

parsed_message.title: fix(arrange): stop unsynced Sample length reacting to global tempo, fix blank waveform on paste/duplicate
parsed_message.description: stop unsynced Sample length reacting to global tempo, fix blank waveform on paste/duplicate
parsed_message.body:
ArrangeResyncUnsyncedSampleLengths (added last round) recomputed an
unsynced clip's length from its full sourceDurationSeconds every time the
live transport BPM changed - even for a clip the user had manually
trimmed/split, snapping its length back and looking like random cutting.
An unsynced clip's length should only ever change from an explicit,
manual edit (the Sample BPM field, sync toggle, or a drop) - never from
the global tempo alone. Removed the function and its per-frame poll
entirely.
Separately: ArrangePasteAt and ArrangeDuplicateSelection give a copied
Sample clip a brand new id (the static-waveform cache's key) but never
called ArrangeRefreshSampleStaticWave for it, so every pasted/duplicated
Sample clip rendered with no waveform at all until some unrelated edit
happened to touch it. Both call sites now refresh the cache for every
newly created id.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

parsed_message.title: fix(arrange): sync Sample static waveform cache and unsynced clip length to live tempo
parsed_message.description: sync Sample static waveform cache and unsynced clip length to live tempo
parsed_message.body:
The static waveform cache (ArrangeComputeSampleStaticWave) always inverted
the synced-clip length formula (TicksToSeconds(length, sampleBpm)) even for
unsynced clips, so it sliced the wrong sub-range of the decoded source file
the moment sync was off - the drawn waveform no longer matched what was
actually audible. Added SampleClipWindowSeconds() as the exact inverse of
SampleClipLengthTicks, branching on syncToTempo the same way, and wired
ArrangeRefreshSampleStaticWave() into every UI site that edits sync/Sample
BPM so the cache never goes stale.
Also: an unsynced clip's length only ever tracked explicit edits to the
Sample BPM field, never a live change to the global project tempo - so
turning off sync and then adjusting the transport BPM (rather than the
per-clip field) still visibly grew/shrank the clip's rendered length even
though nothing about the clip itself changed. Added
ArrangeResyncUnsyncedSampleLengths(), polled once per frame alongside the
existing ArrangePollMediaImports(), which recomputes length + refreshes the
static wave for every unsynced Sample clip when the live tempo moves.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
parsed_message.raw:
fix(arrange): sync Sample static waveform cache and unsynced clip length to live tempo

The static waveform cache (ArrangeComputeSampleStaticWave) always inverted
the synced-clip length formula (TicksToSeconds(length, sampleBpm)) even for
unsynced clips, so it sliced the wrong sub-range of the decoded source file
the moment sync was off - the drawn waveform no longer matched what was
actually audible. Added SampleClipWindowSeconds() as the exact inverse of
SampleClipLengthTicks, branching on syncToTempo the same way, and wired
ArrangeRefreshSampleStaticWave() into every UI site that edits sync/Sample
BPM so the cache never goes stale.

Also: an unsynced clip's length only ever tracked explicit edits to the
Sample BPM field, never a live change to the global project tempo - so
turning off sync and then adjusting the transport BPM (rather than the
per-clip field) still visibly grew/shrank the clip's rendered length even
though nothing about the clip itself changed. Added
ArrangeResyncUnsyncedSampleLengths(), polled once per frame alongside the
existing ArrangePollMediaImports(), which recomputes length + refreshes the
static wave for every unsynced Sample clip when the live tempo moves.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

parsed_message.title: fix(build): pin Linux FFmpeg FetchContent to immutable BtbN release tag
parsed_message.description: pin Linux FFmpeg FetchContent to immutable BtbN release tag
parsed_message.body:
BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds' "latest" tag is a rolling pointer whose assets get
replaced in place, so the pinned SHA256 hashes go stale over time and
break fresh CMake configures with a hash-mismatch FetchContent
failure (hit on arm64 during Linux Phase 5 AppImage work). Repin all
four linux64/linuxarm64 gpl/lgpl shared archives to the immutable
autobuild-2026-09-15-13-18 tag with hashes verified by downloading and
sha256sum'ing the tarballs directly, and document the re-pin process
for next time.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

parsed_message.title: fix(arrange): time-stretch Sample BPM sync instead of pitch-shifting, fix unsynced length drift
parsed_message.description: time-stretch Sample BPM sync instead of pitch-shifting, fix unsynced length drift
parsed_message.body:
Tempo sync on an Audio Sample clip drove the same varispeed read-rate
scaling as the Pitch knob, so any BPM-sync change also shifted pitch.
Added a real-time-safe WSOLA time-stretcher (AnalyzeNodes.cpp) so sync
now changes duration while preserving pitch; Pitch stays varispeed.
Clip::length's recompute formula was only correct while synced, but was
also applied when syncToTempo was off, desyncing the clip's declared
length from its actual (untouched) audio duration whenever Sample BPM
was edited. Arrange::SampleClipLengthTicks() now branches on
syncToTempo so unsynced clips keep their real duration.

parsed_message.description: pin Linux FFmpeg FetchContent to immutable BtbN release tag
parsed_message.body:
BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds' "latest" tag is a rolling pointer whose assets get
replaced in place, so the pinned SHA256 hashes go stale over time and
break fresh CMake configures with a hash-mismatch FetchContent
failure (hit on arm64 during Linux Phase 5 AppImage work). Repin all
four linux64/linuxarm64 gpl/lgpl shared archives to the immutable
autobuild-2026-09-15-13-18 tag with hashes verified by downloading and
sha256sum'ing the tarballs directly, and document the re-pin process
for next time.

parsed_message.title: feat(linux): implement VST3 X11 plugin editors (P4 task 4.3)
parsed_message.description: implement VST3 X11 plugin editors (P4 task 4.3)
parsed_message.body:
Ports the editor-window path from PluginVST3Win.cpp to X11: opens a
top-level window sized from IPlugView::getSize(), sets WM_NAME +
WM_DELETE_WINDOW, and embeds the plugin's view via
kPlatformTypeX11EmbedWindowID. Adds one process-wide
Steinberg::Linux::IRunLoop, exposed both through the host IPlugFrame
(for editors) and through HostApplication's host-context queryInterface
(so a plugin can register fd/timer handlers via IPluginFactory3::
setHostContext with no editor open at all - JUCE/DPF both rely on this).
PluginVST3PumpEditorEvents pumps the run loop then drains X11 events for
our windows with a 4ms wall-clock budget, handling WM_DELETE_WINDOW and
resize (ConfigureNotify -> onSize). Every plugin-facing call routes
through the existing RunPluginCallGuarded sigsetjmp/siglongjmp crash
guard. main.cpp's frame-loop pump call sites no longer gate on
AnyPluginEditorOpen(), since factory-context timers need servicing even
with no editor open (verified this is a no-op cost when idle on macOS/
Windows too - CFRunLoopRunInMode(..., 0.0, ...) and PeekMessageW both
return immediately with nothing queued).
Uses a dedicated X11 connection (XOpenDisplay), not GLFW's own
(glfwGetX11Display): GLFW's frame-loop pump unconditionally drains its
connection's entire event queue every frame and silently discards
events for windows it doesn't own (verified against the vendored GLFW
source, x11_window.c's processEvent/_glfwPollEventsX11). Sharing the
connection would mean GLFW eats every editor-window event before this
code ever runs, since glfwPollEvents() runs earlier in the same frame
iteration - breaking window-close and live resize. A second connection
avoids the conflict; X11 window ids are server-side and connection-
agnostic, so IPlugView::attached() still embeds correctly.
CMakeLists.txt links X11 into the Infinite target only (not
infinite-vst3-scanner, which stays headless for out-of-process
scanning) - verified via ldd.
Verified: clean container build (both targets), xvfb-harness.sh --fast
run twice with the same 5 failures both times, all pre-existing per
known-test-failures-linux.txt (AUDIOLIFECYCLETEST/AUDIORECOVERYTEST
container timing flakes, GROUPTEST unrelated pre-existing issue,
PLUGINSCANTEST/AUDIOPARAMSWEEPTEST - the latter fails on ALSA card
enumeration in this container run, unrelated to VST3/editor code, no
code path touched by this change). No new regressions.
Still open within P4: task 4.4 (CI test with a real downloaded plugin -
the editor path above is implemented but unexercised end-to-end without
one) and task 4.5 (sweep/cleanup).

parsed_message.title: Extract C++ namespaces into the AST symbol graph
parsed_message.description: Extract C++ namespaces into the AST symbol graph
parsed_message.body:
build_ast_graph.py previously walked namespace_definition bodies without
pushing the namespace name onto the scope stack, so namespace-scoped
free functions lost their qualifying prefix and namespaces themselves
(Platform, GLUtil, etc.) never got a symbol entry at all. Gave
namespace_definition the same push/emit/recurse/pop treatment already
used for class_specifier/struct_specifier. Anonymous namespaces recurse
without pushing a scope name. Symbol count: 6,930 -> 7,279 (+79
namespace entries, plus corrected prefixes for functions inside them).
Re-ran the eval suite after rebuilding the index: AST Symbol & Caller
Precision 57.8% -> 59.4%, aggregate 86.1% -> 86.5%. Smaller than the
back-of-envelope estimate (~68-70%/89%) I gave beforehand — turned out
"Platform" was already earning partial credit pre-fix because the
scoring substring-matches against retrieved snippet text, and every
indexed ast_symbol doc for that subsystem literally contains the word
"platform" in its templated description, independent of whether the
symbol itself existed in the graph. The fix is still a net real gain
and closes a genuine blind spot (namespace-scoped symbols/callers were
invisible to blast-radius queries before this).
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

used for class_specifier/struct_specifier. Anonymous namespaces recurse
without pushing a scope name. Symbol count: 6,930 -> 7,279 (+79

scoring substring-matches against retrieved snippet text, and every
indexed ast_symbol doc for that subsystem literally contains the word
"platform" in its templated description, independent of whether the
symbol itself existed in the graph. The fix is still a net real gain
and closes a genuine blind spot (namespace-scoped symbols/callers were
invisible to blast-radius queries before this).

Cognitive-twin tooling for Infinite: AST/git/docs/skills extractors feeding
an 8,070-row hybrid FTS5+dense SQLite index, distilled System1/System2
reasoning schemas, SFT+DPO training datasets, a brain_core.py reasoning

  attempt had only saved a config, never actual adapter weights) via
  mlx_lm.lora; had to drop to batch-size=1 + --grad-checkpoint to fit the

  86.1%) by grounding a per-subsystem anchor-symbol table in brain_core.py:
  architecturally load-bearing symbols (ParamMailbox, INode, ...) that own
  the invariant behind most bugs in a subsystem but are rarely named in the
  bug report's own words, so the lexical scorer never found them. Anchors
  only inject if they still resolve against the live AST graph, so a
  rename/removal is a silent no-op rather than a fabricated citation.

  one (jinaai/jina-embeddings-v2-base-code) and measured a regression
  (57.8% -> 54.4%): 86% of the indexed corpus (ast_symbol rows) has no
  actual code in its embedded text, just a templated one-line description,

parsed_message.title: Fix Sample split waveform/seek with a source-offset field
parsed_message.description: Fix Sample split waveform/seek with a source-offset field
parsed_message.body:
A split Sample clip's right half kept srcUid but had no way to know
where in the source file its own audio actually starts, so its static
waveform restretched the whole decoded file across its rect (showing
the file's start again instead of continuing the left half's shape)
and AudioEngine's retrigger/seek math always seeked relative to the
file's own beginning.
Add Clip::sourceOffsetSeconds (Sample-only): how far into the decoded
source buffer a clip's audio starts. Split() derives it for the right
half from the cut point converted ticks -> seconds via the clip's own
sampleBpm (tempo-invariant by construction). CarveRange - the same
implicit-split shape used by PlaceOverwrite and DuplicateBlock - gets
the identical treatment for both its "strictly contains" and "overlaps
right edge" cases.
Plumb the field through ClipWindow (AudioEngine.h/.cpp) so the exact-
seek lookahead folds it into elapsedSeconds before the existing pitch/
tempo-ratio scaling, and through ArrangeComputeSampleStaticWave (main.cpp)
so the static-waveform cache slices peaks to a clip's own sub-range of
the decoded file instead of the whole thing - triggered at import time
(offset 0) and now also at both Split call sites via the new
ArrangeRefreshSampleStaticWave helper.
Audit: TrimEdge/TrimGroupEdge share the same start-edge-moves shape but
are out of this fix's scope - flagged as a follow-up task rather than
folded in here.

parsed_message.title: Static Sample waveforms, Sample BPM UI, and click-to-scrub
parsed_message.description: Static Sample waveforms, Sample BPM UI, and click-to-scrub
parsed_message.body:
Step 2: Audio Samples now draw a static peak array computed once at
import/bounce time from the fully-decoded source buffer
(ArrangeComputeSampleStaticWave, called from ArrangePollMediaImports
right after OpenFromDecoded/before length is set), stretched linearly
across the clip regardless of BPM warp. Stored in a new
gArrangeSampleStaticWaves map, kept mutually exclusive per clip id with
the existing gArrangeClipWaves live-fill cache (Audio Clip, unchanged).
Because ArrangeApplyClipBounceResult sets sampleDropped=true before
routing through the same pending-import/poll path a drag-drop import
uses, "Bounce to Sample" gets the static wave and sourceDurationSeconds
for free, with no separate bounce-specific code.
Step 2: click-to-scrub on a Sample's body, reusing the ruler's
ArrangeScrubBegin/Update/End and xToTick/gridSnap conversion. Bound to
middle-click rather than any left-click combination, since every
left-click gesture on a clip (plain, Alt, Cmd/Ctrl, Shift, on the body
or an edge) is already claimed by select/drag/trim/group-scale/blade -
this is purely additive. gArrangeScrubButton tracks which button drives
the current scrub so the ruler's own release/continuation logic works
for either source without the two colliding.
Step 3: "Sample BPM" field (with a relocated, isSample-gated "Sync to
Tempo" checkbox) in the docked Clip Settings panel's Audio Sample
branch, editing sampleBpm and recomputing length from the persisted
sourceDurationSeconds via ArrangeEdit. Same fields added to the
right-click context menu, gated on sampleDropped - it previously showed
an ungated "Sync to Tempo" checkbox that silently applied to a
manually-patched Audio Clip too (step 5 consistency-sweep finding).
Step 5: verified the multi-select bulk-edit panel has no gain/pan/
pitch/BPM controls at all, so a mixed Sample+Clip selection can't leak
BPM edits onto a Clip; verified the retrigger-conflict guard is
unaffected and still Sample-only.

parsed_message.title: Add live BPM-sync rate override for Audio Samples
parsed_message.description: Add live BPM-sync rate override for Audio Samples
parsed_message.body:
Step 3's playback side. New AudioNode::SetClipRateOverride(ratio),
mirroring SetClipPitchOverride, applied in AudioFilePlayerAudioNode's
per-sample varispeed read alongside the existing pitch ratio via a new
ParamMailbox slot. Adds AudioFileNode::Buffer() so the arrange layer can
read the decoded source for its static waveform (step 2).
ClipWindow gains sampleBpm (0 when not synced) instead of a ratio baked
at topology-rebuild time: tempo changes deliberately never trigger a
topology rebuild (ticks are tempo-invariant across the model), so a
baked ratio would go stale on a live tempo edit. RunTopology instead
computes tempo/sampleBpm fresh every block from the live project tempo
it already reads, and pushes that through SetClipRateOverride.
Step 4: the discontinuity-gated SeekToClipOffset's elapsedSeconds is
now also scaled by this same live ratio, alongside the existing
pitchRatio scaling, so a retrigger seeks to the tempo-corrected offset
instead of the file's native-speed offset.
SamplerNode is intentionally not touched: ArrangeImportMediaFile and
ArrangeApplyClipBounceResult only ever spawn an "Audio File" node for
an Arrange audio clip, so SamplerNode can never be a clip's
terminal.sourceNode - AudioNode::SetClipRateOverride's default no-op is
already correct there, and adding an unreachable override would be
dead code.

parsed_message.title: Fix cache budget, audio cursor, clip-bounce scope and Windows media type
parsed_message.description: Fix cache budget, audio cursor, clip-bounce scope and Windows media type
parsed_message.body:
Follow-ups to cae4444, from a review of that commit.
Platform.mm - the scrub frame cache no longer being cleared on seek is what
makes scrubbing cheap, but it also means each handle now grows to its ceiling
and stays there. The 512 MB cap was per handle, so a four-clip project would
have sat on 2 GB of decoded frames. It is now one budget for the whole app,
with handles registered so eviction takes the globally least-recently-used
frame. That makes the cache shared state, and video decoding is not
single-threaded (ArrangeMediaImport opens a dropped clip and pulls its first
frame on a worker), so the registry, the clock and every frameCache touch are
behind a mutex. Also: a per-handle entry ceiling so the linear LRU scans stay
cheap for small frames; kReverseLookbackSeconds is used again rather than a
literal, and its comment now describes the 0.5s the code actually does; the
nearest-frame cache fallback no longer serves a frame up to 25 ms AHEAD of
the request; and the no-frame-produced path no longer records readerPts at a
position the reader is not at, which made the next call resume forward
decoding from the wrong place.
AudioEngine - the retrigger pass walked its cursor to numWindows once the
playhead passed the last clip and stored it there. The render pass reads that
as out of range and restarts at 0, so every block after the last clip paid a
full forward walk of the lane - the opposite of the O(1) the cursor exists
for. Clamped before storing.
main.cpp - "Bounce / Render Clip" bounded its range to the selected clips but
scoped output by lane, so another clip sharing that lane inside the range was
rendered into the bounce. Added a clip scope alongside the lane scope, honored
by the audio scheduler, the video collector and the live-source refusal sweep
(which would otherwise refuse a bounce over a camera on a clip it was not
rendering). A builder that resolves no clips now leaves an empty range and
fails visibly instead of writing four beats of silence.
The render dialog's source logic moved out of popup lambdas into
ArrangeRenderEffectiveAudioSource / ArrangeRenderEffectiveVideoSource, because
ARRANGERENDERTEST's section E was asserting against a private copy of the
logic cae4444 deleted - it kept passing while the shipping behaviour changed.
E now drives the shipping helpers, and a new E2 covers the clip scope. Removed
the code the dropdowns left stranded (sArrangeRenderCanvasUid,
ArrangeRenderCollectOutputNodes, the unreachable canRender clauses) and marked
Settings::renderAudioSource/renderVideoSource deprecated - they are still
serialized for file-format compatibility but nothing reads them.
MediaWin.cpp - MF_MT_YUV_MATRIX was being set on inType, which is
MFVideoFormat_RGB32 and has no YUV matrix. SetInputMediaType can reject the
unexpected attribute, and the SUCCEEDED(hr) chain would then abort recorder
setup silently. Dropped from inType; outType keeps it, and inType keeps the
full-range tag that tells the converter what our RGB is.
Verified: builds clean, hygiene fast tier 30/30, video/media/ui groups pass.
RECEXPORTTEST, AUDIOLIFECYCLETEST and AUDIORECOVERYTEST fail identically on
main in this session - no audio device available (CoreAudio -10875).
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

parsed_message.body:
Video Samples and Audio Samples on the Arrangement Timeline now only hard-seek
their underlying source when the arrangement's target position actually
diverges from where the node's own clock already is (a scrub, a loop wrap not
yet caught up, or a fresh Play landing mid-clip), instead of forcing an
absolute seek every frame. Continuous playback lets each node's normal
wall-clock/block-accumulated position tracking do the work, which stops the
sub-frame jitter that was fighting Platform::VideoFrameAt's forward-resume
fast path and causing stutter/hangs during ordinary playback.
WrapPosition(), and add SyncToArrangement()/SeekTo() so the Arrangement
Timeline can compare against the same wrapped position and only reset when
it differs by more than one frame (VideoSourceNode.h, VideoSourceNode.cpp).
mLastBlockEndBeat and only call SeekToClipOffset on sampleDropped windows
when a real discontinuity is present (AudioEngine.h/.cpp, AnalyzeNodes.cpp).
(ArrangeModel.h, Patch.cpp/.h, PatchJson.cpp, AudioNode.h, SamplerNode.cpp,
WavetableSynthCore.h, main.cpp).
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(arrange): gate Arrangement Sample seeks on real discontinuities

Video Samples and Audio Samples on the Arrangement Timeline now only hard-seek
their underlying source when the arrangement's target position actually
diverges from where the node's own clock already is (a scrub, a loop wrap not
yet caught up, or a fresh Play landing mid-clip), instead of forcing an
absolute seek every frame. Continuous playback lets each node's normal
wall-clock/block-accumulated position tracking do the work, which stops the
sub-frame jitter that was fighting Platform::VideoFrameAt's forward-resume
fast path and causing stutter/hangs during ordinary playback.

- VideoSourceNode: factor the trim/loop wrap math out of CookIfNeeded into
  WrapPosition(), and add SyncToArrangement()/SeekTo() so the Arrangement
  Timeline can compare against the same wrapped position and only reset when
  it differs by more than one frame (VideoSourceNode.h, VideoSourceNode.cpp).
- AudioEngine: detect per-block discontinuities against a persisted
  mLastBlockEndBeat and only call SeekToClipOffset on sampleDropped windows
  when a real discontinuity is present (AudioEngine.h/.cpp, AnalyzeNodes.cpp).
- Wire up Arrangement clip retriggering and related model/patch plumbing
  (ArrangeModel.h, Patch.cpp/.h, PatchJson.cpp, AudioNode.h, SamplerNode.cpp,
  WavetableSynthCore.h, main.cpp).

parsed_message.title: test(linux): wire CameraLinux's YUYV/MJPEG converters into INFINITE_CAMERACONVTEST
parsed_message.description: wire CameraLinux's YUYV/MJPEG converters into INFINITE_CAMERACONVTEST
parsed_message.body:
CameraLinux.cpp already exposed YuyvToRgbaForTest/MjpegToRgbaForTest
"for INFINITE_CAMERACONVTEST in main.cpp" per its own file comment, but
nothing actually called them - no camera self-test existed anywhere in
main.cpp yet. Adds RunCameraConvTest(), gated __linux__: builds a
synthetic 2x2 YUYV buffer and checks the converted color is a
recognizable red, then round-trips a synthetic solid-color image
through stb_image_write's in-memory JPEG encoder and CameraLinux's own
MJPEG decoder, checking the recovered color survives JPEG's lossy
compression within a generous tolerance. This is the only way to
exercise the MJPEG-format webcam path without a real camera device -
neither CI nor any container here has one.

MJPEG sub-checks); macOS build still compiles clean with the new
__linux__-gated code inert.

every frame"). Windows's MediaWin.cpp has no equivalent and reseeks on
every backward step same as Linux did, but gets away with it via
Media Foundation's hardware-accelerated seek. This confirms a reverse-
frame cache is a genuine, already-proven cross-platform requirement for
a software decoder, not a Linux-only quick fix - so this ports macOS's
existing design rather than inventing new architecture:
nothing new for it, before ever touching the decode thread.
already covered by the cache, and on a real backward seek, seeks

frames decoded on the way there repopulate the cache and buy several

or fast-scrub step triggered a full av_seek_frame + avcodec_flush_buffers
on MediaLinux's decode thread - the thread's jumpedBackward check fires
on every step during reverse playback since the target position keeps
moving behind the last delivered frame.

Initially suspected a Linux-specific GOP misconfiguration (a 2-second
GOP meant a short test clip could have only one keyframe). Shrinking
gop_size to fps/4 was tested and disproved that: the x264 log confirmed
the encoder config changed (keyint 7 vs 60, 9 I-frames vs 1), but

- VideoHandle gains a `frameCache` (FIFO by pts, capped at 256MB).
- Every frame VideoFrameAt delivers (forward or backward) is cached.
- VideoFrameAt serves a request from the cache when the ready queue has
  nothing new for it, before ever touching the decode thread.

  already covered by the cache, and on a real backward seek, seeks
  kReverseLookbackSeconds behind the target (not exactly to it) so the
  frames decoded on the way there repopulate the cache and buy several
  more reverse steps before the next real seek.

parsed_message.title: fix(test): correct VIDEOAUDIOTEST's hardcoded expected audio duration
parsed_message.description: correct VIDEOAUDIOTEST's hardcoded expected audio duration
parsed_message.body:
The test asserted the recorded audio track was ~1.5s (the file-audio
tone clip's own length), but all three platforms' recorders
(Platform.mm's AppendAudioUpToLocked, MediaWin.cpp's and
MediaLinux.cpp's WriteFileAudioTrack) deliberately loop a shorter
file-audio source to fill the *video's* full recorded duration when
AudioFileNode::loop is true (its default) - confirmed identical
intent in all three implementations. The test's own fixture never
disables looping, so on every platform the real recorded audio is
~2.0s (60 frames / 30fps), not 1.5s.
This was never a Linux bug: it surfaced here only because the Linux
port is the first time this test exercised a real recorder end to
end. Compare against the actual recorded video duration instead of a
hardcoded constant.

~2.0s (60 frames / 30fps), not 1.5s.

port is the first time this test exercised a real recorder end to
end. Compare against the actual recorded video duration instead of a
hardcoded constant.

parsed_message.title: fix(arrange): fix ArrangeSliderFloat text-edit race/focus-steal, wire up clip retriggering
parsed_message.description: fix ArrangeSliderFloat text-edit race/focus-steal, wire up clip retriggering
parsed_message.body:
ArrangeSliderFloat's double-click-to-edit raced with its own click-drag
path (a value would snap to the click position for one frame before the
text box opened), and hover-to-type could steal keystrokes from any other
focused widget since it only checked "not this slider", not "nothing else
active". Both are fixed by deferring a fresh click's activation until it's
known whether a second click, a real drag, or neither follows, and by
gating hover-to-type on no widget anywhere holding ActiveId.
Also closes a gap in ArrangeContentEqual: pan/pitch/opacity/color-grade/
retrigger were missing from the gesture-undo content diff, so dragging
those sliders changed the live value but pushed no undo entry and never
marked the patch dirty.
Clip::retrigger existed in the model, was serialized, and had a UI
dropdown, but nothing in the audio engine ever read it - Timeline
(Continuous) and Retrigger on Enter were audibly identical. Wires it up:
AudioNode gets a RequestRetrigger() hook (AudioFilePlayerAudioNode reuses
its existing Restart request), AudioTerminal carries the clip's source
node, and RunTopology gets a lookahead pass that seeks the node before it
cooks a block whose span crosses a retrigger window's start. When a
node is shared across more than one lane, retrigger is suppressed for
those clips (falls back to continuous) rather than let two lanes fight
over one playback position, and the Clip Settings panel shows why.

parsed_message.title: feat(linux): implement video decode and recorder in MediaLinux.cpp
parsed_message.description: implement video decode and recorder in MediaLinux.cpp
bullets: Set AVCodecContext::pkt_timebase before avcodec_open2() so
The real root cause: the decode thread's backward-seek detection
parsed_message.body:
Real FFmpeg/libx264-backed VideoOpen/VideoFrameAt/RecorderStart/
RecorderAppend(Audio)/RecorderStop for Linux, replacing the P3 stubs.
Includes two correctness fixes found while chasing RunRecExportTest
reporting 35-54 spurious video "flash onsets" instead of the expected 5:
frame->best_effort_timestamp's B-frame reorder math uses the right
timebase.
compared the caller's requested target against its own readahead
buffer-ahead progress (a thread-local decode-head position) instead of
against what had actually been delivered to the caller. Since the
readahead queue intentionally decodes ahead of the consumer by design,
this made every normal readahead cycle look like the caller seeking
backward, forcing an av_seek_frame + avcodec_flush_buffers + queue-clear
on nearly every loop iteration - a livelock that could never make real
forward progress in a clip with no interior keyframes near the target.
Fixed by judging the backward-seek check against
VideoHandle::deliveredSeconds (the position actually handed to the
caller via VideoFrameAt), and made that field a std::atomic<double>
since it's written by one thread and read by another.
Verified via three consecutive clean INFINITE_RECEXPORTTEST runs (0ms
drift/offset/lead on every one of the 5 audio/video markers) and a full
headless-tests.sh pass under Xvfb.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
parsed_message.raw:
feat(linux): implement video decode and recorder in MediaLinux.cpp

Real FFmpeg/libx264-backed VideoOpen/VideoFrameAt/RecorderStart/
RecorderAppend(Audio)/RecorderStop for Linux, replacing the P3 stubs.

Includes two correctness fixes found while chasing RunRecExportTest
reporting 35-54 spurious video "flash onsets" instead of the expected 5:

- Set AVCodecContext::pkt_timebase before avcodec_open2() so
  frame->best_effort_timestamp's B-frame reorder math uses the right
  timebase.
- The real root cause: the decode thread's backward-seek detection
  compared the caller's requested target against its own readahead
  buffer-ahead progress (a thread-local decode-head position) instead of
  against what had actually been delivered to the caller. Since the
  readahead queue intentionally decodes ahead of the consumer by design,
  this made every normal readahead cycle look like the caller seeking
  backward, forcing an av_seek_frame + avcodec_flush_buffers + queue-clear
  on nearly every loop iteration - a livelock that could never make real
  forward progress in a clip with no interior keyframes near the target.
  Fixed by judging the backward-seek check against
  VideoHandle::deliveredSeconds (the position actually handed to the
  caller via VideoFrameAt), and made that field a std::atomic<double>
  since it's written by one thread and read by another.

Verified via three consecutive clean INFINITE_RECEXPORTTEST runs (0ms
drift/offset/lead on every one of the 5 audio/video markers) and a full
headless-tests.sh pass under Xvfb.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

prebuilt GPL FFmpeg+libx264 (H.264 recording) and LGPL FFmpeg (decode/playback
only, no bundled H.264 encoder) - same FetchContent pattern already used for
ONNX Runtime. Pins exact upstream FFmpeg 8.1 and x264 source tarballs+SHA256

the CMake link, per the licence decision in docs/plans/linux/phase-03-media.md.

and CameraLinux.cpp remain P3 stubs, landing in follow-up commits.

parsed_message.title: fix(arrange): stop canvas drop handler from stealing Finder drops meant for the timeline
parsed_message.description: stop canvas drop handler from stealing Finder drops meant for the timeline
parsed_message.body:
The node-editor canvas's own OS-file-drop handler ran unconditionally
whenever gDroppedFiles was non-empty, clearing the shared list every
frame. Since Arrange::Settings::dockSide defaults to bottom, the
Arrange panel's own drop handling (inside DrawArrangePanelContent)
runs after the canvas block in frame order, so it never saw a
Finder drop dragged onto the timeline - the canvas silently consumed
it first, misidentifying the file's node type via extension in the
worst case. Guard the canvas handler to skip drops that land inside
the Arrange panel's own screen rect (gArrangePanelRectMin/Max),
which it already tracks, so the two handlers never race for the
same drop regardless of dock side.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

parsed_message.title: fix(arrange): also force redraw of Render3DNode's scene cache offline
parsed_message.description: also force redraw of Render3DNode's scene cache offline
parsed_message.body:
Render3DNode::CookIfNeeded has its own live-preview change-gate
(BuildSceneSignature() equality) that skips the shadow/opaque/
transmissive passes and reuses mColorTex whenever nothing it tracks
changed since the last cook. This is the same bug shape as the
already-fixed NodeViewport cache, but on the path arrangement clips
take when the assigned node is Render3DNode itself (or anything
downstream of it) rather than a raw IGeometrySource - CompositeArrange
TimelineVideo's else-branch reads GetOutputTexture() directly and
trusts whatever this cache last produced.
The signature isn't wrong, just insufficient for offline export's
guarantee: some upstream revisions don't tick on every export frame
(e.g. ParticleSystemNode's fixed-step accumulator, or an animated
albedo-only texture that BuildSceneSignature's texturedMaterial check
doesn't scan), so two adjacent export frames can hash identical and
silently recapture the prior frame's pixels under a new timestamp.
Add !Transport::Instance().IsOfflineMode() to the skip condition so a
take always redraws, mirroring the NodeViewport::Render forceRedraw
fix instead of duplicating its own bypass mechanism.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

parsed_message.title: feat(arrange): drag-and-drop media import onto the timeline
parsed_message.description: drag-and-drop media import onto the timeline
parsed_message.body:
Drop audio, video, or image files from the browser panel or Finder
directly onto an Arrange lane: the matching source node is spawned,
a clip is placed immediately in a loading state, and the real decode
(dr_wav/dr_mp3/dr_flac/AVAudioFile/video/image) runs off the main
thread via a new Arrange::MediaImportManager, mirroring SampleScanner's
threading pattern.
Audio clips get new pitch (+/-24 semitones) and syncToTempo fields;
syncToTempo is "length only" - the clip's timeline length is computed
once from the file's natural duration at drop-time tempo, never
revisited on a later tempo change. Video/image clips get a basic
3-slider color grade (brightness/contrast/saturation), wired into the
arrangement compositor shader as a per-clip pass that no-ops at
defaults.
The clip context menu gains Rename/Active entries usable from any
clip type, plus Gain/Pan/Pitch/Sync to Tempo (audio) and Color Grade
(video/image) controls.

parsed_message.title: fix(arrange): force real redraw of geometry lanes during offline export
parsed_message.description: force real redraw of geometry lanes during offline export
parsed_message.body:
CompositeArrangeTimelineVideo composites geometry-source clips through
NodeViewport's cached mini-viewport render. NodeViewport::Render is a
live-preview change-gate meant for UI glances - it skips re-rendering
and returns the prior frame's texture whenever the node's own
mesh/model/material/camera/instancing/texture revisions haven't ticked.
The offline export pump never signaled otherwise, so it recaptured
identical pixels under a correct-but-stale timestamp whenever a
geometry clip's revision counters happened not to tick between two
consecutive export frames, showing up as stutter/duplicate frames.
Pass Transport::Instance().IsOfflineMode() as NodeViewport::Render's
existing (previously unused at this call site) forceRedraw argument so
every offline-exported frame gets a real redraw. Live preview callers
(gNodeViewports) are untouched.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

parsed_message.title: fix(mesh): make metaball edge lerp order-independent, fixing x86_64 weld
parsed_message.description: make metaball edge lerp order-independent, fixing x86_64 weld
parsed_message.body:
MeshOps::BuildWeldMap already quantised positions to an integer grid before
hashing - that part was sound. The actual x86_64-only defect was upstream in
EmitTetra's lerpPoint (src/core/Mesh.cpp): two tetrahedra sharing an edge each
classify their own corners into inside[]/outside[], so the same grid edge
could be lerped as (a, b) from one tetrahedron and (b, a) from its neighbour.
Those two expressions are mathematically equal but not bit-identical, and
x86_64 and arm64 contract the FMA differently - so the "same" vertex landed a
ULP apart, on opposite sides of one of BuildWeldMap's quantisation
boundaries, on x86_64 only. Reproduced exactly via docker --platform
linux/amd64 (apart: 8 open edges BROKEN) versus the arm64 container (0 open
edges, watertight), then confirmed the specific vertex pair with a temporary
debug dump before reverting it.
Fix: canonicalise lerpPoint on corner identity (lexicographic on position)
rather than the caller's inside/outside labelling, so both call sites always
evaluate the exact same expression for a given edge.
Verified INFINITE_PHASECTEST=1 now reports 0 open edges/watertight on both
x86_64 and arm64, and the full 3d + compositing hygiene groups (31 checks)
pass on x86_64. Removed the now-stale PHASECTEST entry from
known-test-failures-linux.txt and corrected the linux-parity skill's
diagnosis, which had guessed BuildWeldMap itself was comparing floats
directly.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Merge: fix the arrangement wave-fill test failure

ARRANGEWAVETEST's "arrange wave filled by playback" sub-check reported
0/32 buckets and 0 non-silent on macOS. Two bugs in the section-G fixture:

- Use-after-realloc: the ARRANGERENDERTEST and ARRANGEWAVETEST blocks each
  held a GraphNode* across a later SpawnNode(), which can reallocate gNodes.
  The clip's srcUid then read as 0 and RebuildAudioTopology skipped it. Each
  uid is now captured immediately after its own spawn.

  device or an offline-render job, so a hand-rolled ProcessOffline fixture
  produced silence.

48510 frames @ 44100 Hz, and driver.sh --fast is 30/30 with no known xfails
(it was 29/30 with this as the one red).

parsed_message.title: fix: keep windows.h out of main.cpp; baseline the x86_64 metaball weld failure
parsed_message.description: keep windows.h out of main.cpp; baseline the x86_64 metaball weld failure
parsed_message.body:
Adding platform/common/PathOpen.h to main.cpp broke the Windows build in
a place nowhere near the include. On _WIN32 that header pulls WinCommon.h
and so <windows.h>, and wingdi.h declares a FUNCTION named Polyline,
which hides core/Mesh.h's global `struct Polyline` - so every MeshOps
declaration taking a `const Polyline&` stopped naming a type and MSVC
emitted a wall of errors pointing at Mesh.h. main.cpp had included no
Windows header at all before this, which is why that struct has been safe
for years.
The helper was not needed: the window-icon branch is Linux-only (Windows
takes SetWindowIconFromResource, macOS takes neither), and on Linux a
path is already UTF-8, so a plain std::ifstream is correct. Comment at
the call site explains why not to reach for the portable helper here.
This was hidden behind the scanner link error - Infinite depends on the
scanner target, so while that failed to link, main.cpp was never compiled.
Fixing one revealed the other.
PHASECTEST is a different animal and is baselined, not fixed: its metaball
watertightness check reports 8 open edges on x86_64 and 0 on arm64 from an
identical 6096-triangle mesh, because BuildWeldMap compares float positions
against an epsilon that x86_64 codegen moves them across. Nothing in the
port touches Mesh.h. It is real and user-visible - a non-watertight blob
renders shattered under backface culling, and every x86_64 user is on the
failing side - so the baseline entry carries the whole story and says to
remove it with a fix in BuildWeldMap, not before P5.
Both traps are now in linux-parity §3.6 and §3.7, along with the rule the
second one really teaches: local green on arm64 is not green.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

parsed_message.title: fix(win): link the VST3 scanner against SubjectMaskOnnx; upload per-test logs
parsed_message.description: link the VST3 scanner against SubjectMaskOnnx; upload per-test logs
parsed_message.body:
PlatformWin.cpp is compiled into two executables. Moving OrtMatting out
of it into common/ so Linux could share it left the second one -
infinite-vst3-scanner, the out-of-process plugin prober - without the
partner file, and it failed to link on both Windows arches with four
unresolved OrtMatting symbols. WIN32_SOURCES does not reach that target;
it has its own source list. Anything extracted out of PlatformWin.cpp or
PluginVST3Win.cpp has to be added in both places.
This landed in 9477e6b and has been broken on the branch since. It went
unnoticed because no CI run on this branch had ever completed - the two
before it were cancelled by the next push - so the first real Windows
signal arrived after the merge, not before it.
Separately: driver.sh writes /tmp/infinite_test_<NAME>.log per check and
on failure prints only "see <path>", which is worthless from a CI log
because the path is on a runner that is already gone. PHASECTEST passes
on the arm64 container and fails on x86_64 CI, and there is currently no
way to see which of its sub-checks failed. Upload them.

parsed_message.title: Merge: linux-parity skill and the fixes the pre-merge gate found
parsed_message.description: Merge: linux-parity skill and the fixes the pre-merge gate found
parsed_message.body:
Follow-up to the P0+P1 merge. Two things the advisory gate caught before
that merge and one the owner asked for after it.
The gate found that adding the Linux "Dialog helper:" diagnostic to
SysInfo had silently deleted the GLSL Version printf beside it - a
macOS and Windows regression hiding inside a Linux change - and flagged
TextLinux's alpha blend as the straight-vs-premultiplied mistake this
codebase has made before. The blend is correct; the buffer is
premultiplied by contract with Platform.mm's CGBitmapContext. It now
says so, since the next reader won't have Platform.mm open beside it.
linux-parity is the third-platform companion to windows-parity. It
deliberately restates none of it - the abstraction rules are shared and
cross-referenced - and covers only what Linux does differently, plus the
inverted posture that matters most: Linux can be executed locally, so
Linux claims should be run rather than reasoned about.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

parsed_message.title: skill: add linux-parity, the third-platform companion to windows-parity
parsed_message.description: skill: add linux-parity, the third-platform companion to windows-parity
parsed_message.body:
windows-parity exists because nobody here can run Windows, so the skill
front-loads reading. Linux is a different problem: it can be executed
locally in the container rig, so the posture is inverted - run it rather
than reason about it - and the skill says so up front.
It deliberately does not restate windows-parity. The one-abstraction
rule, byte-identical signatures, GLSL 330 strictness and the denormal
convention are shared and cross-referenced instead. What is new is what
Linux does differently: the obligation is now three-sided and
src/platform/common/ is the preferred landing site for anything Windows
and Linux genuinely share; fontconfig and FreeType must be cached or
they cost per-frame; there is no HarfBuzz, so complex scripts render
unjoined (a gap shared with Windows, not a Linux regression); optional
libraries are dlopen'd rather than linked so a distro packaging
difference cannot stop the binary starting; nothing chdirs the way Cocoa
does; STBI_NO_STDIO means stbi_load compiles and then fails to link; and
an AppImage inherits its glibc floor from the build host.
The verification section is written around what the rig cannot prove -
every render goes through llvmpipe, no real GPU driver has run this
code, no real desktop has - because the two worst bugs of this port were
both verification steps that could only report success.
Also tags AudioSpikeStart's Linux stub as the deliberate never-phased
exception it is, matching PlatformWin.cpp:662, so the skill's
stub-without-a-phase-tag audit reads clean.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

parsed_message.title: Merge: Linux port P0 (skeleton + rig) and P1 (desktop)
parsed_message.description: Merge: Linux port P0 (skeleton + rig) and P1 (desktop)
bullets: fast tier is 30/30 and the ui,3d,compositing render groups are 45 pass
parsed_message.body:
Infinite now builds and runs on Linux as an x86_64 desktop app. This
merge closes the first two phases of docs/plans/linux: the platform
skeleton with a verification rig, and the desktop layer.
What is real: the build is green under both Clang and GCC; ldd shows no
direct libGL/libGLX/libEGL and no direct libX11, so GLFW picks X11 or
Wayland at runtime rather than the link being nailed to one; the hygiene
with 1 known xfail; the headless CI suite exercises a real SIGSEGV
through the new backtrace handler and a real TLS request. Six
per-category screenshots render through Mesa's llvmpipe and are gated on
actually containing an image.
What is not covered: every render here goes through llvmpipe, so no real

parsed_message.description: restore the dropped GLSL Version line, document the premultiplied text buffer
parsed_message.body:
Adding the Linux "Dialog helper:" diagnostic to SysInfo accidentally
deleted the GLSL Version printf next to it. glslVersion was still being
fetched and then never printed, on every platform - so this was a
macOS and Windows regression hiding inside a Linux change.
TextLinux's blendPixel does dst*(1-a) + src*a with no divide by alpha,
which looks exactly like the straight-vs-premultiplied blending mistake
this codebase has made before. It's correct: Platform.mm fills the same
buffer through a CGBitmapContext with kCGImageAlphaPremultipliedLast, so
premultiplied is the contract. Said so in a comment, because the next
reader won't have Platform.mm open beside it.

parsed_message.title: tools(linux): gate shots on colour count, not byte size, and pin macOS references
parsed_message.description: tools(linux): gate shots on colour count, not byte size, and pin macOS references
parsed_message.body:
The old gate failed a shot under 20 kB. It was worthless: a blank editor
grab measured 230 kB against a real render's 172 kB, because an empty
grid of hairlines compresses worse than actual imagery. Every blank
frame sailed through it.
Count distinct colours instead - ImageMagick where it exists (already a
declared apt dep), else a dependency-free PNG decoder for stock macOS
python3, else SKIP rather than a silent pass. A true empty editor
measures 183 colours at native resolution and real renders land between
3391 and 18602, so the threshold sits at 600. Measure at native
resolution if you ever retune it: downscaling roughly doubles the count
and calibrating on shrunk images produced two false positives.
Two other things had to change for the references to be real. shots.sh
picked the Linux ELF when run on macOS, since both binaries live in one
worktree - select by uname. And every macOS reference initially rendered
blank because imgui-node-editor restores canvas pan and zoom from $HOME,
so the shots inherited whatever the operator had last scrolled to; the
fixtures now run under a throwaway HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME.

parsed_message.title: test: cover the Syphon-hidden-on-Linux path, and stop lying about screenshots
parsed_message.description: cover the Syphon-hidden-on-Linux path, and stop lying about screenshots
parsed_message.body:
Hiding the Syphon/Spout nodes from the Add menu on Linux leaves them
registered so old patches still load, but nothing exercised that: the
spawn path and the load path are different code, and suppressing one is
exactly what breaks the other. SYPHONPATCHTEST writes a two-node Syphon
patch, reads it back and asserts both nodes survive ApplyPatchData. It
returns before glfwInit(), so it runs in the headless CI suite as well
as in the hygiene tiers.
The screenshot writer printed "wrote <path>" whether or not the write
succeeded. That is not a cosmetic bug - it is the only signal the shot
harness has, and on macOS the write fails easily, because Cocoa chdir's
a bundled app to Contents/Resources so a relative path names a directory
that isn't there. The harness was reading a success line for files that
had never been written.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

spawn path and the load path are different code, and suppressing one is
exactly what breaks the other. SYPHONPATCHTEST writes a two-node Syphon
patch, reads it back and asserts both nodes survive ApplyPatchData. It

arrange: fix ARRANGEWAVETEST wave-fill-by-playback failure

Two bugs in the section G fixture kept the timeline audio topology
empty and, once fixed, silent:

- Both the ARRANGERENDERTEST and ARRANGEWAVETEST spawn blocks held a
  GraphNode* from an earlier SpawnNode() call across a later
  SpawnNode() call, which can reallocate gNodes and invalidate every
  pointer into it. The dereferenced uid read stale/zeroed memory, so
  the placed clip's srcUid was 0 and RebuildAudioTopology skipped it
  as an offline/deleted clip, producing an empty topology.

  silence: a hand-rolled ProcessOffline fixture never triggers
  RebuildAudioTopology's CookIfNeeded/PrepareToPlay priming, which
  only fires for a live device or an offline-render job. Added the
  same priming used by the neighboring arrange render test fixture.

run-infinite-hygiene --fast --skip-build.

parsed_message.title: arrange: live clip waveforms and video thumbnails (WP8)
parsed_message.description: arrange: live clip waveforms and video thumbnails (WP8)
parsed_message.body:
Audio clips draw the waveform of what actually came out of their source
node, video clips draw a thumbnail of what they show.
The waveform is position-indexed, not streamed: the audio thread folds a
min/max accumulator into the per-sample envelope loop that already walks
the clip windows, and publishes one bucket per 1/16 beat through a new
lock-free SPSC ring (ClipPeakRing) once the playhead crosses out of it.
Bucket k always means the same slice of the clip, so playing a bar twice
overwrites rather than appends and scrubbing backwards fills in what was
skipped. Peaks are measured pre-envelope and pre-gain, so editing a fade
or a gain does not invalidate what is already drawn.

parsed_message.body:
The gate conflated two independent questions. Copyright is a non-issue:
the default binary is already GPLv3 via the Steinberg VST3 SDK, and
FFmpeg --enable-gpl and x264 are GPLv2-or-later, so they flow upward into
v3 cleanly. Every other bundled component is GPL-compatible, and the
Apache-2.0 model weights are v3-compatible but not v2-compatible, which
independently pins the combined work to v3.
The real exposure is patents, and it is specific to Linux. macOS encodes
H.264 through AVAssetWriter and Windows through IMFSinkWriter, so in both
cases the OS vendor supplies the encoder and has paid the AVC pool. Linux
has no OS encoder, so bundling x264 makes this project the distributor of
an H.264 encoder for the first time. Accepted: the app is free and open
source, far below any threshold ever enforced, and this is what OBS,
Kdenlive, Shotcut, HandBrake and every distro's FFmpeg already do. The
alternative would make Linux record a different, worse file than the
other two platforms.
Three conditions are part of the decision:
promises that INFINITE_ENABLE_VST3=OFF yields an MIT binary; linking GPL
FFmpeg unconditionally would break that promise silently. Fedora and
Flathub's main repo also cannot ship H.264 at all.
prebuilt GPL binaries without being able to produce matching source is
the usual way projects fall out of compliance, so pin upstream source
tarballs with SHA256 and archive or rebuild them.
as a follow-up.
VA-API hardware encode, which would put Linux back in the same structural
position as macOS and Windows, is noted for P5 rather than P3 - it cannot
be verified under llvmpipe.

The gate conflated two independent questions. Copyright is a non-issue:
the default binary is already GPLv3 via the Steinberg VST3 SDK, and
FFmpeg --enable-gpl and x264 are GPLv2-or-later, so they flow upward into
v3 cleanly. Every other bundled component is GPL-compatible, and the
Apache-2.0 model weights are v3-compatible but not v2-compatible, which
independently pins the combined work to v3.

The real exposure is patents, and it is specific to Linux. macOS encodes
H.264 through AVAssetWriter and Windows through IMFSinkWriter, so in both
cases the OS vendor supplies the encoder and has paid the AVC pool. Linux

source, far below any threshold ever enforced, and this is what OBS,
Kdenlive, Shotcut, HandBrake and every distro's FFmpeg already do. The

other two platforms.

position as macOS and Windows, is noted for P5 rather than P3 - it cannot
be verified under llvmpipe.

parsed_message.description: decode the window icon from memory, not stbi_load
parsed_message.body:
The window-icon path did not link on Linux: undefined reference to
stbi_load. The single STB_IMAGE_IMPLEMENTATION in this target
(EnvironmentNode.cpp) is compiled with STBI_NO_STDIO, so the path-based
loaders are never emitted - only the *_from_memory entry points exist.
This never showed on macOS or Windows because neither takes that branch.
Reads the file through OpenIfstreamUtf8 and decodes with
stbi_load_from_memory, matching how MediaDecodePortable already handles
the same constraint.

parsed_message.title: fix(linux): collect real Linux shots instead of committed macOS PNGs
parsed_message.description: collect real Linux shots instead of committed macOS PNGs
parsed_message.body:
The harness artifact step was:
find . -maxdepth 2 -name "*.png" -exec cp {} "$ARTIFACTS_DIR/" \;
which swept up PNGs COMMITTED to the repo - docs/screenshot.png,
website/full_page_capture.png, assets/Infinite*.png - every one of them
captured on macOS. The downloaded artifact therefore looked like proof
that Linux rendered correctly while containing no Linux pixels at all.
Meanwhile the one genuine render the driver does produce,
/tmp/infinite_hygiene_shot.png, was never collected, and neither --fast
nor --group sets RUN_SHOT in the first place.
Collection is now restricted to files this run produced. New
tools/linux/shots.sh drives six existing dev fixtures with
IMAGERESYNTH_SCREENSHOT so the binary writes each PNG itself from
glReadPixels, and fails an entry that produces no file or one under 20 kB
(a window that came up but drew nothing still yields a valid, tiny PNG).
Frames are per fixture: 3DTEST and TEXT3DTEST print their verdict and
close early, so the shot has to land before that.
The same script regenerates tools/linux/reference-shots/ on macOS, so
both sets come from identical fixtures at identical frames and can be
compared side by side in the one downloaded artifact.
Shots soft-fail: a missing shot is visible in the artifact but must not
mask the driver's own verdict, which is what EXIT_CODE carries.

parsed_message.title: perf(linux): cache fontconfig config, resolved paths and FT_Face
parsed_message.description: cache fontconfig config, resolved paths and FT_Face
parsed_message.body:
Text rasterization rebuilt the entire font world on every call.
FcInitLoadConfigAndFonts() parses /etc/fonts/**, every user config and
validates the font cache; it ran once per ResolveFontPath, and
ResolveFontPath runs up to three times per RasterizeText (requested
family, DejaVu Sans fallback, fontconfig default). FT_New_Face then
mmapped and parsed the font file, paired with FT_Done_Face on the way
out. All of that repeated whenever any Text node parameter moved.
Now: one process-wide FcConfig, a family+style -> path memo, and a
path -> FT_Face map whose faces live for the process. Reuse is safe
because both entry points hold gFtMutex (an FT_Face is not thread-safe)
and both call FT_Set_Pixel_Sizes before measuring or drawing, so no size
state carries between calls. A font file that fails to load is cached as
nullptr rather than re-parsed every frame.
AvailableFontFamilies now takes gFtMutex too - it previously touched
fontconfig with no lock at all, and it shares the config now.
Also documents the complex-script shaping gap (no HarfBuzz: Arabic,
Devanagari and Thai render unjoined). That is a shared Linux+Windows
limitation, not a Linux regression, so it is recorded rather than fixed
here.

arrange: exact render range, render sources, persisted settings, job model (WP7a)

The Arrangement Timeline's render stops being a single hard-wired take and
becomes a job: a tick range, an audio source, a video source and an output
file, started through one function that no path can skip.

- #1/#6b Audio source (Timeline clips / Canvas output / None) and Video
  source (Timeline clips / a canvas Output node / None) replace the two
  "include" checkboxes that never reached the take. gOfflineRender's single
  arrangeDriven flag splits into timelineVideo (composite the lanes) and
  timelineAudio (Timeline Strict terminals), so picture and sound can come
  from different places. Video None writes a WAV through AudioFileWriter on
  its own pump - no encoder, no frames, no OutputNode.
- #2 The take's frame budget is ceil(durationSec * fps) via OutputNode's new
  offlineTotalFramesOverride, not whole seconds x fps.
- #4 The hardware-source refusal now covers arrangement takes, scoped to the
  nodes that enabled clips inside the range actually reference; a canvas-
  sourced side still gets the whole-patch sweep.
- #5 "Match Clips" and the Whole-arrangement range skip disabled and
  unassigned clips, and fall back to the patch's Output node before 1080p.
- #7 Size, fps, format, range kind, sources and folder live in
  Arrange::Settings and travel with the patch instead of being statics.
- #8 An existing file, or a path another queued job already owns, opens an
  Overwrite / Auto-rename / Cancel prompt at submit time.

The queue itself (window, reorder, retry, lock overlay) is WP7b; Render Now
already runs through it as a one-job queue.

arrange: id selection, multi-drag, groups, enable, offline clips, lane pick, undo coverage (WP5a)

Timeline UI now edits Arrange::Model gArrange directly through the model ops;
the legacy gArrangeStreams mirror is re-derived only when revision or tempo
changes (audio/video still read it until WP5b).

- Selection is a set of clip ids plus an anchor, pruned on patch generation
  change; undo resolves to the same clips or clears.
- Multi-clip drag (snapshot + reapply, one undo entry per gesture, no entry
  for a no-move click), group move / edge trim / Shift-scale, Alt-click a
  single member, Cmd+G / Cmd+Shift+G.
- `0` / Keypad 0 toggles enabled; Cmd+C/V clipboard (cleared on New/Open),
  Cmd+D / Shift+D duplicate as a block, Cmd+E split, Delete.
- Deleting a node leaves its clips offline (ClearSource), restored by undo.
- Add to Timeline picks the lane from the node's outputs (Video/Audio submenu
  for VideoSourceNode); the canvas Assign picker is id-based.
- Dock side (bottom/top) in View > Arrangement Timeline and the monitor's
  context menu; top-bar audio button only powers the engine, a Timeline badge
  shows when timeline audio routing is on.
- Panel shortcuts are gated off during a drag/gesture; node deletion during a
  gesture also clears the gesture's before-snapshot.
- New fixture INFINITE_ARRANGEEDITTEST (tier1 + tier2 + full); shortcuts
  table gains an Arrangement Timeline category; shortcuts-sweep check.py maps
  digit and Keypad digit keys.

parsed_message.title: fix(ui): correct Windows DPI scaling and add manual UI Scale override
parsed_message.description: correct Windows DPI scaling and add manual UI Scale override
parsed_message.body:
On Windows, GLFW window coordinates are physical pixels and
glfwGetWindowContentScale() reports the actual OS/monitor DPI factor, unlike
macOS where it's Retina-only sharpness info. The font block baked glyphs at
baseSize*xscale and then divided the same xscale back out via
FontGlobalScale, cancelling exactly and pinning text to a fixed 15 physical
px regardless of Windows display scaling (150%/200% had no effect on 4K).
ImGuiStyle::ScaleAllSizes() was also never called, so widget metrics never
scaled either.
Windows now bakes the font directly at baseSize*xscale with
FontGlobalScale=1 and calls ScaleAllSizes(xscale), so both text and widget
metrics track the monitor's DPI setting. macOS keeps its existing
Retina-aware math unchanged. Also adds a persisted gUiScale manual multiplier
(Appearance tab, "UI Scale" slider, requires restart) on top of the OS scale,
stored in Infinite.appearance as ui.scale=. Moved CategoryColors::LoadPreference()
earlier in startup, before the font/DPI block, since the override must be
known before the font atlas is baked.
Fixes #21

parsed_message.title: Fix MOLDERTEST determinism false-positive; document reconstruction gap
parsed_message.description: Fix MOLDERTEST determinism false-positive; document reconstruction gap
parsed_message.body:
The "same seed/generation diverged" failure was a fixture bug, not a
MolderDsp::Mutate/Rng bug: it memcmp'd the whole MolderDsp::Genome struct,
which ends in a trailing bool and therefore has compiler-inserted padding
that no constructor ever initializes. Two logically-identical Genomes could
differ in that uninitialized padding. Replaced the memcmp with an explicit
field-by-field comparison.
The "-6.7dB reconstruction error" failure is a real, already-investigated
gap in the additive resynthesis (dense-harmonic mainlobe overlap), not a
stale threshold — left open and documented rather than fixed or papered
over, since closing it needs real per-harmonic overlap compensation. Added
a "Known pre-existing failures" section to audio-pipeline-sweep/SKILL.md
(its driver has no known-failure baseline mechanism, unlike
run-infinite-hygiene) plus a forward-looking cross-reference in
known-test-failures.txt.
