arrange: schedule the whole timeline once, in beats (WP3)

Timeline audio was scheduled from whichever clips happened to be under the
playhead when the topology was built, and rebuilt whenever that set of
clips changed. That is what made the second of two adjacent clips of one
node play silent (the set never changed, so the stale single-clip window
stayed), made seeking between two clips of the same node silent for the
same reason, landed onsets up to a UI frame late, and reset delay
compensation at every clip boundary.

The topology now covers the whole arrangement. Seeds are every enabled,
assigned clip on every audio lane; one terminal per (laneId, srcUid,
srcOutput) carries all of that combination's windows, main-thread
allocated into AudioTopology::clipWindows and freed with the ProcessList
through the existing retire path. Clip boundaries never rebuild.

The envelope moves from seconds to beats, so a tempo change no longer
drags every clip's onset with it, with a per-terminal window cursor
(O(1) amortized) and a 2 ms declick at every window edge that is not
abutted by its neighbour - an abutting edge is one continuous run of the
same node and must not dip.

Routing depends on the mode and nothing else: bool gArrangeAudioMode
becomes enum class AudioMode { Canvas, Timeline }, defaulting to Canvas
and never persisted, reset on launch, New and Open. Hiding the panel or
hitting pause no longer changes what is in the topology; paused in
Timeline mode is silence, gated in RunTopology. The arrangement render no
longer forces the mode on without restoring it.

Rebuilds are triggered by a fingerprint over everything the schedule is
built from rather than a revision counter, because the panel edits the
legacy mirror from ~190 sites and one of them forgetting to bump a
counter would silently reintroduce exactly this bug.

Also fixed, found while auditing the above:
- A disabled audio clip was never excluded; `enabled` was not read at all.
- Terminal PDC lived in the disposable terminal vector and clicked on
  every rebuild. It now lives in a main-thread map, retired only once
  CompletedGeneration() confirms the audio thread is past it.
- The block crossing a loop end had its whole envelope placed on the new
  lap's axis, dropping the last few ms before every loop point.
  Transport::BlockStartBeats() captures the real start before the wrap.
- WriteNodeBool("bypassed") returned without a rebuild, though
  ResolvedAudioSource follows `bypassed`.

New INFINITE_ARRANGEAUDIOTEST (8 sections, deterministic, offline) and a
new TRANSPORTTEST section guarding the loop-crossing block axis.

parsed_message.title: transport: tempo-safe beats, beat seek, and a block-accurate loop (WP2)
parsed_message.description: transport: tempo-safe beats, beat seek, and a block-accurate loop (WP2)
parsed_message.body:
Three bugs in the clock that the arrangement stands on.
Tempo. Beats() is beatsOffset + (Seconds - secOffset) * bpm, so applying
a new bpm in place re-measured the whole elapsed span at the new tempo -
the playhead teleported mid-play and dragged every beat-placed clip with
it. SetTempo now *stages* the value; the clock owner (AdvanceAudioClock,
BeginOfflineAudioBlock, Tick) applies it at a block boundary after
rebasing the offsets to the current position, so Beats() is continuous
across the change. Tempo() reports the staged value, so UI and
seconds<->ticks conversions never see a stale bpm. A seek re-seats both
offsets anyway, so it just consumes the staged tempo with no rebase.
Seek. Added SeekBeats(double). The arrangement playhead is Beats(), so
timeline gestures address the clock in beats; Seek(seconds) stays for the
seconds-native callers (video scrub, offline frame stepping).
Loop. The wrap ran in the arrangement panel's draw, once per UI frame, so
playback sailed past the loop end by a whole frame - tens of milliseconds
of audio that should not have been heard, and unbounded during a stall.
It also only ran while the panel was visible. Transport::SetLoop(enabled,
beatStart, beatEnd) now holds it in atomics and wraps wherever the clock
advances, so the overshoot is at most one audio block. The wrap uses fmod
rather than snapping to the loop start, so the crossing block's overshoot
carries into the next lap instead of being dropped, and it bumps
mResetEpoch exactly as the old Seek-based wrap did. SetOfflineMode(true)
suspends the loop and restores it after, so a render walks its range once
instead of looping forever.
The panel keeps editing the loop in seconds (WP5 moves the UI to ticks)
and publishes it at the boundary; the model owns it in ticks for
save/load, and SyncLegacyFromArrange re-seats both sides so a saved loop
comes back armed rather than as a band playback ignores.
New INFINITE_TRANSPORTTEST drives the audio clock by hand with the real
engine stopped, so it is deterministic and needs no audio device:
tempo continuity   jump 0.0427 beats against a 0.0427 budget, and the
post-change rate is exactly double
seek beats         position and seconds agree, negatives clamp
loop wrap          10 laps, zero observable overshoot
offline            reaches 12.8 beats past a 4-beat loop, loop still
armed afterwards
no-engine fallback same guarantee on the Tick() path
Registered in the hygiene driver's tier 1 and tier 2 lists.

parsed_message.title: fix(plugins-panel): stop iterator invalidation when removing a VST3 search folder
parsed_message.description: stop iterator invalidation when removing a VST3 search folder
parsed_message.body:
The "VST3 search folders" list in the Plugins panel iterated
gPluginScanner.Folders() directly (a live reference to the scanner's
internal vector) and called RemoveFolder() - which erases from that same
vector - from inside the loop. Erasing mid-iteration invalidates the
loop's iterator, which is undefined behavior and can corrupt the heap in
ways that surface far away (observed as an unrelated ImGui internal
stack-size assertion crashing the app soon after use).
Snapshot the folder list before iterating, matching the defer-until-after
or copy-first idiom already used for the same pattern in the Samples and
Media library panels.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

parsed_message.title: fix(vst3-scan): stop macOS batch scanner from over-blocklisting plugins
parsed_message.description: stop macOS batch scanner from over-blocklisting plugins
parsed_message.body:
The macOS batch-scan retry loop in ProbeVST3BundlesBatch never removed
already-described bundles from the retry list, had no iteration cap, and
relied solely on a dispatch_once-gated sentinel check to attribute a crash
to an offending bundle. A single crashing/slow plugin could therefore spin
the same batch indefinitely or silently fail to get attributed within one
scan, causing legitimate plugins to accumulate onto the persisted blocklist
across app relaunches ("most of my VSTs are blocklisted").
Port the three safeguards the Windows implementation already has: drop
successfully-described bundles from the retry list each pass (forward
progress), cap total iterations, and directly blocklist the front bundle
when a crash pass describes nothing at all.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
parsed_message.raw:
fix(vst3-scan): stop macOS batch scanner from over-blocklisting plugins

The macOS batch-scan retry loop in ProbeVST3BundlesBatch never removed
already-described bundles from the retry list, had no iteration cap, and
relied solely on a dispatch_once-gated sentinel check to attribute a crash
to an offending bundle. A single crashing/slow plugin could therefore spin
the same batch indefinitely or silently fail to get attributed within one
scan, causing legitimate plugins to accumulate onto the persisted blocklist
across app relaunches ("most of my VSTs are blocklisted").

Port the three safeguards the Windows implementation already has: drop
successfully-described bundles from the retry list each pass (forward
progress), cap total iterations, and directly blocklist the front bundle
when a crash pass describes nothing at all.

parsed_message.title: fix(gesture-recorder): freeze looping recordings on spacebar pause
parsed_message.description: freeze looping recordings on spacebar pause
parsed_message.body:
Gesture-recorded playback timestamped and replayed itself against
ImGui::GetTime() (wall clock), so a looping recording kept animating
even after pausing the global transport with spacebar. Every other
time-based modulator freezes on pause because it reads Transport's own
clock instead.
Added an internal clock to GestureRecorder that only advances while
Transport::IsPlaying() is true, and switched every timestamp/playback
call site (NotifyMovement, MaybeFinishArmedRecording, GetPlaybackValue,
BeginFrame, undo/redo's GestureClockNow) to read it instead of
ImGui::GetTime().

parsed_message.title: fix(mod): stop ModSliderInt from stomping expression/recording writes
parsed_message.description: stop ModSliderInt from stomping expression/recording writes
bullets: value changed for some other reason. That guard is source-agnostic -
parsed_message.body:
ModSliderInt reseeded its backing proxy float from the node's *value
every frame unless Modulation::IsModulated() was true, but IsModulated
only detects a wired modulation cable - it doesn't see an active
expression or gesture/mod-recorder playback driving the same param.
Since the UI draw pass runs before ApplyModulationAndPalette applies
those each frame, any expression/recording write got stomped by the
next frame's reseed before the audio thread ever saw it, so params
driven this way (e.g. NoteSwitcherNode's manual slot) appeared frozen
while a wired LFO on the same control worked fine.
ModKnobInt already had the correct fix for this, for an unrelated
reason (it needs to preserve its drag accumulator across frames): it
tracks the last value it wrote back itself and only reseeds when
cable, expression, or recording all look the same to it - so porting
it into ModSliderInt fixes the shared helper for every caller at once,
including SwitcherNode's and Switcher3DNode's manual-slot sliders,
which had the identical latent bug.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
parsed_message.raw:
fix(mod): stop ModSliderInt from stomping expression/recording writes

ModSliderInt reseeded its backing proxy float from the node's *value
every frame unless Modulation::IsModulated() was true, but IsModulated
only detects a wired modulation cable - it doesn't see an active
expression or gesture/mod-recorder playback driving the same param.
Since the UI draw pass runs before ApplyModulationAndPalette applies
those each frame, any expression/recording write got stomped by the
next frame's reseed before the audio thread ever saw it, so params
driven this way (e.g. NoteSwitcherNode's manual slot) appeared frozen
while a wired LFO on the same control worked fine.

ModKnobInt already had the correct fix for this, for an unrelated
reason (it needs to preserve its drag accumulator across frames): it
tracks the last value it wrote back itself and only reseeds when
*value changed for some other reason. That guard is source-agnostic -
cable, expression, or recording all look the same to it - so porting
it into ModSliderInt fixes the shared helper for every caller at once,
including SwitcherNode's and Switcher3DNode's manual-slot sliders,
which had the identical latent bug.

dropdown next to "shading" in the Material node's params panel.

Phase 5: geometry-domains audit - sweeps and chain fuzzer

Extends geometry-transform-sweep's rig per the Phase 5 plan:

- MATERIALSWEEPTEST/TEXTURESWEEPTEST: new material/texture probes
  covering side channels A and E across 17 node types each, mirroring
  MAPPINGSWEEPTEST's established pattern (channel F).
- COLOURSWEEPTEST (built from scratch - it did not exist anywhere in
  the codebase despite the plan's "widen from 8 to 22" framing):
  covers side channels B/C across ~25 of 29 node types, with explicit
  documented exclusions for what's out of scope (channel D, nodes
  needing real file/curve data, already-audited D6 sites).
- MAPPINGSWEEPTEST: extended to InstanceOnPointsNode, which surfaced a
  real gap - it had no GetMappingTransform() override at all, silently
  falling back to the identity default. Fixed by forwarding from
  instanceShape, the same shape as its GetMaterial()/GetMaterialTexture()
  overrides.
- CHAINFUZZTEST: a fixed-seed (0xC0FFEE) randomised fuzzer building 200
  three-to-five-node chains from 11 single-input operator types,
  asserting determinism, colour-in/colour-out, and no manufactured
  colour on each rebuild.
- INSTANCESWEEPTEST wired into driver.sh's GROUP_3D - it existed in
  main.cpp but was never part of the hygiene gate.

Fresh grep this session puts the node count at 29, not the 28 the
geometry-domains.md doc currently claims - worth reconciling separately.

parsed_message.title: Component passthrough for pass-through geometry wrappers (Blender's rule)
parsed_message.description: Component passthrough for pass-through geometry wrappers (Blender's rule)
parsed_message.body:
Null3D, Material, Mapping and Cloth only ever look at GetMesh() from their
input, so a point cloud or curve riding alongside it on the same cable
vanished silently - a Null3D between a cloud producer and a cloud consumer
laundered the cloud away, and Cloth swallowed one outright (the concrete
example the geometry-domains audit calls out). Forwards GetPointCloud()/
PointCloudRevision()/GetCurve()/CurveStamp() from input on all four, matching
how they already forward PassthroughSource() and the other side channels.
Scoped to nodes that are pure pass-throughs or read only GetMesh() with no
opinion on the other components; multi-input merges (Join) and nodes with
their own dedicated cloud pin (InstanceOnPoints) are unaffected.

parsed_message.title: D3/D4: Join always preserves colour, rename Set Color to Set Vertex Color
parsed_message.description: D3/D4: Join always preserves colour, rename Set Color to Set Vertex Color
parsed_message.body:
D4: Join Geometry's "keep input colours" checkbox meant merging could
silently destroy per-input colour by default - the existence of an opt-in
"don't destroy my data" checkbox was itself the tell. A merge should
always preserve input colour, so the parameter (and its UI checkbox) is
removed; the always-preserve code path becomes unconditional.
D3: "Set Color" collided with Material, which also claims to set colour
(albedo) - the two combine multiplicatively, so "Set Color red + Material
red = dark red" with nothing in either name warning about it. Renamed to
"Set Vertex Color" to state which of the two colour concepts it actually
writes (per-vertex colour, not the material's albedo).

Add MaterialRevision/MappingRevision to IGeometrySource, fix stale material caches

IGeometrySource exposed GetMaterial()/GetMappingTransform() with no
revision counterpart, so two RebuildIfNeeded() caches could go stale
on a material-only upstream edit:

- JoinGeometryNode bakes an input's material colour into vertex colours
  (keepInputColours path) but never checked material revision, so a
  material-only change upstream never invalidated the merged mesh cache.
- MeshToPointsNode has the same staleness bug for its inheritMaterial-
  driven point tint.

Adds MaterialRevision()/MappingRevision() virtuals (base default 0) plus
a shared ComputeContentRevision<T> FNV-1a hash helper, and implements
them across the IGeometrySource hierarchy wherever GetMaterial()/
GetMappingTransform() is overridden (FieldPrimitiveNode and
ParticleSystemNode skipped: both return a constant Material/
MappingTransform, so the base default of 0 is already correct).

JoinGeometryNode and MeshToPointsNode now track a built material
revision per slot/input and invalidate their cache when it changes.
Also closes a related gap in Render3DNode::BuildSceneSignature(),
which value-compared Material per slot but never captured
GetMappingTransform() at all; SceneSignature now carries and compares
mapping[] alongside material[].

parsed_message.title: Fix Join Geometry merge discarding a downstream Material's colour
parsed_message.description: Fix Join Geometry merge discarding a downstream Material's colour
parsed_message.body:
Two independent defects, both in JoinGeometryNode's merge path.
1. Manufactured vertex colour. The merge filled Mesh::vertexColor from
each input's material albedo unconditionally, even when every input was
colourless. vertexColor and Material::color are two independent inputs
to the same shader product (base = uBaseColor * vInstanceColor *
vVertexColor), but only vertexColor travels inside the mesh, and
nothing downstream can tell manufactured filler apart from authored
colour. So `join -> material(red) -> join -> render` rendered the inner
join's manufactured white and ignored the Material entirely - the outer
join saw HasVertexColor() and took the "input already has colour"
branch. The merge now bakes colour only when there is real colour to
preserve: some input carries authored vertexColor or per-instance
colour, or the inputs' albedos actually differ. When it does bake, it
bakes each input's absolute colour and GetMaterial() reports a neutral
albedo, so the shader product reproduces each part exactly instead of
tinting every part by whichever input materialFrom points at.
Regression from d135d88, shipped in v0.3.4.
2. Invisible material invalidation. The dirty check tracked MeshRevision,
matrices, instancers, mode and keepInputColours - not the input
materials it was baking. IGeometrySource has no MaterialRevision(), and
MaterialNode::MeshRevision() forwards its input's stamp verbatim, so a
colour change upstream of a merge could never invalidate the baked
colours; dragging the picker moved nothing at all. Input albedo is now
part of the dirty check (mBuiltAlbedos), and the per-input GetMaterial()
calls are fetched once per rebuild rather than three times, since joins
nest and that walk multiplies at every level.
Adds COLOURSWEEPTEST: a probe source with a fixed material feeds every
geometry-consuming node type and asserts none of them invent vertexColor
for a colourless mesh, plus three targeted Join checks including the exact
reported patch. Reverting either fix fails it.

parsed_message.title: feat(plugins): surface skipped VST2 plugins in the scan results
parsed_message.description: surface skipped VST2 plugins in the scan results
parsed_message.body:
The VST3 directory walk now also flags top-level entries with a
recognized-but-unsupported plugin extension - a ".vst" bundle (macOS
VST2) or a bare ".dll"/".vst" file sitting directly in a scanned VST3
folder (a Windows VST2 binary dropped in by mistake). Files living
inside a valid ".vst3" bundle are never visited by this walk in the
first place, so they're never misflagged.
Platform::UnsupportedPluginsSeen() reports the list, following the
exact contract of the existing VST3ScanFailures(): reset at the start
of every EnumerateVST3Plugins() call, read immediately after. It's
plumbed through PluginScanner the same way mFailed/mPendingFailed
already travel, and surfaced in the Plugins panel next to the
blocklist/failed-bundle trees as an expandable "N VST2 plugins found
and skipped - Infinite hosts VST3 and AU only" entry, worded so it
reads as a format limitation rather than a bug - the same reasoning
FailedBundles was built on.
kIndexSchemaVersion is not bumped: Entry's shape is unchanged, this is
an additive sibling list, so no rescan needs to be forced.
VST2 hosting itself remains explicitly out of scope. This is
filename/extension detection only - the files are never opened,
loaded, or executed. That's a licensing decision, not a technical
one: Steinberg stopped issuing new VST2 SDK licenses in October 2018,
so there's no way to legally host VST2 plugins in a new codebase.

parsed_message.title: feat(3d): add Explode by Loose Parts (connected components)
parsed_message.description: add Explode by Loose Parts (connected components)
parsed_message.body:
Explode's `by` param now selects Faces (unchanged default: push each
triangle along its own normal, flat-shading in the process) or Loose Parts
(push each connected component of the mesh outward as a rigid unit).
Loose-parts detection unions triangle corners by BuildWeldMap()
representative id, not raw vertex index - primitives duplicate vertices at
every UV seam/hard edge (e.g. Cube(1) has 24 vertices for 8 corners), so
union-find over raw indices would shatter one physical part into several
bogus components along its own seams. A plain array-based union-find with
path compression settles component ids per triangle from its root.
Each component is pushed along normalize(componentCentroid - meshCentroid)
by amount * (0.4 + RandFrom(seed, componentId) * 0.6), reusing the exact
RandFrom call shape from the existing face-explode path so the seed slider
feels consistent between modes. Degenerate case (component centroid
coincides with the mesh centroid): fall back to the component's area-
weighted average face normal; if that's also near-zero, leave the part in
place.
The loose-parts path deliberately skips RecalculateNormals(in, true,
false) - that flat-shades and duplicates vertices per face, which is
correct for face-explode but would destroy each part's original shading
here. It operates on a plain copy of the input mesh and only moves
existing vertex positions.
Wired the `by` enum into GeometryOpNode's shared param struct
(explodeBy), VisitParams (save/load), the mesh-cache Signature/operator==
(so toggling it rebuilds), and a "by" dropdown next to Explode's
amount/seed sliders in main.cpp, matching the existing per-op dropdown
convention (e.g. TrailsNode's blend dropdown).
Build is clean and the full geometry-transform-sweep passes.

parsed_message.title: feat(blend): add Anti-Erase mode as the exact complement of Erase
parsed_message.description: add Anti-Erase mode as the exact complement of Erase
parsed_message.body:
User request: "Erase does work like a mask in every way - it just needs
an invert button. Or an anti-erase blend mode." Implemented as mode 31
rather than an invert checkbox: a mode index already saves/loads/undoes
and appears in the dropdown for free, while a checkbox would need a new
VisitParams entry, a patch-format field, and a params-panel slot on two
different node types (BlendNode and LayerStackNode) - and it would sit
greyed-out for the other 30 modes that don't use it.
Naming: considered "Mask" per the original phrasing ("Erase... works
like a mask"), but the Node Reference Manual already uses "Mask" as a
term for other, unrelated things (the "Unsharp Mask" filter node, and

parsed_message.description: add pivot point to Transform op (GeometryOpNode kTransform)
parsed_message.body:
Adds pivotX/Y/Z to the Transform geometry op so rotate/scale happen about
an arbitrary point instead of always the mesh's own origin. Matrix
composition becomes T(pos) . T(pivot) . R . S . T(-pivot); at the default
pivot (0,0,0) both translations are identity so this is a bit-identical
no-op with the prior behavior (verified via geometry-transform-sweep, all
sweeps pass unchanged).
Scoped deliberately to the Transform op only, not all ten primitive node
headers that separately redeclare posX/Y/Z - that would mean touching
Geometry3DNodes.h, ShapeNode.h, ModelSourceNode.h, Text3DNode.h,
OceanNode.h, UtilityNodes.h (x2), AudioRibbonNode.h, SimulationNodes.h,
CurveNode.h and TextNode.h for one concept, which is out of scope for this
fix. One node (the Transform geometry op), one param panel.
Registers pivotX/Y/Z in VisitParams for save/load, and folds them into
GeometryOpNode::Signature so a pivot-only change invalidates the mesh
cache. Adds "pivot x/y/z" sliders to the Transform params panel in
main.cpp, alongside the existing move/rotate/scale controls.

parsed_message.title: fix(instancing): carry mesh point colours into Instance on Points
parsed_message.description: carry mesh point colours into Instance on Points
parsed_message.body:
InstanceOnPointsNode::Rebuild's mesh point-source path (the one every
Image to Points -> Points to Vertices -> Instance on Points graph uses)
built mTransforms but never pushed anything into mColors, which was
cleared at the top of Rebuild(). Instances always rendered white for
this path, even though MeshPoint already carries r/g/b (populated by
MeshOps::ToPoints from Mesh::vertexColor) and every consumer already
reads InstanceColors() and forwards it to MeshOps::RealizeInstances.
The particle-cloud path already did this correctly (pushes p.r/g/b
alongside each transform); mirrored that pattern for the mesh path,
pushing colour on the exact same loop iterations as the transform so
the two arrays stay index-aligned.

parsed_message.title: fix(3d): correct Join Geometry vertex-colour merge and keep per-input colour
parsed_message.description: correct Join Geometry vertex-colour merge and keep per-input colour
parsed_message.body:
JoinGeometryNode::Rebuild's kMerge branch only appended placed.vertexColor
when non-empty, without padding to placed.vertices.size()*3 for inputs that
lacked vertex colour. That misaligned colour data with vertex indices
whenever a colourless input preceded a coloured one (and usually silently
dropped colour entirely once Mesh::HasVertexColor()'s size check failed).
It also meant a merged mesh always rendered with one material/colour
(materialFrom's), so e.g. a red sphere merged with a yellow cube came out
entirely red.
Fix always appends exactly one colour triple per vertex per input: the
input's own placed.vertexColor when well-formed, otherwise a fill of that
input's material albedo (Material::color). This keeps mCache.vertexColor
index-aligned with mCache.vertices and lets each merged part keep its own
colour via the existing aVertexColor render path.
Adds a new "keep input colours" bool param (default on) next to "material
from input" so merge can still reproduce the old single-material look when
turned off. Registered in VisitParams for save/load, and tracked in the
node's dirty-check (mBuiltKeepInputColours) so toggling it triggers a
rebuild.
Verified with geometry-transform-sweep's driver.sh (all sweeps pass).

parsed_message.title: fix(blend): weight blend result by backdrop alpha, fix output-alpha compositing
parsed_message.description: weight blend result by backdrop alpha, fix output-alpha compositing
parsed_message.body:
BlendNode.cpp and LayerStackNode.cpp both mixed the blend-mode result
directly against unpremultiplied a.rgb/acc.rgb and combined alpha with
max(a.a, b.a). Where the backdrop was transparent, blendMode() was fed
whatever colour sat under alpha 0 (usually black), so Multiply/Darken/
Burn etc. produced black fringes around transparent edges. And max()
alpha meant stacking two 50% layers gave 0.5 instead of the correct
0.75.
Replaced both compositing steps with the standard source-over formula:
as = source coverage (uMix * b.a in BlendNode; amt = uOpacity*layer.a
in LayerStackNode)
cs = mix(source.rgb, blended, backdrop.a)   -- mode degrades to Normal
as the backdrop's alpha goes to 0
ar = as + backdrop.a * (1 - as)
cr = (cs*as + backdrop.rgb*backdrop.a*(1-as)) / ar, guarded for ar~0
Verified algebraically that for the common opaque-over-opaque case
(a.a == b.a == 1, uMix == 1 / amt == 1) this reduces to exactly the old
behaviour: cs collapses to `blended`, ar collapses to 1, and cr
collapses to `blended` -- bit-identical to the previous
mix(a.rgb, blended, uMix*b.a) / max(a.a,b.a) result. So every existing
patch blending two fully-opaque layers is unaffected; only partially
transparent backdrops/layers change (correctly).
Erase branches (uMode/uModes[i] == kEraseMode) are untouched in both
files, per the bug report -- Erase's current alpha-only behaviour is
correct.
Cleanup: replaced the magic number 30 with BlendModes::kEraseMode in
both shader-string erase checks.
Did not hoist a shared composite GLSL snippet into BlendModes.h: the
two call sites use different variable names and control flow (a/b pair
with an early erase early-return vs. an accumulator loop with
continue), so sharing would need an awkward macro/snippet with several
parameters and wouldn't meaningfully reduce duplication. Fixed both
copies independently instead.
Build verified clean via cmake --build build.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

parsed_message.title: fix(mesh): weld duplicate vertices when accumulating smooth normals
parsed_message.description: weld duplicate vertices when accumulating smooth normals
parsed_message.body:
Root cause: MeshOps::RecalculateNormals's smooth path accumulated face
normals through the raw, unwelded `indices` array. Every primitive in
this codebase duplicates vertices at UV seams and hard edges (PushGrid
gives Cube(1) 24 vertices for 8 corners, see the comment near
BuildWeldMap's caller), so each duplicate only ever accumulated its own
single face normal. On a cube, where every vertex belongs to exactly
one face, that made smooth normals identical to flat normals -
the Normals node with "flat shade" off appeared to do nothing. On a UV
sphere/cylinder the seam vertices were never averaged with their
duplicates, producing a visible normal seam and a wrong-reading
cylinder cap rim.
Fix: accumulate face normals per weld-group representative (via
BuildWeldMap(in), the same helper and pattern MeshOps::Smooth already
uses for vertex positions), normalize per representative, then copy
each representative's normal back out to every vertex in its group.
Geometry itself is not welded - vertex count and positions are
unchanged, only the normal each duplicate reports is now shared with
its coincident neighbors. This also composes correctly with the flip
option: winding/flip is applied per accumulated normal exactly as
before, so a flipped-winding mesh still welds and flips consistently.
Explicit judgement call: no angle threshold / auto-smooth option was
added. `flat shade` is already the "keep every edge hard" answer, and
a threshold would introduce a parameter this node doesn't currently
expose.
Verified: full rebuild is clean, and
.claude/skills/geometry-transform-sweep/driver.sh passes all sweeps.

parsed_message.title: fix(mesh): make RecalculateNormals flip actually reverse winding
parsed_message.description: make RecalculateNormals flip actually reverse winding
parsed_message.body:
MeshOps::RecalculateNormals's flip=true path only negated the computed
normal vector; Mesh::indices winding was left untouched. Since the main
3D render shader does back-face culling with no gl_FrontFacing fixup,
flipping normals without reversing winding didn't invert the surface —
it just lit the same visible faces from behind, going black. (The node
mini-viewport shader does have a gl_FrontFacing fixup, so preview and
final render disagreed on any flipped mesh.)
Fix: when flip is true, also reverse each triangle's winding — swap the
2nd/3rd vertex in out.indices in the smooth (shared-vertex) path, and
emit the three expanded vertices in reversed order in the flat
(unshared-vertex) path. The winding reversal happens after normals are
computed from the original winding, and the already-negated normal is
exactly what the reversed winding would itself produce, so the two stay
consistent — orientation is genuinely inverted, matching Blender's Flip
Normals.
GeometryOpNodes.cpp's Displace and Wrap ops both call
MeshOps::RecalculateNormals directly for their own flipNormals handling
(no duplicated flip logic), so they pick up the fix automatically.

parsed_message.title: fix(field): retune noise-driven synth gain staging, rebuild foliage as clustered points
parsed_message.description: retune noise-driven synth gain staging, rebuild foliage as clustered points
parsed_message.body:
The sin-hash noise fix made noise genuinely broadband, but the highpass/
resonant-filter stages downstream (Snare, Hi-Hat, Noise Sweeper) were
gain-staged against the old correlated noise's much lower post-filter
energy, so they now overdrive their soft-clip and produce audible
distortion. Reduced their pre-clip gains and softened the clip curves;
Sweeper's resonant filter had no output limiter at all, so its feedback
could ring well past +-1 - added one and trimmed the feedback amount.
Piano's hammer-noise excitation was too large a fraction of the strike
transient and had no limiter on partial 1; scaled it down and restored
a soft limiter.
Bonsai Foliage Canopy was a continuous noise-shaped Sphere, so no matter
how the formula was tuned it could only ever read as a bumpy ball -
structurally the wrong technique for foliage. Rebuilt it the same way
the existing Flower/Pine Tree/Mushroom presets build organic detail:
Points topology with explicit golden-angle-placed clusters, each an
independent puffy blob, giving actual bonsai foliage pads instead of a
single lumpy sphere. Brilliant Cut Diamond's normal was a coarse
per-band constant instead of the true slanted facet-plane normal, so
lit facets barely differed from each other; computed the real pavilion/
crown/table plane normals so the facets actually catch light distinctly.

parsed_message.title: fix(field): replace flawed noise generator, rework Piano and Bell synthesis
parsed_message.description: replace flawed noise generator, rework Piano and Bell synthesis
parsed_message.body:
The multiplicative-congruential real-number recurrence used for noise
(seed = (seed*11035.152+0.12345)%1.0) short-cycled and correlated,
producing a tonal "screech" instead of broadband noise, which also
degraded every noise-dependent preset (snare, hi-hat, sweeper, crackle,
raindrops). Replaced with a standard sin-hash pseudo-random generator
across all five.
Acoustic Grand Piano used an exact 2x harmonic ratio and a per-sample
soft-saturator; real piano partials are stretched sharp of integer
ratios (inharmonicity), so the second partial now sits at 2.035x, and
the saturator was removed to free register budget for a hammer-noise
excitation "chiff" (the compiler's SSA-only allocator has no register
reuse and the original was already at 122/128 registers).
Crystalline Tubular Bell used arbitrary partial ratios (1, 2.76, 5.40),
which read as xylophone-like rather than bell-like. Replaced with the
named partials of real bell acoustics - prime, tierce (the
characteristic minor-third "bell" dissonance), and nominal (perceived
strike pitch/brightness) - trimmed to 3 partials to fit the register cap.
parsed_message.raw:
fix(field): replace flawed noise generator, rework Piano and Bell synthesis

The multiplicative-congruential real-number recurrence used for noise
(seed = (seed*11035.152+0.12345)%1.0) short-cycled and correlated,
producing a tonal "screech" instead of broadband noise, which also
degraded every noise-dependent preset (snare, hi-hat, sweeper, crackle,
raindrops). Replaced with a standard sin-hash pseudo-random generator
across all five.

Acoustic Grand Piano used an exact 2x harmonic ratio and a per-sample
soft-saturator; real piano partials are stretched sharp of integer
ratios (inharmonicity), so the second partial now sits at 2.035x, and
the saturator was removed to free register budget for a hammer-noise
excitation "chiff" (the compiler's SSA-only allocator has no register
reuse and the original was already at 122/128 registers).

Crystalline Tubular Bell used arbitrary partial ratios (1, 2.76, 5.40),
which read as xylophone-like rather than bell-like. Replaced with the
named partials of real bell acoustics - prime, tierce (the
characteristic minor-third "bell" dissonance), and nominal (perceived
strike pitch/brightness) - trimmed to 3 partials to fit the register cap.

parsed_message.title: fix(field): stop constant folder from mistaking vector literals for scalars
parsed_message.description: stop constant folder from mistaking vector literals for scalars
parsed_message.body:
vec3(1.0, 0.2, 0.2)'s IR Literal node stores numberValue = vecValues[0]
for reporting convenience, but the x*0/x*1/+0/-0 identity folds and the
both-literals arithmetic fold read that field without checking lanes,
so a vector literal whose first component was 0.0 or 1.0 got silently
treated as the scalar identity and dropped from the expression - which
broke the Cybernetic Skull Hologram pixel preset (eyes * vec3(1.0, 0.2, 0.2)
collapsed to just eyes, leaving a stale vec3 type on the surviving node).

parsed_message.title: fix(ui): crop overflow toolbar items instead of overlapping, restore tab gap
parsed_message.description: crop overflow toolbar items instead of overlapping, restore tab gap
parsed_message.body:

was positioned by an absolute cursorX with no awareness of how far the
left cluster (menus/transport/BPM/telemetry) had grown, so on a narrow
window the two clusters would draw on top of each other. They now check
available space against the left cluster's actual extent and drop
lowest-priority items first (icon toggles, then search, then Update)
instead of overlapping.

a later commit had regressed the value tuned to fix the exact same
"adjacent rounded highlights read as one merged blob" issue.

parsed_message.title: Fix crash-on-click in the new UI Debugger's Item Picker
parsed_message.description: Fix crash-on-click in the new UI Debugger's Item Picker
parsed_message.body:
All 3 of today's crash reports (~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports) share
one root cause: ImGui::ItemHoverable's Item Picker check,
`if (g.DebugItemPickerBreakId == id) IM_DEBUG_BREAK();`. The stock
IM_DEBUG_BREAK on this platform is __builtin_debugtrap() - a real SIGTRAP,
fine under a debugger but fatal in a plain double-clicked .app with none
attached. Menu > "UI Debugger / Item Picker" (added last round to let UI
feedback point at an exact widget) exposes exactly this path, and it fired
whether the clicked item was a canvas node or a control inside the
Debugger window itself - every crash trace ends in the same line.
Redefined IM_DEBUG_BREAK() to a no-op in imconfig.h: the Item Picker's
hover highlighting still works, only the trap-on-click is defused.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

parsed_message.title: Delete dialog borders and dock separators; unify the accent emphasis ladder
parsed_message.description: Delete dialog borders and dock separators; unify the accent emphasis ladder
parsed_message.body:
Three fixes, all chosen so they cannot ping-pong between light and dark.
1. No border on any floating window or popup (style.WindowBorderSize /
PopupBorderSize = 0, and PushElevatedPanelStyle zeroes its own sizes).
Every "black/white edge around the dialog" report has been this 1px
outline: it straddles two backgrounds (the dialog's fill on one side,
whatever it floats over on the other), so no colour is right against
both and each theme change re-breaks it. The opaque fill, rounding and
shadow already say "this is above the canvas".
2. No divider line on docked panels (viewport / mod-matrix / perf panel).
Same straddling problem - it was a fixed dark constant, then a themed
one, and read wrong both times. The panel's panelBg fill against the
canvas' windowBg is the separation.
Both are theme-independent: there is no longer an element to mis-colour.
3. One accent emphasis ladder. Selection states were the accent at nine
different alphas composited over whatever sat behind them, which is why
the Settings tab, the browser Modules tab, a selected list row and the
Field editor's Apply button read as four unrelated purples from one
accent. AccentTint/AccentEmphasis{Hover,Selected,Pressed} pre-composite
over panelBg and return opaque colours, so an emphasis level is the same
RGB everywhere. ApplyTheme's Header*/Tab* now share those exact
constants, and the hand-rolled "selected" blues that never tracked the
theme at all (Export/Record format toggles x5, audio-record format
toggle, macro radio selector, perf Edit Mode, library now-playing row)
route through them too.

Fix Performance Matrix Edit Mode: NumBox double box, Bipolar knob drag, Toggle size, light-mode black boxes

Four related bugs in the Performance Matrix's Edit Mode controls and
light-mode rendering:

- NumBox (kind 6) drew a hand-drawn background/border, then let DragFloat's
  PushSliderStyle-pushed FrameBg/Border paint a second frame on top -
  visible as a "double box", loudest in light mode where the border is
  opaque. Scope FrameBg/FrameBgHovered/FrameBgActive/Border to transparent
  and FrameBorderSize to 0 around just that DragFloat call.

- Bipolar knob (kind 8, Pan/Detent) didn't respond to drag. Root cause was
  not a missing PushID (DrawPerfElement already scopes one per element) but
  BipolarKnobFloat ending with ImGui::Dummy() instead of ImGui::ItemSize() -
  Dummy's ItemAdd(bb, 0) overwrites g.LastItemData with a zero id, so
  DrawPerfElement's post-call IsItemActive() check (dragHold()) always saw a
  dead item and erased the held raw drag value every frame the knob was
  mid-drag. KnobFloat already carries this exact fix with an explanatory
  comment; BipolarKnobFloat didn't.

- Toggle (kind 3) nearly filled its 1x1 cell (cardSize-18/-28), oversized
  next to every other control. Capped it the same way Knob's diameter is
  capped: cellSize * 0.52, clamped 28..44.

  shown on every IModulator node - LFO, Pattern, etc.) and the Drum
  Sequencer's own step grid (distinct from PatternNode's already
  theme-aware DrawPatternStepGrid) both hardcoded a near-black fill
  regardless of theme. Made both theme-aware - the meter reuses the
  existing ScopeBgCol/ScopeBorderCol/ScopeMidLineCol helpers, the step grid
  gets a light-mode palette matching DrawPatternStepGrid's own.

Verified with a temporary screenshot fixture (spawning Toggle/NumBox/two
Bipolar-knob perf elements, and separately a Drum Sequencer + Pattern + LFO
+ Mod Curve node cluster) in both GitHub Light and Nord presets; fixture was
reverted before this commit, confirmed by diff.

parsed_message.title: Add theme-preset swatch previews; fix Nord's low-contrast dim text
parsed_message.description: Add theme-preset swatch previews; fix Nord's low-contrast dim text
parsed_message.body:
Task A: the Appearance tab's theme combo was plain text, so a user had
to already know what "Dracula" or "Tokyo Night" looked like to pick
between them. Each dropdown row now draws three small bordered
swatches (panelBg/text/accent) fingerprinting that preset, plus the
same strip next to the closed combo's current-selection label. Added
CategoryColors::UiThemeForPreset(index) to read any preset's UiTheme
without switching the live one. Swatch borders are chosen from the
live theme's own polarity (light live theme -> dark border, dark live
theme -> light border) rather than each swatch's own color, so a
near-white or near-black preset swatch stays legible against a
same-toned active popup. Verified with the live theme set to
Catppuccin Latte, Infinite, and GitHub Light in turn.
Task B: measured textDim-vs-panelBg contrast across all 9 presets.
Nord came in far below the rest (~1.36:1, next-worst was Tokyo Night
at ~2.5:1) - TextDisabled-style text (e.g. "audio off" in the top bar)
was nearly unreadable in Nord specifically. Blended Nord's textDim
50/50 toward nord4 to land at ~3.6-4.4:1 against panel/window, keeping
the same blue-grey hue. Verified before/after via a temporary
Infinite.theme override (backed up and restored).

parsed_message.body:
Real-world .ply files people download (Sketchfab, photogrammetry scans,
CloudCompare/MeshLab exports) are almost never trained 3DGS output - they're
plain x,y,z,red,green,blue point clouds. LoadSplatPly was silently applying
the trained-3DGS field-present-but-zero defaults to these (SH-DC-missing ->
flat 0.5 gray, opacity-missing -> sigmoid(0)=0.5, scale-missing -> exp(0)=1.0
world-unit radius), which rendered as one solid semi-transparent gray blob
once thousands of 1-unit splats overlapped.
LoadSplatPly now falls back per field when the trained property is absent:
conversion; falls through to flat gray only if neither is present.
opaque (1.0) if neither is present, instead of the old 0.5.
point density (bounding-box diagonal / cbrt(splat count)) in a second
pass after UpdateBounds(), instead of a fixed 1.0-world-unit radius.
SplatCloud::hadTrainedFields is set false whenever any of the above fired,
and SplatSourceNode's status string now appends "(no scale/opacity/color
data - auto-estimated)" so a degraded load isn't mistaken for a real one.
All three fallbacks are gated on property presence in the header, decided
once before the vertex loop, so a real 3DGS export (INFINITE_SPLATIOTEST's
fixture, all fields present) takes the exact same code path as before -
verified unchanged. Extended that fixture with a new bare-color-cloud .ply
covering the fallback path, and added an end-to-end check through the real
SplatSourceNode + Render3DNode (INFINITE_SPLATNODETEST) confirming real red
pixels render (not flat gray) at a sane, non-1.0 splat size.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
parsed_message.raw:
Splat loader: degrade gracefully for plain colored point cloud .ply

Real-world .ply files people download (Sketchfab, photogrammetry scans,
CloudCompare/MeshLab exports) are almost never trained 3DGS output - they're
plain x,y,z,red,green,blue point clouds. LoadSplatPly was silently applying
the trained-3DGS field-present-but-zero defaults to these (SH-DC-missing ->
flat 0.5 gray, opacity-missing -> sigmoid(0)=0.5, scale-missing -> exp(0)=1.0
world-unit radius), which rendered as one solid semi-transparent gray blob
once thousands of 1-unit splats overlapped.

LoadSplatPly now falls back per field when the trained property is absent:
  - color: f_dc_0/1/2 missing -> red/green/blue (0-255) directly, no SH_C0
    conversion; falls through to flat gray only if neither is present.
  - opacity: opacity missing -> alpha (0-255) directly (not sigmoid'd); fully
    opaque (1.0) if neither is present, instead of the old 0.5.
  - scale: scale_0/1/2 missing -> a radius estimated from the cloud's own
    point density (bounding-box diagonal / cbrt(splat count)) in a second
    pass after UpdateBounds(), instead of a fixed 1.0-world-unit radius.
SplatCloud::hadTrainedFields is set false whenever any of the above fired,
and SplatSourceNode's status string now appends "(no scale/opacity/color
data - auto-estimated)" so a degraded load isn't mistaken for a real one.

All three fallbacks are gated on property presence in the header, decided
once before the vertex loop, so a real 3DGS export (INFINITE_SPLATIOTEST's
fixture, all fields present) takes the exact same code path as before -
verified unchanged. Extended that fixture with a new bare-color-cloud .ply
covering the fallback path, and added an end-to-end check through the real
SplatSourceNode + Render3DNode (INFINITE_SPLATNODETEST) confirming real red
pixels render (not flat gray) at a sane, non-1.0 splat size.

parsed_message.description: Fix Video In opening the wrong/no camera when no device is chosen
parsed_message.body:
An empty deviceId (meaning "auto-pick") was passed straight through to
Platform::CameraOpen, but the two platforms disagree on what empty
means: macOS silently falls back to AVFoundation's own default device
(often the built-in FaceTime cam, not a plugged-in USB capture card),
while Windows treats it as a hard failure and never opens anything.
The UI dropdown already resolved and displayed the intended default
device from the same isDefault/first-device logic, but never told the
node what it had picked, so what the UI showed and what actually got
opened were two different things.

parsed_message.description: Phase 3: SplatSourceNode - Gaussian Splat node in the palette
bullets: IGeometrySource::SplatSizeMultiplier/SplatOpacityMultiplier/GetSplatTint,

parsed_message.body:
Adds SplatSourceNode (src/nodes/SplatSourceNode.h/.cpp), a terminal
IGeometrySource that loads a .ply/.splat Gaussian splat cloud (file picker
or drop) and feeds Render3D's Phase 2 EWA-splatting pass end to end.
Controls (7, mirroring ModelSourceNode's file-node conventions): file
picker+drop, point size (modulatable), opacity (modulatable), tint
(colour), crop (radius from centroid), max splats (opacity*scale budget).
No SH-mode control: SplatIO already collapses SH down to a single flat
linear colour at load time, so there is nothing left for a mode dropdown
to switch between.
Crop/max-splats are edit-time reductions baked into a derived cloud
(SplatSourceNode::RebuildDerivedCloud, gated by its own cache signature
of load-revision+crop+maxSplats per new-geometry-node SKILL.md S4); point
size/opacity/tint are live per-frame multipliers so they can be modulated
without re-cooking the GPU data texture (design doc S8).
Required minimal additions to the Phase 2 render path to support the live
multipliers (not a refactor):
with forwarding implementations added to every wrapper/passthrough node
(AudioDisplacementNode, FieldElementNode, GenerativeNodes, GeometryOpNodes,
PointDistributionNodes, UtilityNodes, Switcher3DNode) per the
new-geometry-node passthrough-forwarding rule.
quad radius, so the EWA falloff shape grows with it), uOpacityMult and
uTint multiply into vColor.
splatTint fields - without this the new live uniforms would silently
freeze under modulation, since CookIfNeeded's cache gate only compared
the existing signature fields.
GL_POINTS point-cloud path as a cheap splat-cloud approximation (per
design doc's explicit allowance).
(PlatformWin.cpp).
Wiring: CMakeLists.txt, main.cpp include/REGISTER_NODE("Gaussian Splat",
"3D")/help text/DrawSplatSourceParams+dispatch entry, and a drop-handler
branch. ".ply" is ambiguous with ModelSourceNode's existing mesh-import
extension, so a bare .ply drop is unchanged (still spawns Model 3D) unless
dropped directly onto an existing Gaussian Splat node; ".splat" is never
ambiguous and always targets the splat node.

Adds SplatSourceNode (src/nodes/SplatSourceNode.h/.cpp), a terminal
IGeometrySource that loads a .ply/.splat Gaussian splat cloud (file picker
or drop) and feeds Render3D's Phase 2 EWA-splatting pass end to end.

picker+drop, point size (modulatable), opacity (modulatable), tint

linear colour at load time, so there is nothing left for a mode dropdown
to switch between.

(SplatSourceNode::RebuildDerivedCloud, gated by its own cache signature
of load-revision+crop+maxSplats per new-geometry-node SKILL.md S4); point

without re-cooking the GPU data texture (design doc S8).

parsed_message.title: Add GPU Gaussian splat rendering to Render3DNode (Phase 2)
parsed_message.description: Add GPU Gaussian splat rendering to Render3DNode (Phase 2)
parsed_message.body:
IGeometrySource gets GetSplatCloud()/SplatCloudRevision() (nullptr/0
default), forwarded through every passthrough wrapper (GeometryOpNode,
DisplacementNode, SetColorNode, WrapNode, MergeByDistanceNode,
Null3DNode, MaterialNode, MappingNode, AudioDisplacementNode,
MeshResynthNode, FieldElementNode, Switcher3DNode) so a splat cloud
survives every existing node chain instead of silently vanishing.
Render3DNode draws splats in a second pass after opaque geometry:
depth test on/write off, premultiplied additive-over blending,
back-to-front order. GPU state per slot (GpuSplat) uploads splat data
into a static GL_RGBA32F texture (4 texels/splat: pos+opacity,
cov0-2, cov3-5, rgb) only when SplatCloudRevision() changes; per-frame
cost is just a GL_R32UI index VBO (glVertexAttribDivisor=1) driving
glDrawArraysInstanced. A persistent background thread (SplatSorter)
computes back-to-front order via a 16-bit-quantized O(N) counting
sort and hands the render thread a completed index buffer
non-blockingly, skipping the sort entirely when the camera hasn't
moved enough. The vertex shader (GLSL 150) projects the 3D covariance
to 2D via the EWA Jacobian, eigendecomposes it for a 3-sigma quad, and
culls behind the near plane; the fragment shader computes Gaussian
falloff from the conic and discards below 1/255 alpha. A VRAM/
fill-rate budget guard mirrors the existing sprite guard.
Verified against all 4 stated exit criteria with real compiled-binary
test runs (INFINITE_SPLATRENDERTEST, INFINITE_SPLATORBITTEST,
INFINITE_SPLATCACHETEST, all ad hoc fixtures gated behind getenv, not
wired into run-infinite-hygiene). GROUP_3D and the fast tier of
run-infinite-hygiene both pass with no regressions; clean build with
no new compiler warnings in any touched file.
Node UI, SplatSourceNode, and Field processing of splats are
explicitly out of scope for this phase (see docs/plans/
gaussian-splat-node.md).

Add Gaussian splatting research, design plan, and implementation prompt

Research doc covering the algorithm, 2026 format/tooling standards, the
offline-conversion decision, macOS/Windows parity, and reference repos —
plus a four-phase build plan and a copy-paste prompt scoped to phases 1-2.

Two constraints read out of this tree drove the whole design:
- GL 3.3 core with #version 150 shaders (main.cpp:47889) rules out compute
  shaders and GPU sorting, so the WebGL2-class architecture (static data
  texture + CPU sort + small per-frame index buffer) is the port target.
- Render3D's existing instanced billboard path for point clouds
  (Geometry3DNodes.cpp:1732) is what the splat pass extends.

Also assessed whether Field has a place here. It does not belong in the hot
path — the sort is not expressible and the element backend is a CPU
interpreter — but a one-shot conditioning pass at edit time is worth having.
That changes a phase-1 decision: the loader now retains de-log'd scale and
the normalised quaternion on the CPU struct (28 B/splat, never uploaded) so a
later Field pass does not need a per-splat eigendecomposition.

parsed_message.title: Carry gesture recordings and expressions across undo, duplicate and paste
parsed_message.description: Carry gesture recordings and expressions across undo, duplicate and paste
bullets: Undo/Redo left recordings running. ApplyPatchData respawns every node
Duplicate and paste dropped expressions and recordings entirely.
parsed_message.body:
Three pieces of per-param state key off (nodeIndex, paramIndex) and live
outside the node, so anything that respawns or copies nodes has to move
them by hand. Modulation links and palette bindings already were. Typed
expressions and Shift-drag recordings were not, in different places:
with a fresh index, so a recording either kept driving a param the undo
had just restored (undo visibly "didn't stick") or landed on whatever
unrelated node next took its index. NewPatch cleared Modulation but not
the recorder, so recordings also leaked into the next patch, and node
delete had no GestureRecorder counterpart to UnbindAllFor.
The undo stack now stores UndoEntry { patch, gestures } and restores
the recordings through the same old->new remap RemapViewportPanelNodes
uses. Since a knob grab pushes its checkpoint before NotifyMovement,
record -> undo removes the recording and redo brings it back, matching
what a typed expression (which is in Patch::Data) already did.
CaptureClusterLinks/ApplyClusterLinks carried three parallel vectors
through five call sites, so each new kind of state was a ten-site edit
nobody made. They now take one ClusterClipboard, with exprs and
gestures added; a copied recording keeps its startTime so the duplicate
loops in phase with the original.
Also, in the EQ visualizer: the curve is drawn from all five bands but
only the selected band's knobs exist, so once the bands stopped sharing
a paramIndex a loop on a band you had switched away from moved the curve
with nothing on screen to explain or stop it. Each band's handles now
carry the knob's recording red, and grabbing one cancels the loops on
exactly the params that drag writes.
New GESTUREUNDOTEST covers record/undo/redo. Undo/Redo route the clock
through GestureClockNow(): they are reachable from headless fixtures
that run before ImGui::CreateContext(), and ImGui::GetTime() dereferences
GImGui unconditionally (PERFMATRIXTEST segfaulted on it).
WTDRAGTEST baselined: it fails only under driver.sh, and does so equally
on a clean HEAD build with this work stashed out.

parsed_message.title: Give each EQ band its own param index
parsed_message.description: Give each EQ band its own param index
parsed_message.body:
The five bands' freq/Q/gain knobs all went through
`row.Knob("freq", n->ParamPtr(kEqFreqParam[selBand]), ...)`, so
gParamCounter issued ONE ordinal per knob for all five bands and
DiscreteParamSlot hashed ONE slot for all five `type` dropdowns. A
gesture recorded on band 1's freq kept replaying (and drawing red)
after switching to band 3, driving band 3's freq; a modulator bound

parsed_message.title: Fix knob gesture recording: trailing Dummy was eating the item state
parsed_message.description: Fix knob gesture recording: trailing Dummy was eating the item state
parsed_message.body:
KnobFloat and VFaderFloat both ended with ImGui::Dummy() to reserve the
full layout cell. Dummy is ItemSize *plus* ItemAdd(bb, 0), and that
ItemAdd overwrites g.LastItemData with a zero id - so every
IsItemActivated/IsItemActive/IsItemHovered that ModKnob runs after the
widget returns was querying the spacer, not the InvisibleButton.
IsItemActive() is false for an id-0 item even mid-drag, so ModKnob's
whole post-draw block was dead: no undo checkpoint on grab, no
GestureRecorder::StopPlayback, and no NotifyMovement. Shift+drag never
opened a recording session, so IsRecording() stayed false and the red
tint from 2cc158a/69ec2f9 never had anything to show - on the EQ band
freq/Q/gain knobs and on every other ModKnob in the app. ModSlider's
identical block always worked because ImGui::SliderFloat leaves its own
item last; BipolarKnobFloat and the fader path used by Macro Knob/Slider
worked because they call the recorder internally, before the Dummy.
Switching both to ImGui::ItemSize advances the layout cursor exactly as
Dummy did and leaves the InvisibleButton's item data standing.

parsed_message.title: test: add headless node-chain and mixed-stress perf fixtures
parsed_message.description: add headless node-chain and mixed-stress perf fixtures
parsed_message.body:
INFINITE_NODECHAINPERFTEST: spawns a synthetic Noise -> N x Invert -> Output
straight chain (INFINITE_PERFCHAINLEN) to measure per-node cook cost in
isolation. Used to confirm the N=800-1600 "hang" from the handover doc is a
GPU VRAM/texture-footprint ceiling (each node's own persistent FBO; default
1024x1024 RGBA8 - not a stack-depth or algorithmic issue), and is not
reachable at realistic graph sizes (~100-150 nodes).
INFINITE_MIXEDSTRESSTEST: builds a realistic-shape graph instead (3D
geometry tree + 12-voice audio rack + auto-bound LFO modulation,
INFINITE_MIXEDSTRESSTEST=<scale>) to stress what an actual patch looks like.
Surfaced a real finding: generic modulation landing on a few structurally-
expensive params (GeometryNode shape/detail/sides/bevel - full mesh rebuild,
Render3D width/height/antialias - FBO/shadow-map realloc, Join Geometry
mode - mesh-boolean CSG instead of concatenation) causes severe erratic
per-frame cost (75ms-9.8s) totally independent of node count. Excluding
those params from the auto-binder, the same 121-node graph holds a steady
~200fps. Both fixtures gated behind INFINITE_..._VERBOSE for per-frame
stderr logging.

parsed_message.title: perf: cache FilterNode uniform locations instead of querying every cook
parsed_message.description: cache FilterNode uniform locations instead of querying every cook
parsed_message.body:
glGetUniformLocation is a driver-side name lookup, not free, and every
uncached FilterNode cook was doing 5 + params.size() of them per frame.
Locations are fixed for the life of a linked GL program, so look them up
once in EnsureShader() and reuse them in RunShaderPass. Straight 400-node
filter chain: 70.61ms/frame -> 41.36ms/frame (~40% faster).

parsed_message.title: fix: snap-to-scale-then-clamp could leak out-of-key notes
parsed_message.description: snap-to-scale-then-clamp could leak out-of-key notes
parsed_message.body:
Random Note Generator, Bouncing Balls, and CV to Pitch all snapped a
pitch to the current scale and then clamped the result into the
node's lo/hi range with a plain numeric clamp. The range boundary
itself isn't guaranteed to be in-scale, so a wandering note could get
shoved onto an out-of-key boundary note (e.g. C#4 while locked to C
major pentatonic).
Add MusicTime::SnapToScaleInRange, which searches inward from the
crossed boundary for the nearest in-scale note instead of clamping
blindly, and use it at all three call sites.
parsed_message.raw:
fix: snap-to-scale-then-clamp could leak out-of-key notes

Random Note Generator, Bouncing Balls, and CV to Pitch all snapped a
pitch to the current scale and then clamped the result into the
node's lo/hi range with a plain numeric clamp. The range boundary
itself isn't guaranteed to be in-scale, so a wandering note could get
shoved onto an out-of-key boundary note (e.g. C#4 while locked to C
major pentatonic).

Add MusicTime::SnapToScaleInRange, which searches inward from the
crossed boundary for the nearest in-scale note instead of clamping
blindly, and use it at all three call sites.

ElementIRProgram's declaredAttribs list (ElementScope::

for it - ElementBackend's existing OpStoreAttrib codegen for a plain
local's first assignment was already unconditional, it was just

parsed_message.title: Field step 23: element neighbour reads (OPEN-B)
parsed_message.description: Field step 23: element neighbour reads (OPEN-B)
parsed_message.body:
Answers OPEN-B with the spelling decided in language-decisions-and-presets.md:
`X.at(k)` reads element k's X, where X is P, N, uv, Cd, a declared attrib, or
an element state cell. Step 22 made evolving textures writable; this makes
evolving meshes writable, which was the other half of the same ask.
The read always sees the cook's INPUT buffer - the incoming mesh for an
attribute, the previous cook's value for a state cell - never a value written
earlier in the same loop. That is the load-bearing rule: element j's result
must not depend on whether element j-1 has already run, or the loop stops
being vectorizable and the domain stops being deterministic. The VM snapshots
exactly the bases a kernel names, once, before any element runs; a kernel with
no `.at()` copies nothing. Indices clamp to [0, count-1], so element 0 asking
for i-1 sees itself and an open chain behaves like an open chain.
`.at()` on a param or frame value is refused with a message saying it holds one
value for the whole mesh, not one per element; outside an element kernel it
points a pixel kernel at `A(uv + d)` instead. The parser needed no change -
`P.at(i - 1)` already parsed as a dotted call.
`age` is now reserved in the element domain too, for the reason it was added to
pixel in step 22: a simulation needs a one-shot seed and `frame` is the global
cook counter. Element simulations must also keep their positions in state
rather than P, since the store is refilled from the incoming mesh every cook -
both new presets, Verlet Rope and Buckling Ribbon, are written that way.
A pre-existing bug surfaced: length, normalize, distance, dot and cross were
missing from the element interpreter and fell through its lane-wise if/else
chain as 0.0, so `length(P)` read zero for every vertex and the shipping
"Radial Ripple" and "Spherical Bulge" presets were uniform instead of radial.
fract, fmod and atan2 were missing the same way. All eight are implemented; a
zero-length normalize returns zero rather than NaN, matching the domain's
existing clamp-don't-poison rule for sqrt and log.
Verified by INFINITE_FIELDELEMENTTEST sections 11-16, including one test that
fails if the index is dropped and one that fails if the snapshot is taken after
the loop instead of before it. /run-infinite-hygiene passes except GROUPTEST,
which fails identically on clean main.

both new presets, Verlet Rope and Buckling Ribbon, are written that way.

A pre-existing bug surfaced: length, normalize, distance, dot and cross were
missing from the element interpreter and fell through its lane-wise if/else
chain as 0.0, so `length(P)` read zero for every vertex and the shipping
"Radial Ripple" and "Spherical Bulge" presets were uniform instead of radial.
fract, fmod and atan2 were missing the same way. All eight are implemented; a
zero-length normalize returns zero rather than NaN, matching the domain's
existing clamp-don't-poison rule for sqrt and log.

Verified by INFINITE_FIELDELEMENTTEST sections 11-16, including one test that
fails if the index is dropped and one that fails if the snapshot is taken after
the loop instead of before it. /run-infinite-hygiene passes except GROUPTEST,
which fails identically on clean main.

Answers OPEN-C from algorithms.md with the spelling decided in
language-decisions-and-presets.md: a pixel state cell can be read at a
coordinate, `A(uv + d)`, lowering to one texture() fetch of the previous
cook's cell. Bare `A` stays sugar for `A(uv)`. The boundary rule is
per-cell - `state float A = 1 [wrap]`, default clamp, `border` reads the
declared initial value - because wrap and clamp are two different pictures,
not two spellings of one. An offset read of a frame/element/sample cell is
refused with a message saying the cell has no spatial extent.
This is what makes reaction-diffusion, advection and every flow effect
writable as Field text instead of C++, and both ship as presets.
Adds `age`, a pixel reserved name holding cooks since the node's state was
cleared. A simulation needs a one-shot seed and `frame` cannot give one - it
is the global cook counter, already in the thousands when a node spawns - so
without `age` a Gray-Scott kernel starting from uniform B = 0 sits on a fixed
point forever.
A kernel containing any offset read gets an RGBA32F state bank; one without
keeps RGBA16F, since 16F drifts visibly within seconds for anything that
integrates but is exact enough for trails.

the CPU prologue evaluator, which does not know `res` - it evaluated to 0,
and every kernel that measured a texel got a texel size of zero.
the first at zero. The pixel partition now hoists scalars only.

parsed_message.raw:
Field step 22: offset reads of pixel state cells (OPEN-C)

Answers OPEN-C from algorithms.md with the spelling decided in
language-decisions-and-presets.md: a pixel state cell can be read at a
coordinate, `A(uv + d)`, lowering to one texture() fetch of the previous
cook's cell. Bare `A` stays sugar for `A(uv)`. The boundary rule is
per-cell - `state float A = 1 [wrap]`, default clamp, `border` reads the
declared initial value - because wrap and clamp are two different pictures,
not two spellings of one. An offset read of a frame/element/sample cell is
refused with a message saying the cell has no spatial extent.

This is what makes reaction-diffusion, advection and every flow effect
writable as Field text instead of C++, and both ship as presets.

Adds `age`, a pixel reserved name holding cooks since the node's state was
cleared. A simulation needs a one-shot seed and `frame` cannot give one - it
is the global cook counter, already in the thousands when a node spawns - so
without `age` a Gray-Scott kernel starting from uniform B = 0 sits on a fixed
point forever.

A kernel containing any offset read gets an RGBA32F state bank; one without
keeps RGBA16F, since 16F drifts visibly within seconds for anything that
integrates but is exact enough for trails.

Two pre-existing bugs surfaced, neither introduced here:
- `res` and `aspect` were frame-domain, so `d = 1.0 / res` was hoisted into
  the CPU prologue evaluator, which does not know `res` - it evaluated to 0,
  and every kernel that measured a texel got a texel size of zero.
- a hoisted vec2/3/4 was uploaded with glUniform1f, leaving every lane past
  the first at zero. The pixel partition now hoists scalars only.

Verified by INFINITE_FIELDPIXELTEST assertions 19-27, including a diffusion
test that fails if the fetch coordinate is ever dropped. /run-infinite-hygiene
passes except GROUPTEST, which fails identically on clean main.

parsed_message.description: add FieldSynthNode, FieldPrimitiveNode, and device catalog assets (steps 19-21)
parsed_message.body:
Step 19: FieldSampleNode ("Field Effect") becomes audio-effects-only -
note input removed, audio input moved to slot 0, frame-domain declared
outputs now emit real synthetic Assign IR and alias the RMS modulator.
Step 20: FieldPrimitiveNode, a pure from-scratch geometry generator
(Circle/Spiral/Grid Lattice/Fibonacci Sphere/Helix presets) decoupled
from FieldElementNode's old no-input fallback mode.
Step 21: FieldSynthNode, a polyphonic Field-kernel synth with per-voice
SampleVM state, voice stealing, and FM Bell/Subtractive Saw/Karplus-Strong/
Dual Oscillator Pad presets.
PinTable gains Field::gLiveCableDisconnector: dropping a declared pin

same explicit index) by reserving kFieldDeclaredParamBase=50 for
declared params, separate from native controls' gParamCounter range.

an unexpectedly-unblocked cross-connection, rewrites FIELDPINNODETEST's

registration in Info.plist.in and the Windows .rc), the Field language

parsed_message.title: Field step 18: device faceplate polish for Field node bodies
parsed_message.description: Field step 18: device faceplate polish for Field node bodies
parsed_message.body:
Regrids the four Field*Params compact bodies (element/pixel/sample/graph)
onto AudioKnobRow per node-ui-pillars, adds inline live previews to Pixel
(96x96 texture) and Sample (existing scope call) node bodies, and folds
DrawFieldDeviceControls' preset/device bar into each floating Field editor
window so a device can be switched without closing the editor.
AudioKnobRow (and BeginFieldKnobGrid/DrawFieldParamKnobGrid, which sit on
top of it) previously assumed a live ImGui frame; used under
gParamRegisterOnly - as the four Field bodies now are, and as
RunFieldParamTest exercises before ImGui has a context at all - its
constructor and Knob/Checkbox/End() crashed on a null ImGui window. Fixed
by mirroring the early-return-before-any-ImGui-call convention ModKnob/
ModCheckbox/RegisterDiscreteParam already use.
Also fixes a real staleness bug the new preset bar would otherwise trigger:
each editor window's `editBuf` only refreshed on a pointer switch, so
loading a device from inside the editor and clicking Apply would silently
overwrite it with the stale buffer. Tracks lastKnownCode per window instead.
audit_node_params.py never recognized AudioKnobRow::Checkbox (used by ~30
existing node bodies before this change, including Field's new rows) as a
modulatable widget - fixed so docs/node_param_audit.md reports it correctly.
WTDRAGTEST/AUDIOLIFECYCLETEST/AUDIORECOVERYTEST/PLUGINDRAGTEST failures
reproduce identically with this step's changes stashed out (no real audio
device or VST plugins in this sandbox, WTDRAG flaky); baselined in
known-test-failures.txt.

parsed_message.title: Field step 17: .infdev portable device file format
parsed_message.description: Field step 17: .infdev portable device file format
parsed_message.body:
Adds Field::DeviceFile (src/core/field/FieldDevice.h/.cpp) as a pure
serialization type plus SaveToInfdevFile/LoadFromInfdevFile file I/O
wrappers, using the vendored nlohmann::json. Each Field node type
(FieldElementNode, FieldPixelNode, FieldSampleNode, FieldGraphNode,
FormulaNode) gets ToDeviceFile()/LoadDeviceFile() to round-trip its
code, ParamTable values (by name), and a small set of domain-specific
nodeSettings, ending in the same Apply()/compile call LoadPreset(int)
already uses so a bad file keeps the last-working program via
LastError().
Adds Platform::OpenDeviceDialog()/SaveDeviceDialog() on both macOS
(Platform.mm) and Windows (PlatformWin.cpp), a ".infdev" branch in the
drag-and-drop dispatch gated on domain match, and per-node UI: a
combined factory+user devices dropdown (scanned from
AppPaths::AppSupportDir()+"/Devices/<domain>/", cached not rescanned
every frame) plus Save/Export/Import buttons, wired through the
existing deferred-popup and gDropdown idioms with node-index (not raw
pointer) capture for cross-frame lifetime safety.
Adds the INFINITE_FIELDDEVICETEST harness (5 assertions: JSON
round-trip, file I/O round-trip, undeclared-param-name ignored,
malformed code keeps last-working program + LastError(), mismatched-
domain drop is a no-op) - all passing. FIELDPIXELTEST's pre-existing
"If Lowering" failure (unrelated - confirmed via diff that this step
never touches FieldParse/FieldIR) is now baselined in
known-test-failures.txt.

parsed_message.title: Field step 16: FieldGraphNode "Unpack to Canvas"
parsed_message.description: Field step 16: FieldGraphNode "Unpack to Canvas"
parsed_message.body:
Adds an "Unpack to Canvas" button next to Regenerate on FieldGraphNode
(enabled when encapsulated and mMountedIndices is non-empty). Clicking it
flips encapsulated to false, reveals every mounted child on the canvas,
lays them out left-to-right by topological depth (Field::ComputeEmitDepths,
new in FieldGraphKernel) and top-to-bottom within a depth using the
existing auto-place width classification (now shared as
IsWideAutoPlaceType instead of duplicated), and wraps the revealed cluster
in a new GroupNode. Follows the doc's trap-T14 deferred-mutation shape:
a phase-1 flag armed by the button click, phase-2 polls real
ed::GetNodeSize() each frame (range-checked per INFINITE_SAMPLERDRAGTEST's
existing pattern) until every revealed node's measured size is valid, then
finalizes the layout and spawns the group.
Per the plan doc's corrected §4.3 finding: the operation never touches
mBoundaryOutput, never calls Regenerate(), and never replaces the
FieldGraphNode itself, so an outer cable wired to its boundary output pin
needs zero reconnection - RunFieldGraphRegenerate's own boundary-detach
code already resolves that cable's real target as the FieldGraphNode
instance, not the terminal. INFINITE_FIELDGRAPHUNPACKTEST's assertion 4
asserts this directly rather than assuming it.
Along the way, found and fixed a real pre-existing gap the unpack-then-undo
test is the first path to exercise: FieldGraphNode::VisitParams restored
mOwnership from ownershipText on load/undo/redo but never rebuilt the
derived mMountedIndices cache, so the per-frame hiddenFromCanvas sync loop
had nothing to iterate after a reload - a child stayed visible forever
after undoing back to encapsulated == true. Fixed by rebuilding
mMountedIndices alongside mOwnership in that same branch.
New FIELDGRAPHUNPACKTEST fixture covers: no-op on an empty mMountedIndices,
correct encapsulated/hidden/group-membership state, non-overlapping layout,
topological x-ordering across 3 depths, boundary-cable identity
preservation, and one-step undo/redo correctness.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

parsed_message.title: Field step 15: FieldGraphNode encapsulation (Instrument Mode) - implementation
parsed_message.description: Field step 15: FieldGraphNode encapsulation (Instrument Mode) - implementation
parsed_message.body:
Regenerating a FieldGraphNode now mounts its emitted children as real
gNodes entries hidden from the canvas (GraphNode::hiddenFromCanvas) rather
than spawning them visibly - they still cook, register params, and count
toward audio topology every frame via a new VirtualGraphHost (mirrors
MainGraphHost, kept separate per the doc's anti-sharing trap). A param
declared as a direct pass-through to a mounted child's own param
(set(handle, "name", declaredParam)) is tracked via SetSpec::sourceParamName
and forwarded every frame through FieldGraphNode::PushLiveParams, without a
full Regenerate(). Boundary output preview: FieldGraphNode::TerminalIndices()
derives the graph's unconsumed emit()-ed nodes, and the node body reuses
DrawPreview for whichever terminal has a texture. Encapsulated defaults to
true for new nodes but false for a patch saved before this field existed
(ApplyPatchData forces it before LoadParams runs, since ParamVisitor leaves
an absent key's field untouched).
Adds INFINITE_FIELDGRAPHENCAPTEST (5 assertions) and
INFINITE_FIELDGRAPHLIVEPARAMTEST (3 assertions) per the step's exit
criterion; both pass. FIELDGRAPHTEST's existing segfault, cable-logic-
sweep's NOTEFANOUTTEST no-verdict at its default frame budget, and
run-infinite-hygiene's AUDIOLIFECYCLETEST/AUDIORECOVERYTEST/PLUGINDRAGTEST
failures are all confirmed pre-existing against the pre-step-15 baseline
(no real audio device or VST plugins in this sandbox), not regressions.
Out of scope for this step (flagged, not built): the audio-terminal inline
waveform preview (doc §5.3.1), image/audio/geometry-typed boundary input
pins (§5.2), routing a live-forwarded param through its target's own
ParamRef/ParamMailbox instead of a raw field write (§4.2's stated gap), and
boundary-pin cable-identity bookkeeping (§5.4).

parsed_message.description: Field step 13: dynamic pins Phase 2b - implementation
parsed_message.body:

three Field node types (Element, Sample, Pixel): PinTable-backed compacted
output layering (native -> toggle -> declared), a shared ReconcileFieldPins
helper giving real diff-based cable-orphan refusal (keep-last-working-program
discipline), save/load + undo + copy/paste round-trip of declared pin shape,
and FieldPixelNode's declared `input image` pins routed through the real
InputCountFor/CableFor chains in main.cpp. A Field::gLiveCableChecker function
pointer bridges the cross-translation-unit gap so each node's Apply() (in its
own .cpp) can query main.cpp's anonymous-namespace gLinks cache.

pending runtime-value plumbing, deferred to a follow-up step - see step-13
agent notes. FieldPixelNode's DeclOutput/BackendRegister's sample-domain
equivalent still emit no runtime read/write for a declared output's value;
this step is structural-only (pin count/labels/refusal/save-format), by
design.
