parsed_message.title: Field step 12: dynamic pins Phase 2a - implementation
parsed_message.description: Field step 12: dynamic pins Phase 2a - implementation
parsed_message.body:
Implements docs/plans/field/step-12-dynamic-pins-ir.md's compiler/IR layer
for `output <domain> <type> <name> = <expr>` and `input <domain> <type>
<name>` declarations.
Shared-IR path (Element/Pixel): FieldAst.h gains AstDeclOutput/AstDeclInput,
FieldLex.cpp adds the two keywords, FieldParse.cpp parses the grammar, and
FieldIR.cpp lowers both statements into ElementIRProgram/PixelIRProgram's
new declaredOutputs/declaredInputs vectors, running the S5.3 domain-join
check (expression domain must not be finer than the declared pin domain)
and the S5.8 refusal table (reserved names, duplicates, graph-domain
declarations, the 16-pin ceiling, and each structural type's one legal
domain: geometry->element, audio->sample, image->pixel). `geometry` inputs
support bounded dotted-field access (.P/.N/.uv/.Cd) via a compile-time-only
IR shape with no downstream codegen consumer yet (later work).
Sample-domain path: per the doc's S1.6, BackendRegister.cpp/SampleProgram.h
implement the identical grammar independently of FieldIR.h, since the
sample backend does not share the typed IR with Element/Pixel. A
frame-domain output must be exactly reduce.rms(in, loHz, hiHz); inputs are
collected but deliberately not bound into scope, so referencing one fails
loudly with "used before assignment" rather than resolving to garbage.
PinTable (new): a near-verbatim copy of ParamTable's append-only, name-
keyed, never-reused-id scheme, with S5.4's deliberate difference - a
type/domain/direction change retires the old id and mints a new one rather
than updating in place. Reconcile() is purely a discoverability pass (never
refuses, never touches cable state); the accept/refuse decision belongs to
step 13/14's Apply().
Adds INFINITE_FIELDPINDECLTEST (src/main.cpp), a compiler-level harness
covering every S5.1/S5.8 wrong/right/refusal row, both backend paths, and
PinTable's idempotence/rename/retire-and-remint/serialization behavior, and
registers it in the hygiene driver's TIER1_CHECKS. Purely additive: full
FIELDTEST corpus stays 170/170, and FIELDELEMENTTEST/FIELDPARAMTEST/
FIELDSTATETEST/FIELDTRANSFERTEST/FIELDSAMPLETEST/FIELDPINSTEST/
FIELDGRAPHRATETEST/FIELDGRAPHUNDOTEST/FIELDGRAPHBLASTTEST all pass
unchanged.
Two pre-existing bugs found and left untouched (confirmed via git-stash
bisection against this branch's unmodified merge base): INFINITE_FIELDGRAPHTEST
segfaults, and FIELDPIXELTEST's Assertion 5 (If Lowering) fails - both
reproduce identically with none of this step's changes applied.

for all four Field node types, each via a purely C++-hardcoded,
append-only menu toggle - zero IR change, zero domain-inference change.

  pre-existing ModulatorInputSlot binding's output index to 0 on every

  Regenerate() (PollTriggerEdge), entirely separate from
  emit()/connect()/set()/place().

All four toggles refuse to turn off while a live cable is attached
(cable-orphaning refusal policy), surfaced via a per-node transient
`pinRefusal` string.

Also fixes a real bug caught while writing the new self-test: both
FieldElementNode::ModulatorOutput and FieldSampleNode::ModulatorOutput
returned a live IModulator* for index 1 unconditionally, ignoring the
enabling bool - so a "hidden" pin (OutputCount()==1) could still be

ordering for all four node types; cable-orphaning refusal detection;

proving the bool defaults false and the pin shape reverts. Registered
in run-infinite-hygiene's TIER1_CHECKS.

cables only go into 3D nodes" rule (src/main.cpp) computes srcGeometry
etc. as a whole-node dynamic_cast, not scoped to the specific output
index being connected from - so FieldElementNode's new "publish"
output (index 1) is wrongly rejected by any ModulatorInputSlot
destination, because the node is always an IGeometrySource via its
index-0 output. This is core connection-compatibility logic shared by
the whole cable system; fixing it is out of scope for this step. Left
documented in FIELDPINSTEST with a self-verifying check so the note

Field node UX pass: generator modes, live previews, auto-layout, pin fixes

- Graph domain: allow a fresh local to shadow a name reserved by a
  different domain (fixes `for (i = ...)` matching the canonical doc
  example), while still refusing assignment to a same-domain builtin.
- FieldPixel: unconnected src no longer forces alpha to 0, which was
  making every default preset render fully transparent (root cause of
  the black preview/thumbnail).
- FieldGraphNode: hide its vestigial output pin/preview (meta-node, no
  picture to show); auto-layout newly spawned nodes left-to-right by
  call site when the kernel never calls place().
- FieldElement: generate a synthetic point set when nothing is wired
  into its input, so it can act as a source instead of only a modifier.
- Live previews wired into each Field editor window: geometry viewport
  (Element), rendered image (Pixel), waveform scope (Sample).
- FieldElementNode and FieldPixelNode never had their input pins
  registered in InputCountFor/CableFor, so neither could actually be
  wired despite declaring a real input slot; FieldPixelNode's `src`
  input is upgraded from a bare INode* to an ImageCable so it cooks its
  upstream node before sampling it, matching every other image input.

Field step 9: sample domain (register-machine kernel, per-sample per-voice)

Adds FieldSampleNode: a Field kernel compiled to branchless register-machine
bytecode (BackendRegister.cpp) and run once per audio sample per voice on
the real-time audio thread (SampleRuntime.h interpreter,
AudioFieldSampleNode). Dedicated compiler rather than a reuse of FieldIR's
typed IR, since the sample domain's target - straight-line bytecode with no
runtime jumps - is a different shape than the GLSL-shaped IR Element/Pixel
share.

Key decisions (full writeup in docs/plans/field/step-09-notes.md):
- if/else compiles to branchless Select via SSA-style scope merging; for
  loops are compile-time-unrolled (constant bounds only, cap 64).
- state cells live per-voice in AudioFieldSampleNode, not in SampleProgram
  itself (avoids use-after-free on program retirement); (name,type)
  transplant on hot-reload is resolved on the main thread against a
  retained copy of the last compiled program.
- any NoteOn (idle or stolen voice) resets that voice's state - no
  legato exception, unlike Envelope::ResetLevel.
- reduce.rms(in, loHz, hiHz) requires the literal 'in' argument and
  compile-time constant band edges; it runs once per block directly on the
  raw input buffer (ReduceRmsBandLimited is a batch function, not
  per-sample) and publishes through the existing MeterRing.
- once-per-block NaN/inf sweep with state reset + fault counter, ±4.0
  output clamp, denormal flush on state write-back, 128-param hard cap as
  a compile error.
- ParamTable's persisted id and the sample domain's dense mailboxId are
  kept as two separate spaces, resolved by name every frame rather than by
  assumed iteration order.

Wired into main.cpp (Synths category, matching Oscillator/Equation/Sampler),
with an INFINITE_FIELDSAMPLETEST fixture (9 sections: compile+execution,
state transplant, param smoothing, voice reset, 129-param and non-constant
loop-bound refusals, NaN recovery, reduce.rms publish, zero allocation) and
two new AUDIOPARAMSWEEPTEST baseline entries for the node's structural
maxVoices and ParamTable's internal bookkeeping field.

All existing Field fixtures (FIELDTEST, FIELDELEMENTTEST, FIELDPARAMTEST,
FIELDSTATETEST, FIELDPIXELTEST, FIELDTRANSFERTEST) and the full hygiene
suite still pass; no new regressions beyond the 3 pre-existing
environment-only failures (AUDIOLIFECYCLETEST, AUDIORECOVERYTEST,

parsed_message.title: Field step 8: domain transfer operators (reduce/map/broadcast/resample/downsample)
parsed_message.description: Field step 8: domain transfer operators (reduce/map/broadcast/resample/downsample)
parsed_message.body:
Implements the five transfer operators specified in
docs/plans/field/step-08-transfer-operators.md: reduce (element/sample ->
frame), map (bounded unroll with per-instance state), broadcast (implicit
only, explicit calls refused), resample (legal domain crossings only), and
downsample (state-cell hold + gated write, desugared in both the element
bytecode and pixel GLSL backends).
Fixed a real bug surfaced by INFINITE_FIELDTRANSFERTEST SECTION 5: both
map-lowering implementations (element in FieldIR.cpp's LowerMapStatement,
and the inline pixel-backend block) pre-register N per-instance state cells
into scope, then re-lowered the body's original (renamed) `state` decl
statement through the generic statement lowering path — which re-declared
the same name into a scope that already had it, failing with "duplicate
declaration". Fix: skip AstKind::DeclState statements in the per-instance
unroll loop in both places, since they're already registered.
All Field fixtures pass (FIELDTEST, FIELDELEMENTTEST, FIELDPARAMTEST,
FIELDSTATETEST, FIELDPIXELTEST, FIELDTRANSFERTEST) and the full hygiene gate
is clean except for 4 pre-existing environment failures unrelated to Field
(RECEXPORTTEST/AUDIOLIFECYCLETEST/AUDIORECOVERYTEST: no real audio device in
this sandbox; PLUGINDRAGTEST: plugin scan environment).
The sample half of reduce is deliberately deferred to step 9, which lands
the audio-thread register machine reduce needs to run inside.

parsed_message.raw:
Field step 7 fixes: pixel kernels that use params, vectors, bools or state now work

The step-7 fixture passed 12/12 while most real kernels were rejected --
it grepped the emitted source for the shape of the right answer instead of
compiling representative kernels. Fixes, each with a new assertion:

- params: the body referenced fld_v_<name> while the declaration emitted
  fld_p_<name>, so every kernel declaring a param failed to link.
- bools: GlslTypeString returned "bool", but every comparison / ! / && this
  backend emits produces a 0.0-or-1.0 float and GLSL has no implicit
  bool<->float conversion. Bool now lowers to float.
- broadcast: clamp(col, 0.0, 1.0), lerp(vec3, vec3, float) and friends had no
  matching fld_ overload. Scalar args are now promoted to the call's result
  rank at emission, rather than adding ~15 mixed-rank helper overloads.
- if: was emitting the arithmetic mix with a 0.0/1.0 selector, which turns an
  inf/NaN in the unselected branch into NaN in the result. Now uses the
  bool-selector overload.
- col/alpha/xy/res/aspect are entry-valued, so the canonical filter shape
  `y = col.r * 2.0` / `col = ...` is no longer rejected as a delay-free cycle.
- state kernels wrote state to the visible output. A second pass driven by a
  fld_outMode uniform now renders picture into mOut; the ping-pong pair holds
  state only, and swaps once after both passes.
- presets: 3 of 4 did not parse (missing [min, max] range syntax).
- Apply now compiles into locals and commits only after link, so a failed
  edit keeps the last working program.
- FieldPixelNode.cpp / PixelState.cpp included <OpenGL/gl3.h> directly,
  which breaks the Windows build; both now use the src/core/gl3.h shim.
- PixelState::BindReadUnits takes the cached uniform location instead of
  calling glGetUniformLocation every cook.

Known and deferred: lineToIrNode is populated but unused, so driver-line ->
source-span mapping is unimplemented; no GL_MAX_TEXTURE_IMAGE_UNITS /
GL_MAX_FRAGMENT_UNIFORM_COMPONENTS queries; EmitNode still has silent 0.0
fallbacks; vec2/3/4 state cells break the cell->channel packing.

Verified: FIELDPIXELTEST 18/18, FIELDTEST section A 170/170,
FIELDELEMENTTEST / FIELDPARAMTEST / FIELDSTATETEST OK, tier 1 16/16.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

parsed_message.title: Slicer UI: crossthrough checkbox, attack slider, six-row grid
parsed_message.description: Slicer UI: crossthrough checkbox, attack slider, six-row grid
parsed_message.body:
Reorders the body into six two-column rows so the envelope pair
(attack | decay) sits adjacent and `volume` no longer takes a ragged
full-width row. Reordering the float sliders shifts modulation pin
ordinals, which is free only because this node has not shipped yet.
The crossthrough toggle is a ModCheckbox, not an AudioToggleButton:
ModCheckbox registers a discrete param, so the toggle is modulatable and
performance-matrix assignable, and it passes GetFrameHeight() to
DrawDiscreteParamPin so its modulation dot is centred with no per-node
offset code (P2). Discrete params come from kDiscreteParamBase and are
keyed by label hash, so adding it renumbers no float pin. It sits in the
left cell of row 6 with the right cell deliberately spare - eleven
controls is odd, and the far edge of the last row is P6's sanctioned
position for the one hole.
decay's detent now reads "hold" rather than "inf", which is what it
actually does now that it owns only the envelope.
Extends RunSlicerFixture with three new sections: crossthrough off
confines a slice to its own next onset (peak after the boundary
< 1e-4 - the assertion the whole change exists for), crossthrough on is
its exact complement, and a 50 ms attack ramps in against a 0 ms control
render. The attack section synthesises its own constant-amplitude sine:
the existing fixture WAV's bursts are exp(-t*200) enveloped, so a 50 ms
attack measured against them would be a false FAIL.
No draw-side playhead clamp: the audio-side confinement makes the
drawing correct on its own, and a clamp would hide a voice that is
really still advancing.

parsed_message.title: Slicer: split Voice::infinite into noDecay + confine, add attack
parsed_message.description: Slicer: split Voice::infinite into noDecay + confine, add attack
parsed_message.body:
Voice::infinite conflated three separate concerns - the amplitude
envelope, the slice boundary, and note-off eligibility. Split it into
`noDecay` (envelope only: hold at full level) and `confine` (boundary
only: stop at this slice's next onset), latched per voice at note-on
from the new `crossthrough` param. Note-off stays keyed to noDecay.
Also fixes a live bug: StartVoice read the *smoothed* mailbox value to
make the *discrete* no-decay detent decision, so a note-on landing a few
ms after the user released the decay slider at the top of its throw saw
a mid-ramp value and silently started a decaying voice. Detents now read
the plain atomics (which also stops the extra out-of-phase smoother
advance per note-on).
New `attack` param (0..500 ms) EXTENDS the hidden 2 ms de-click ramp
rather than stacking a second envelope on it - one raised cosine of
max(2 ms, attack) - so at attack = 0 the output is bit-identical to
before. `crossthrough` is a plain atomic, not a mailbox param: a bool
has no ramp.
ReloadFromPath saves/restores both new params so copy/paste keeps them.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
parsed_message.raw:
Slicer: split Voice::infinite into noDecay + confine, add attack

Voice::infinite conflated three separate concerns - the amplitude
envelope, the slice boundary, and note-off eligibility. Split it into
`noDecay` (envelope only: hold at full level) and `confine` (boundary
only: stop at this slice's next onset), latched per voice at note-on
from the new `crossthrough` param. Note-off stays keyed to noDecay.

Also fixes a live bug: StartVoice read the *smoothed* mailbox value to
make the *discrete* no-decay detent decision, so a note-on landing a few
ms after the user released the decay slider at the top of its throw saw
a mid-ramp value and silently started a decaying voice. Detents now read
the plain atomics (which also stops the extra out-of-phase smoother
advance per note-on).

New `attack` param (0..500 ms) EXTENDS the hidden 2 ms de-click ramp
rather than stacking a second envelope on it - one raised cosine of
max(2 ms, attack) - so at attack = 0 the output is bit-identical to
before. `crossthrough` is a plain atomic, not a mailbox param: a bool
has no ramp.

ReloadFromPath saves/restores both new params so copy/paste keeps them.

parsed_message.title: Slicer node: sample chopping synth with onset and grid modes
parsed_message.description: Slicer node: sample chopping synth with onset and grid modes
parsed_message.body:
Loads or records a sample, chops it at detected transients or on the
transport grid, and plays each slice chromatically from MIDI note 36.
Onset detection runs on a worker thread and is relaunched only by the
sensitivity control; `onsets` is a main-thread top-N-by-strength prune
of the cached candidate list and slice by / division recompute
boundaries with no analysis at all. Slice boundaries reach the audio
thread as plain atomics (published count-last with release ordering)
rather than smoothed mailbox params. Eight note voices with a 2 ms
raised-cosine steal crossfade carried by ghost slots, so a steal needs
no allocation and no lock.
Markers are drag-editable in onsets mode and persist in the patch, so
a reload restores hand-placed boundaries instead of re-detecting.

parsed_message.title: Slicer: clean-room onset detection DSP
parsed_message.description: Slicer: clean-room onset detection DSP
parsed_message.body:
Log-magnitude spectral flux with a SuperFlux 3-bin max-filtered
reference frame and a Dixon-style adaptive peak picker, implemented
from the primary literature (cited in the header). Post-processing:
silence gate, backtrack to the preceding energy minimum, zero-crossing
snap, minimum inter-onset interval, hard slice cap.
Frames are centred (zero-padded at both ends) so an ODF frame index
converts directly to a sample position; an un-centred framing reports
onsets up to fftSize/2 early, landing them in the silence ahead of the
attack where the silence gate then rejects them outright.

parsed_message.title: Video node: add modulatable start/end trim positions
parsed_message.description: Video node: add modulatable start/end trim positions
parsed_message.body:
Adds trimStart/trimEnd params that set the in/out playback window for
the video Source node, affecting both video and audio. trimEnd <= 0.0
means "unset - use full duration", matching the existing sentinel
convention already used for mDuration.
Both the video-side position wrap (loop fmod / non-loop clamp) and the
audio thread's independent free-running read cursor are re-anchored to
the effective [trimStart, trimEnd] window instead of [0, duration],
with a degenerate/inverted-range guard so a modulated start >= end
falls back to the full clip rather than misbehaving. The audio side
gets its own copy of the trim window (pushed through the existing
ParamMailbox, like speed/volume) rather than relying solely on the
coarser ~250ms discontinuity snap, so short trim windows stay in sync.
Existing negative-speed reverse playback and the Windows loop-freeze
fix are untouched - VIDEOSPEEDTEST and VIDEOLOOPWRAPTEST both still
pass with defaults.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

parsed_message.title: Fix viewport panel losing its node cards after Undo/Redo
parsed_message.description: Fix viewport panel losing its node cards after Undo/Redo
parsed_message.body:
Undo/Redo rebuild the graph via ApplyPatchData, which respawns every
node with a fresh index. gViewportPanelNodes is session-only UI state
(not part of Patch::Data), so it was left holding stale indices after
any Undo/Redo, silently dropping or mis-targeting docked viewport
cards. ApplyPatchData now optionally hands back its old->new index
remap, and Undo/Redo use it to carry gViewportPanelNodes across.

parsed_message.title: Windows: fix video loop freezing after one play-through
parsed_message.description: Windows: fix video loop freezing after one play-through
parsed_message.body:
VideoSourceNode's loop-wrap logic only runs when mDuration > 0, but
MediaWin.cpp's single MF_PD_DURATION query could silently leave
durationSeconds at 0.0 for some fragmented/streamed MP4/MOV containers,
so playback clamped to end-of-file instead of wrapping regardless of
the loop flag.
Add two fallbacks in VideoThreadMain: a presentation-descriptor
duration query (a genuinely different MF API path), then a last-resort
seek-to-far-past-EOF probe that reads back the last real timestamp.
A truly unbounded/live source still correctly ends up with
durationSeconds == 0 ("unknown"), so non-loopable sources aren't
affected.
Also adds an additive VIDEOLOOPWRAPTEST assertion in the video speed
self-test that checks Position() actually wraps into [0, Duration())
after looping, since the existing FrameUpdateCount checks only prove
frames keep decoding, not that the position wrapped.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add TouchDesigner-style glTF/GLB drag-and-drop model import

Dropping a .glb or loose .gltf (+ .bin/textures) onto the canvas now
auto-spawns a fully wired Model 3D + Material + one Image Source per
present texture map (albedo/roughness/metallic/normal/ao/emission), with
zero manual cabling - reusing the existing node types rather than adding
new ones.

- Vendor cgltf (external/cgltf/cgltf.h) the same way stb is vendored.
- Platform::LoadImageRGBAFromMemory (Platform.mm + MediaDecodeWin.cpp)
  decodes in-memory image bytes (embedded/base64 glTF textures) with the
  same RGBA8/flip convention as the existing file-path loader. Only the
  macOS side could be built/tested here; the Windows body mirrors it
  byte-for-byte but is unverified on this machine.
- New src/core/GltfImport.{h,cpp}: parses the first mesh/primitive/material
  via cgltf, resolves texture maps (embedded bufferView, base64 data-URI,
  or external file), and channel-splits a combined metallicRoughness
  texture into two independent roughness/metallic images (the shader has
  no combined-texture concept). Cached via AssetCache like every other
  decoder in this codebase.
- ModelSourceNode::Load and ImageSourceNode::Load extension/scheme-sniff
  into this path; ImageSourceNode gains LoadFromDecoded() plus a
  "gltf://<path>#<slot>" pseudo-path so save/load and undo/redo reconstruct
  glTF-derived textures with no special-casing elsewhere.
- main.cpp's drop handler gets its own kGltfExt branch (checked before
  kModelExt): fresh drop spawns+wires the whole rig in one undo step;
  dropping onto an existing Model 3D reloads in place instead of
  duplicating the rig.
- Fixes a latent use-after-free this feature's multi-node spawn exposed:
  SpawnNode's returned GraphNode* points into gNodes (a std::vector), so
  holding one across a later SpawnNode call (growing the vector) could
  dangle. Now captures the stable node index and re-resolves via
  FindNodeByIndex as needed.
- Adds an INFINITE_GLTFDROPTEST self-test fixture driving the real drop
  handler via gDroppedFiles/gDropPos (same queue a real OS drop
  populates) to verify fresh drop wiring, undo/redo, save/reload
  round-trip, drop-onto-existing-node, textureless glTF, loose .gltf, and
  the metallicRoughness channel split - all 41 checks pass.

parsed_message.title: Windows: fix file-audio muxing never reaching the recorded movie
parsed_message.description: Windows: fix file-audio muxing never reaching the recorded movie
bullets: 32000 Hz was treated as a standard AAC output rate. The Windows AAC
The float input media type omitted MF_MT_AUDIO_CHANNEL_MASK, which the
RecorderStop called Flush on the audio stream immediately before
parsed_message.body:
Recording with an Audio File node cabled into Output produced a
video-only MP4 and the status "audio muxing skipped: configuring audio
encoder failed (0xC00D36B2)". 0xC00D36B2 is MF_E_INVALIDREQUEST:
IMFSinkWriter::AddStream is only legal before BeginWriting, and the
file-audio path added its stream from RecorderStop, long after. macOS
hit and fixed the identical bug in Platform.mm (AVAssetWriter refuses
addInput: after startWriting); Windows never got the same fix.
Both audio modes now add their stream in RecorderStart, before
BeginWriting - the file is decoded there anyway, so its rate and channel
count are known. Only the sample writing stays at Stop, where the real
video duration is available. If the audio stream can't be configured the
writer is rebuilt video-only rather than left carrying a typeless stream
that would fail BeginWriting outright, and the Output node now says
"recording (no audio: ...)" instead of claiming audio it isn't getting.
Three further defects in the same path, found while confirming the
above:
encoder accepts only 44100 or 48000, so a 32k source would still have
failed after the ordering fix. It now falls back to 48k like every
other non-standard rate.
resampler the sink writer inserts lists as required - a documented
cause of MF_E_INVALIDMEDIATYPE from SetInputMediaType.
Finalize. Flush discards a stream's queued samples rather than pushing
them out, so it could have thrown away the track that had just been
written. Finalize already drains every stream.
Throttling is also disabled on the sink writer: WriteFileAudioTrack
writes a whole track in one burst at Stop, which is the pattern
throttling exists to stall, and by then the video stream is complete.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
parsed_message.raw:
Windows: fix file-audio muxing never reaching the recorded movie

Recording with an Audio File node cabled into Output produced a
video-only MP4 and the status "audio muxing skipped: configuring audio
encoder failed (0xC00D36B2)". 0xC00D36B2 is MF_E_INVALIDREQUEST:
IMFSinkWriter::AddStream is only legal before BeginWriting, and the
file-audio path added its stream from RecorderStop, long after. macOS
hit and fixed the identical bug in Platform.mm (AVAssetWriter refuses
addInput: after startWriting); Windows never got the same fix.

Both audio modes now add their stream in RecorderStart, before
BeginWriting - the file is decoded there anyway, so its rate and channel
count are known. Only the sample writing stays at Stop, where the real
video duration is available. If the audio stream can't be configured the
writer is rebuilt video-only rather than left carrying a typeless stream
that would fail BeginWriting outright, and the Output node now says
"recording (no audio: ...)" instead of claiming audio it isn't getting.

Three further defects in the same path, found while confirming the
above:

- 32000 Hz was treated as a standard AAC output rate. The Windows AAC
  encoder accepts only 44100 or 48000, so a 32k source would still have
  failed after the ordering fix. It now falls back to 48k like every
  other non-standard rate.
- The float input media type omitted MF_MT_AUDIO_CHANNEL_MASK, which the
  resampler the sink writer inserts lists as required - a documented
  cause of MF_E_INVALIDMEDIATYPE from SetInputMediaType.
- RecorderStop called Flush on the audio stream immediately before
  Finalize. Flush discards a stream's queued samples rather than pushing
  them out, so it could have thrown away the track that had just been
  written. Finalize already drains every stream.

Throttling is also disabled on the sink writer: WriteFileAudioTrack
writes a whole track in one burst at Stop, which is the pattern
throttling exists to stall, and by then the video stream is complete.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

parsed_message.title: Fix Global Scale toggle tooltip corrupting ImGui state mid-node-loop; Delay/Reverb trailing checkbox row spacing
parsed_message.description: Fix Global Scale toggle tooltip corrupting ImGui state mid-node-loop; Delay/Reverb trailing checkbox row spacing
parsed_message.body:
GlobalScaleToggle() drew its tooltip via ed::SetItemTooltip while nested
inside a per-node ed::Begin()/ed::End() pair - not a safe place for the
ed::Suspend()/Resume() that tooltip rendering needs (that pairing is only
ever used once, after the whole node-draw loop, for the popups/minimap/
perf-matrix overlay block). Corrupted ImGui's window/ID state for the rest
of the frame and made the app's top toolbar disappear while hovering the
icon. Now the hover just records intent; the actual tooltip draws later
from the existing post-loop suspended block where it's already known safe.
Also gives Delay's sync-checkbox row and Reverb's analog-checkbox row the
same 8px headerRowH gap already used by Pitch Shift/Ring Mod/Flanger/
Phaser/Bitcrush's trailing analog rows, instead of sitting flush against
the knob row above.

parsed_message.title: Audio Filter: remove redundant output-gain knob, fix frozen LFO overlay
parsed_message.description: Audio Filter: remove redundant output-gain knob, fix frozen LFO overlay
parsed_message.body:
Output section drops the "output gain" knob (redundant with the filter's
own gain knob above) and reflows to 4 cells: sync mode + rate on the left,
env then mix (mix stays bottom-right, P4). outputGainDb stays declared and
applied by AudioFilterKernel - this is UI-only, the underlying DSP param
and value are unchanged.
Root-caused the yellow LFO sweep overlay reading as frozen until a knob
was nudged: AudioFilterKernel::ProcessBlock wrote mLfoMeter once per
sample (44.1k+/sec) into a 4096-entry MeterRing, while the visualizer's
ExtraMeterValue readback only drains 4 entries/frame (~240/sec at 60fps).
The ring fills in under 100ms and then MeterRing::Write silently drops
samples, so the ~4096-sample backlog - itself under 100ms of real audio -
took the UI roughly 17 seconds of frames to page through, during which
consecutive entries were microseconds apart and the overlay read as
stuck. Now writes once per block, the same discipline DynamicsKernel's
GR-bar meter already uses, so the ring stays shallow and the overlay
tracks the live LFO immediately.

parsed_message.description: Audio Filter: fix real FPS-drop root cause, add yellow LFO sweep overlay
parsed_message.body:
The visualizer's throttle only limited how often the curve recomputed,
not the per-call cost of AudioFilterDsp::MagnitudeDb's settle-then-measure
simulation at 160 points (~10-15ms/sweep, over one frame budget on its own).
Drag now recomputes at 48 points instead of 160, and the idle throttle
relaxed slightly (0.05s -> 0.08s).
Also stopped the base curve and freq/gain handle from visually sliding
with the LFO sweep - they now stay at the node's real static value, and
the sweep is drawn as a separate yellow overlay curve on top, matching
how the LFO actually modulates the parameter (an indicator, not a move).

parsed_message.description: Note Filter visualizer: collapse to two colors (blue in-scale, grey off)
parsed_message.body:
Previously the key-color function returned 6 distinct colors (Active,
Snapped, OutOfRange, each split by white/black key) - the muted
"Snapped" state made in-range-but-off-scale keys look like a third
tier, and white/black keys never shared a color. The user only
perceives two states, so KeyColor now maps Active to a single blue
(independent of theme it's brighter/more saturated than the resting
grey) and both Snapped and OutOfRange to a single grey, regardless of
whether the key is drawn as a white or black key - key shape already
conveys white/black, color now only conveys scale membership.
KeyState stays a 3-value enum (NoteState still needs the distinction),
only the color mapping and KeyColor's signature (dropped the unused
isWhite parameter) changed. Root tick and lastIn/lastPassed highlight
rings are untouched.

parsed_message.title: Audio Filter: throttle visualizer recompute + LFO-driven output redesign
parsed_message.description: Audio Filter: throttle visualizer recompute + LFO-driven output redesign
parsed_message.body:
Part 1 - FPS fix: DrawAudioFilterVisualizer recomputed all 160 points
of the frequency-response curve via AudioFilterDsp::MagnitudeDb (a
settle-then-measure simulation up to 8000 samples/point) on every
single frame while a handle was being dragged - up to 1.28M simulated
samples/frame. Cap the recompute to ~20Hz while actively dragging
(signature-changed-while-mouse-down heuristic + a time-based throttle)
without touching MagnitudeDb's math, which stays shared/authoritative
with DSPTEST and EQ. The curve still snaps to full resolution the
instant the drag ends.
Checked DrawEqVisualizer for the same anti-pattern: it uses
EqDsp::BandMagnitudeDb, a cheap closed-form biquad evaluation rather
than a simulation, so it doesn't share this cost profile and is left
unchanged.
Part 2 - output section redesign: removed the "cutoff mod" sidechain
input/modAmount entirely (EffectDefs.cpp hasSidechain/sidechainLabel,
kernel's modBuf/modAmount/modActive/extModOctaves machinery, and the
now-dead FILTER CUTOFF MOD TEARDOWN test fixture in main.cpp).
envAmount is repurposed from an audio envelope-follower depth into an
internal free-running/tempo-synced sine LFO depth (same sync/rateDiv/
rate triplet as Chorus/Flanger/Phaser/Tremolo), publishing its live
output via the existing IEffectKernel::ExtraMeter mechanism so the
frequency-response visualizer can animate the cutoff sweep live with a
single atomic read and zero extra MagnitudeDb calls (an octave shift is
just a constant pixel-space translation on the log-frequency axis).
New params are appended (not inserted) so existing patch indices for
type/freq/q/gain/outputGainDb/envAmount are untouched. Output section
is now output gain / env / rate / mix knobs + a sync dropdown, laid out
via row.index reassignment (DrawChorusBody's precedent) so gParamCounter
ordinals for the three pre-existing knobs don't move.
Added an Audio Filter|rateDiv baseline entry (same rateDiv-with-no-sync-
prereq blind spot as Chorus/Flanger/Phaser/Stutter/Tremolo) and explicit
sweep prerequisites pinning envAmount != 0 for sync/rate, since both are
only observable in the kernel's LFO-active path.

state, with everything else greyed out. The Snapped state (in-range but
off-scale) was a vivid gold/amber that was nearly as saturated/bright as
Active, so in-range keys all looked equally lively regardless of scale
membership and the scale itself never visually popped.

unchanged. Active is untouched in both themes.

luminance (indistinguishable "lit" reading), now reads as a flat, cool-
adjacent grey-tan close to OutOfRange (200,205,218) L=205, distinguished

Light theme, black keys:

clearly desaturated relative to the previous vivid amber) and close to

background.

parsed_message.body:

music-note glyph like every other pitch-quantizing note node. When on,
replayed notes snap to Transport::Key()/Scale() via MusicTime::SnapToScale
on note-on only; the matching note-off is emitted for the same snapped
pitch (looked up from the existing mSounding voice map) so a mid-playback
key/scale change can't hang a note. Recording is unaffected - only
playback quantizes. The keyboard visualizer reflects the snapped pitch
for free, since it reads the same mHeldBits the playback path now writes
the resolved pitch into.
Also puts `loop` on a 4-cell AudioKnobRow matching the Record/Play/Stop/

explanation. The window now sizes to 2-4 octaves and centers on the

range still exceeds the window. The readout strip's snprintf now prints
octave numbers (C3..G5) instead of bare pitch-class names.

Notes) for the same root-anchoring bug - both already anchor to C, not
root, so no fix needed there.

parsed_message.title: Fix glide/portamento: preserve pitch smoother on active voice repitch
parsed_message.description: Fix glide/portamento: preserve pitch smoother on active voice repitch
parsed_message.body:
Bug fix: WavetableSynthCore NoteOn was calling SetImmediate() on every
new note (when v.note != note), which snapped the pitch smoother to the
target frequency instantly and defeated the glide parameter entirely.
Now SetImmediate is only called when the voice was previously inactive
(silent), so active voices glide smoothly from old pitch to new.

note-driven (polyphonic) mode — previously it had no audible effect.
Performance: hoist expf() glide coefficient computation out of per-voice
inner loops in EquationNode and WaveTerrainNode. The glide parameter
doesn't change within a single sample, so computing the coefficient once
per sample instead of once per voice per sample avoids redundant
transcendental function calls.

parsed_message.title: Fix note-on click in Oscillator and Wavetable
parsed_message.description: Fix note-on click in Oscillator and Wavetable
bullets: Continuity across an overlapping note-on. Note 1 sounds for 200 ms
Steady-state loudness unchanged: a held 3-note chord's RMS matches
parsed_message.body:
Both nodes share WavetableSynthCore's voice path, whose polyphony
normalisation recounted `active` every sample and applied 1/sqrt(active)
directly. `active` is an integer, so the gain was a step function: any
note-on overlapping a sounding voice - a chord, or just the previous
note's release tail - moved it 1 -> 2 within one sample and snapped the
gain on the ALREADY-SOUNDING voice from 1.0 to 0.7071. That is a -3 dB
discontinuity in the output waveform (-6 dB with Chorder's 1 -> 4), and
the new note's attack cannot mask it because the step lands on the old
voice. It fired again in reverse whenever a tail went idle.
Ramp the gain through a persistent one-pole (15 ms, fixed - this is a
click fix, not a musical control, so it is deliberately not tied to the
glide knob) instead of applying it as a step. Initialised to 1.0 in
PrepareToPlay, not 0.0, or the first note would fade in. Steady state is
unchanged: the smoother settles on the same 1/sqrt(N).
Also make voice stealing click-free. On the all-busy steal path NoteOn
resets the stolen voice's phase and filter state while Envelope::NoteOn
deliberately keeps mLevel, so a fresh waveform was spliced in at the old
note's amplitude. Zero the amp envelope first, via a new explicit
Envelope::ResetLevel() called only from that path - NoteOn()'s no-reset
behaviour is load-bearing for legato and same-note retrigger and must
stay as it is.
Verified by two new DSPTEST checks in RunWavetableFixture:
with a 4 s release, is released, and note 2 arrives while its tail is
still loud. The scan is on the second difference, not the first: a
level step adds to the waveform's own slew, so whether it reads as a
spike in |x[n]-x[n-1]| depends on which way the waveform happened to
be moving - the first-difference version of this check measured the
real -3 dB step as 0.99x the steady slew and passed the broken code.
The second difference has no such cancellation. Reverting the fix
takes this from 1.03x to 32.6x its threshold.
1/sqrt(3) of the same three notes rendered solo and summed, to within
0.01%.

in this worktree, but both fail identically when the main-built binary
is run from the same directory - environmental (no scanned VST3, movie
writer produces no tracks here), not a regression from this change.

note's release tail - moved it 1 -> 2 within one sample and snapped the
gain on the ALREADY-SOUNDING voice from 1.0 to 0.7071. That is a -3 dB
discontinuity in the output waveform (-6 dB with Chorder's 1 -> 4), and
the new note's attack cannot mask it because the step lands on the old
voice. It fired again in reverse whenever a tail went idle.

Ramp the gain through a persistent one-pole (15 ms, fixed - this is a
click fix, not a musical control, so it is deliberately not tied to the
glide knob) instead of applying it as a step. Initialised to 1.0 in
PrepareToPlay, not 0.0, or the first note would fade in. Steady state is
unchanged: the smoother settles on the same 1/sqrt(N).

Also make voice stealing click-free. On the all-busy steal path NoteOn
resets the stolen voice's phase and filter state while Envelope::NoteOn
deliberately keeps mLevel, so a fresh waveform was spliced in at the old
note's amplitude. Zero the amp envelope first, via a new explicit
Envelope::ResetLevel() called only from that path - NoteOn()'s no-reset
behaviour is load-bearing for legato and same-note retrigger and must
stay as it is.

Verified by two new DSPTEST checks in RunWavetableFixture:

- Continuity across an overlapping note-on. Note 1 sounds for 200 ms
  with a 4 s release, is released, and note 2 arrives while its tail is
  still loud. The scan is on the second difference, not the first: a
  level step adds to the waveform's own slew, so whether it reads as a
  spike in |x[n]-x[n-1]| depends on which way the waveform happened to
  be moving - the first-difference version of this check measured the
  real -3 dB step as 0.99x the steady slew and passed the broken code.
  The second difference has no such cancellation. Reverting the fix
  takes this from 1.03x to 32.6x its threshold.

- Steady-state loudness unchanged: a held 3-note chord's RMS matches
  1/sqrt(3) of the same three notes rendered solo and summed, to within
  0.01%.

in this worktree, but both fail identically when the main-built binary
is run from the same directory - environmental (no scanned VST3, movie
writer produces no tracks here), not a regression from this change.

parsed_message.raw:
Fix Poisson Disk scatter tanking frame rate on Distribute Points on Faces

The saturation break was scaled by the requested point count (cap * 30)
instead of being a fixed measure of local saturation, so a high-density
scatter burned up to 30x cap wasted candidate draws every rebuild - each
walking an unordered_map neighbour grid (heap alloc per new cell, hash +
pointer chase per lookup). Above cap ~66k the break was unreachable
entirely (saturationLimit exceeded the 2M candidate hard cap), so those
scatters burned the full budget every frame.

Fixes:
- saturationLimit is now a fixed 1500 consecutive rejects, independent
  of cap, and always well below the maxCandidates backstop.
- The unordered_map neighbour grid is replaced with a flat open-addressed
  table (gridKeys/gridHead) plus an intrusive per-point linked list
  (cellNext), sized off the accepted-point budget with no per-cell heap
  allocation.
- DistributePointsOnFacesNode now scatters once on the source mesh and
  transforms the result into each instance's space, instead of re-running
  the full Poisson search per instance (up to 256x).

Behaviour change: since the termination rule and per-instance seeding
both changed, an already-saved patch using Poisson mode or instancing
will reopen with a different point count/arrangement. This is unavoidable
for a correct fix.

Added a timing self-test (density 300 / minDistance 0.1 on a sphere,
must finish under 10ms) to DISTRIBUTETEST; the existing minDistance,
determinism, and saturation self-tests are unchanged and still pass.

parsed_message.title: Let an offline stepper wait for the Windows decode thread
parsed_message.description: Let an offline stepper wait for the Windows decode thread
parsed_message.body:
Windows CI caught this: RECEXPORTTEST failed with "0 flash onsets" where main
is green. The rec-export self-test decodes the movie it just wrote by stepping
t from 0 to 6s at 4x the clip's frame rate, and that loop is pure CPU - it
finishes in about a millisecond. With decoding synchronous that was fine. With
decoding on its own thread it raced past the decoder, sampled one early frame
720 times, and saw no flashes at all.
The previous commit's mitigation only waited for the *first* frame, which is
why it did not help. What this consumer actually needs is a way to tell "not
decoded yet" from "there is nothing more" - so add it to the facade rather
than bodging the test:
Platform::VideoDecodeIsCatchingUp(handle)
True while the decoder has not yet read as far as the position last requested
through VideoFrameAt. Constant false on macOS, where VideoFrameAt decodes
synchronously and has therefore always caught up by the time it returns - so
the wait loop never executes there and macOS timing is unchanged. The render
thread must never wait on it; holding the previous frame is the whole point.
Getting the predicate right mattered more than adding it. Defining it as
"not at end of stream" livelocks: a stepper finer-grained than the clip's own
frame rate constantly asks for positions that fall between two frames, and no
amount of waiting will ever produce a frame at or before them. It has to be
"the decoder has not read past the target yet" - once it has, the answer is
settled and waiting cannot change it.
Verified by extracting the real text of MediaWin.cpp's video section, compiling
it against a stub Media Foundation surface, and running it under
ThreadSanitizer. TSan is clean. The unpaced-stepper case reproduces the CI
failure exactly - 4 of 120 frames seen without the new query, 120 of 120 with
it - so that arm of the harness discriminates rather than merely passing.
macOS: builds clean, RECEXPORTTEST passes (6.00s, 5 flash onsets, all three
sync assertions), run-infinite-hygiene 62/63 with only the known
PLUGINDRAGTEST scan-cache flake, which passes on rerun and is unrelated.

Decode video on its own thread on Windows, in hardware where possible

The Video node dropped the whole app's frame rate on Windows while playing
smoothly on macOS. Four causes, all on the Windows side:

  * The source reader never set MF_READWRITE_ENABLE_HARDWARE_TRANSFORMS, so
    H.264/HEVC was decoded on the CPU, where macOS gets VideoToolbox.
  * VideoFrameAt opened an MfScope *and* a ComScope per rendered frame -
    MFStartup/CoInitializeEx per frame, on the render thread, for refcounts
    that never reached zero.
  * Every decoded frame allocated and freed a fresh width*height*4 buffer
    (~8MB at 1080p) where macOS reuses one.
  * All of it - including the keyframe seek a loop wrap triggers - ran
    synchronously inside VideoSourceNode::CookIfNeeded.

Decoding now runs on a dedicated thread that keeps four frames ahead of a
position the render thread publishes, mirroring CameraThreadMain in the same
file: it owns the MFStartup/CoInitializeEx pair for the reader's lifetime and
recycles frame buffers instead of reallocating. VideoFrameAt becomes a
non-blocking pick of the newest decoded frame at or before the target.

Observable behaviour is preserved. A false return still means "keep the
previous frame", which CookIfNeeded already handles, and FrameUpdateCount()
still counts only frames that reached the texture, because a frame is popped
from the queue as it is delivered and cannot be delivered twice.

Output stays RGB32, so the software Video Processor MFT and the RGBA swizzle
still run - but on the decode thread, not the render thread. Accepting NV12
and converting in a shader would remove both; that needs VideoSourceNode to
blit through its own RGBA FBO first and is deliberately left for later.

Platform::VideoFrameAt's signature is unchanged, so Platform.mm is untouched
and macOS does not change. The one shared edit is the offline movie-analysis
loop in the rec-export self-test, which now waits a bounded moment for the
first frame - "nothing decoded yet" is a legitimate answer from an
asynchronous decoder at t = 0.

Verification, plainly: macOS builds clean and run-infinite-hygiene is green
(62/63; PLUGINDRAGTEST is a scan-cache flake that passes on rerun). Neither
proves anything about this change - MediaWin.cpp is not in the macOS build.
The Windows job has not compiled it yet. Per windows-parity §4, even a green
Windows job only proves it links; nothing in CI can reach the video path.

parsed_message.title: Fix stereo-pair corruption in AudioCaptureRing on overflow/odd reads
parsed_message.description: Fix stereo-pair corruption in AudioCaptureRing on overflow/odd reads
parsed_message.body:
AudioCaptureRing::Write() dropped samples one at a time on overflow, so
a call that always hands it an even (L,R-paired) count could still
commit an odd number of trailing floats before the ring filled up.
Nothing re-anchors the stream's L/R phase afterward, so every pair
written after that point is silently channel-swapped - not shorter (the
existing duration/sample-count assertions never catch it), but garbled
until another odd-offset event happens to restore parity by chance.
Read() had the same class of bug from the consumer side for an odd
maxCount. This is a much better fit for a take reported as "sped up
initially, then completely breaks" (alternating noise and silence) than
a pure sample-count shortfall.
Both functions now only ever write/read whole stereo pairs, dropping or
holding back a trailing half-pair instead of committing/returning it
alone. Added INFINITE_AUDIORINGTEST, a deterministic headless
regression test that forces a mid-call overflow and an odd-sized read
and checks the ring never splits a pair - verified it fails against the
pre-fix code and passes against the fix. Also added
INFINITE_OFFLINERENDER_COOKDELAYMS to the offline render fixture to
simulate a heavy per-frame GPU cook (the condition the user's real
patch has that the existing fixture didn't), and wired both into the
av-sync-sweep driver.
AudioCaptureRing.cpp is shared cross-platform code (CMakeLists.txt),
so this fix applies to both macOS and Windows without a separate
Platform:: mirror.

bullets: While waiting for encoder room, keep generating audio, up to a second
Close the audio track once its fixed budget is spent. The audio for a
parsed_message.body:
A render with audio would stop dead a few dozen frames in and never
recover - the progress dialog frozen at 5-9%, Cancel the only way out.
Yesterday's backpressure fix is what made it visible: the pump now waits
for encoder room instead of letting the queue drop frames, and that wait
turned out to be one half of a deadlock.
Measured at the stall, not inferred: writer=writing, videoReady=0,

Two defects behind the "rendered audio is sped up" report, both only
visible on takes long enough to back the encoder queue up:

  what does not fit. That is right for a live take (better to lose a

  Platform::RecorderQueueHasRoom before rendering a frame and waits

  finishing would have taken. Platform::RecorderCancel drops the queued
  frames, skips finalize, and removes the partial file: measured at 3
  main-loop frames on a queue deep enough to have taken hundreds.

MovieInfo now carries per-track durations, and the fixture asserts what
landed in the FILE rather than what was handed to the recorder - the
frame-drop bug passed every append-side assertion we had.

Sweep coverage for both: a 1800-frame take and a cancel on that same
deep queue.

parsed_message.description: Parameterize OFFLINERENDERTEST over fps, sample rate and buffer size
parsed_message.body:
The fixture only ever exercised 10fps at whatever rate the machine's device
happened to negotiate, so neither of the speed defects it now guards against
would have been caught at another fps or rate. INFINITE_OFFLINERENDER_FPS /
_SECONDS pick the take's shape; _RATE / _BUFFER reopen the device the same
way the Audio settings menu's "Apply audio settings" does, so the take can
be checked against a rate the app negotiated rather than one it assumed.
The assertions are derived from the take's own settings instead of hardcoded
to 10 frames: frame count == fps * seconds, movie duration == that same
length, and appended audio == round(frames * rate / fps) within 64 frames
(~1.5ms - one block's rounding on an fps that doesn't divide the rate, and
nothing more).

64/512/2048, all exact to the sample.

parsed_message.title: Fix Offline Render audio speed and give duration real controls
parsed_message.description: Fix Offline Render audio speed and give duration real controls
parsed_message.body:
Two independent defects made a rendered take's audio play back off-speed
against its picture, both in the offline path only:
1. The take's audio was budgeted and muxed at a hardcoded 44100 Hz while
the graph's AudioNodes stay PrepareToPlay'd at the live device's rate -
a 48kHz device rendered as 44.1kHz is an 8.8% speed error. The rate is
now read from the device before it is detached, threaded through
StartOfflineRender, and used for both the per-frame sample budget and
the muxer's declared rate. The per-frame budget also comes from a
running cumulative target instead of a fixed round(sr/fps) quota, so an
fps that doesn't divide the rate evenly can't drift, and a budget over
kAudioMaxBlockFrames (any fps below ~12) is generated in several blocks
instead of being silently truncated - truncation shortened the audio
track, i.e. sped it up against the video.
2. The capture ring was armed before the audio device was detached, so the
live callback kept writing into it during AVAudioEngine's teardown. The
self-test take (1.0s of picture) came out with 1.33s of audio, all of it
past that tail out of sync. The device is now stopped first and the ring
drained before arming.
OFFLINERENDERTEST now asserts the appended sample count against
round(frames * rate / fps) and the movie duration against the take's own
length, rather than merely that an audio track exists - the assertion the
plan called for, and the one that catches both defects.
UI: duration and fps are typed InputInt fields (clamped) with 15/30/45/60s
presets and a live frame-count readout, replacing sliders that made an
exact value fiddly to hit. Offline Render also starts the audio device
briefly if a synth-audio take is requested while audio is off, since the
graph is only PrepareToPlay'd once a device has opened, and leaves it off
afterwards if it was off before.

OFFLINERENDERTEST exercises the live-audio ProcessOffline/capture-ring
path end to end (Oscillator source, not an AudioFileNode) and checks
the muxed file's frame count, video/audio track presence, and
duration. OFFLINERENDERREFUSETEST confirms a hardware-driven source
(Video In) anywhere in the patch makes StartOfflineRenderSession
refuse up front.

AVFoundation's asset metadata for a file this same process just
finished writing can lag the on-disk bytes by a beat, same reason
AUDIORECTEST checks its own movie well after StopRecording rather
than immediately.

parsed_message.title: Add Offline Render capture path and session plumbing
parsed_message.description: Add Offline Render capture path and session plumbing
parsed_message.body:
OutputNode gains a second, fully separate capture path (StartOfflineRender/
CaptureOfflineFrame/RequestFinishOfflineRender/PollOfflineFinalize) driven
frame-by-frame instead of by the live PBO/pacing pipeline - synchronous
glReadPixels, no A/V pacing needed since video and audio are captured in the
same lockstep step. Cancel/finish route through a background finalize thread
(same FinalizeResult pattern as StopRecordingAsync) so a Cancel click never
blocks the UI.
main.cpp adds the session-level plumbing: FindHardwareDrivenNode (refuses a
take up front if the patch has a live camera/MIDI/Syphon source),
StartOfflineRenderSession (stops the live audio device and forces Transport
to play for the take's duration), the main-loop pump that ticks Transport and
calls AudioEngine::ProcessOffline once per offline frame, and a floating
progress/Cancel dialog. Render/duration/preroll controls added to
OutputNode's params panel.

parsed_message.title: Make OutputNode recording stop asynchronous to avoid UI freeze
parsed_message.description: Make OutputNode recording stop asynchronous to avoid UI freeze
parsed_message.body:
StopRecordingAsync() does the GL-bound audio/PBO drain on the render
thread, then hands the recorder handle to a background thread for the
part that can take tens of seconds on a long or backlogged take
(encoder join + AVAssetWriter finishWriting). PollFinalize() picks up
the result once a frame. The interactive Stop button now uses this
path; StopRecording() stays fully synchronous for the destructor and
test harnesses that need the file complete on return.
Also regenerates docs/node_param_audit.md to match current main.cpp.

parsed_message.title: Item 5: cover the drop path and add a one-sided LEAD assertion
parsed_message.description: Item 5: cover the drop path and add a one-sided LEAD assertion
parsed_message.body:
RECEXPORTTEST ran at 320x240, where the whole take's lifetime video
bytes (~54MB) can never cross the 256MB queue budget even with zero
draining - the drop path Item 3 introduced, and the padding semantics
Item 2 fixed, were structurally untested. Parameterize the test by
resolution/label and add two variants: 720p (big enough per-frame to
matter) and "starved" (720p, with the queue's byte budget deliberately
shrunk for the take via a new RecorderSetTestQueueByteBudget hook).
A real hardware encoder drains far faster than this test can produce,
so reproducing an admission rejection needed a smaller ceiling rather
than a slower consumer - removing the backpressure spin outright was
tried first and instead starved the encoder's own dispatch queue of a
chance to run at all (this test thread never yields otherwise),
rejecting ~90% of frames and wiping out marker windows rather than
exercising the bounded, recoverable drops the byte budget is for.
Shrinking the budget to 10MB under the same safe spin every variant
uses gives real, moderate, reproducible drops (1-5 per run here)
without losing any markers.
Also adds a one-sided "video must never lead audio" verdict: the bug
Item 2 fixed made a drop stamp new content backward in time, which
only shows up as a negative video-minus-audio delta, distinct from the
existing DRIFT/OFFSET verdicts. Confirmed passing (worst lead 0ms) in
both the default and starved variants.
Windows mirrors the same queueByteBudget/RecorderSetTestQueueByteBudget
change for parity; compile-unverified here (no Windows toolchain), same
as Items 1-3.
Full sweep: 11/11 pass (av-sync-sweep) and 63/63 pass
(run-infinite-hygiene, after ruling out two known-flaky, unrelated
fixtures via rerun: RECEXPORTTEST's pre-existing hardware VideoToolbox
wedge flake, and PLUGINDRAGTEST).

parsed_message.title: Item 4: pump a frame before Stop's blocking finalize, so it looks alive
parsed_message.description: Item 4: pump a frame before Stop's blocking finalize, so it looks alive
parsed_message.body:
OutputNode::StopRecording() can block the render thread for tens of
seconds under a big deficit (audio backlog flush, PBO readback drain,
the encoder join, finishWriting's runloop spin) - previously the
click that triggers it froze the app with zero visible feedback.
Took the smaller of the two options the fix brief allows for this
item: Stop stays synchronous (no new worker thread, no handle-
ownership handoff, so RECTEARDOWNTEST's both variants need no
changes), but the click now only sets a flag. OutputNode::
RequestStopRecording() marks the stop as wanted and returns
immediately; the button renders a disabled "Finalizing..." state with
the live pending-frame count instead of re-entering the blocking call.
The actual Platform::RecorderStop happens at the very top of the next
frame, right after glfwPollEvents() - the earliest point at which the
previous frame's "finalizing" state is guaranteed to have already
reached the screen via glfwSwapBuffers, so the click is visibly
acknowledged before the app appears to hang rather than during it.
Went with this over the full async rewrite given the risk of the
alternative (a second recorder-handle ownership path racing teardown)
against a straightforward, low-risk fix for the actual complaint: the
app looking frozen with no feedback. If the finalize block itself
still needs to be non-blocking, that's the follow-up commit the brief
scoped separately.

parsed_message.title: Item 3: size the encoder queue by bytes, not by frame count
parsed_message.description: Item 3: size the encoder queue by bytes, not by frame count
parsed_message.body:
kMaxQueueDepth=4 / kMaxPoolSize=8 gave 33MB of elasticity at 1080p but
only ~2MB at 320x240 - resolution-blind, so the same constant left
almost no slack at the resolutions users actually export at.
Replace both caps with a shared 256MB byte budget on frameQueue and
bufferPool, tracked via queuedBytes/poolBytes guarded by the same
mutexes that already protect those containers. The frameQueue.empty()
escape hatch on admission guarantees a single frame larger than the
whole budget still gets in rather than being permanently rejected.
256MB is a starting value (reasonable range 128-512MB per the fix
brief), not a measured one - it buys ~32 frames of elasticity at
1080p RGBA versus the old 4.
Same change on both platforms (Platform.mm, MediaWin.cpp).

PacedRepeat's padding used to write the *new* frame into all N repeat
slots, the earliest of which is N-1 frames in the past - so a dropped
append's catch-up burst placed that content at a PTS earlier than it
was actually rendered, making the video visibly lead the audio.

untouched) so a repeatCount-N frame fills slots 0..N-2 with the
previously-processed frame's pixels and only the final slot with its
own. The very first frame of a take has no previous frame, so it still
uses its own content for all N - there's no better answer for slot
zero.
RecorderPump picks currentFlipped vs prevFlipped per repeat and
swaps prevFlipped in once the frame's repeats are done, regardless
of whether they all reached the writer.
to the worker thread.

movie, 6s take): 180 frames written, 0 dropped, DRIFT 0ms, worst

parsed_message.body:
Every undo/redo and multi-node delete respawns nodes from scratch and
routes through ReloadDerivedState(), which for file-backed nodes calls
into Platform:: to re-decode the source file from disk every time -
even when the file was already decoded earlier this session and hasn't
changed on disk.
Added AssetCache<T> (src/core/AssetCache.h): a generic path-keyed cache
validated by mtime+size and bounded by LRU eviction on a byte budget.
Wired it into the raw-decode step of:
(512MB budget each); GL texture upload still happens per node.
Normalize() (512MB budget); Normalize() is per-node-parameterized
so it still runs on every load from the cached raw data.
a shared wrapper around Platform::DecodeAudioFileToBuffer, since
that call is duplicated across AnalyzeNodes/AudioFileNode,
SamplerNode, GranularNode, PaulStretchNode, MolderNode,
GrainMolderNode, and DrumSequencerNode. All seven now route through
it instead of calling Platform:: directly.
VideoSourceNode is unchanged. Its Open() always constructs a fresh
decoder handle per node instance, and undo/redo always respawns a new
VideoSourceNode (mVideo is null at Open() time), so there is no safe
same-node early-out available without caching the stateful decoder
itself, which is out of scope for this change - stated here plainly
rather than adding a no-op "fix."
Cache benefit isn't reflected in the Part A perf numbers (that stress
patch has no file-backed assets); re-measuring with asset-heavy nodes
is left for a follow-up rather than fabricating a number here.

same 3 pre-existing failures as Part A), geometry-transform-sweep all
green, and audio-node-sweep's mid-playback-delete checks all green.

thread within one block" failures) reproduces byte-for-byte identical
on a pristine, unmodified build in this environment (confirmed via
stash + rebuild diff) - a pre-existing environment issue, not caused

changed on disk.

Added AssetCache<T> (src/core/AssetCache.h): a generic path-keyed cache
validated by mtime+size and bounded by LRU eviction on a byte budget.
Wired it into the raw-decode step of:
  - ImageSourceNode / EnvironmentNode: caches decoded CPU pixel buffers
    (512MB budget each); GL texture upload still happens per node.
  - ModelSourceNode: caches parsed raw vertex/index buffers pre-
    Normalize() (512MB budget); Normalize() is per-node-parameterized
    so it still runs on every load from the cached raw data.
  - AudioDecodeCache (src/core/AudioDecodeCache.{h,cpp}, 1GB budget):
    a shared wrapper around Platform::DecodeAudioFileToBuffer, since
    that call is duplicated across AnalyzeNodes/AudioFileNode,
    SamplerNode, GranularNode, PaulStretchNode, MolderNode,
    GrainMolderNode, and DrumSequencerNode. All seven now route through
    it instead of calling Platform:: directly.

VideoSourceNode is unchanged. Its Open() always constructs a fresh
decoder handle per node instance, and undo/redo always respawns a new
VideoSourceNode (mVideo is null at Open() time), so there is no safe
same-node early-out available without caching the stateful decoder
itself, which is out of scope for this change - stated here plainly
rather than adding a no-op "fix."

Cache benefit isn't reflected in the Part A perf numbers (that stress
patch has no file-backed assets); re-measuring with asset-heavy nodes
is left for a follow-up rather than fabricating a number here.

Verification: clean rebuild, full hygiene suite unaffected (56/59,
same 3 pre-existing failures as Part A), geometry-transform-sweep all
green, and audio-node-sweep's mid-playback-delete checks all green.
audio-node-sweep's headless param-sweep step (381 "reaches audio
thread within one block" failures) reproduces byte-for-byte identical
on a pristine, unmodified build in this environment (confirmed via
stash + rebuild diff) - a pre-existing environment issue, not caused
by this change.

parsed_message.title: Fail INFINITE_RECEXPORTTEST fast when the encoder wedges
parsed_message.description: Fail INFINITE_RECEXPORTTEST fast when the encoder wedges
parsed_message.body:
RunRecExportTest's per-step pacing spin-wait
(Platform::RecorderPendingFrameCount(rec) >= 3) is bounded to 120s per
render step, but that cap resets every step. If AVAssetWriterInput's
isReadyForMoreMediaData never transitions back to ready - plausible on
GitHub's shared macOS runners, which don't reliably have hardware
VideoToolbox encode access - RecorderPump (Platform.mm) blocks forever
by design (see its comment), pendingCount never drops, and every
remaining render step burns its own fresh 120s cap. With ~100 steps
left in a wedge, that's ~3.3 hours, matching two observed CI hangs
(runs 33284955189 and 33292843911) almost exactly.
Track wall-clock time spent waiting across the whole render loop, not
per-step, and bail out with a REC EXPORT FAIL verdict after 45s total
if the encoder never catches up. A wedged encoder now fails in
seconds instead of hanging the runner for hours; a working encoder
(the normal case) never approaches the 45s budget since pendingCount
keeps draining.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

parsed_message.title: Fix mp3/non-native-rate file playback speed and position display
parsed_message.description: Fix mp3/non-native-rate file playback speed and position display
parsed_message.body:
AudioFilePlayerAudioNode::ProcessBlock always advanced its read cursor
by exactly 1 frame per output sample, which only produces correct pitch
and speed when the decoded file's sample rate matches the audio
engine's running rate - e.g. a 44.1kHz mp3 played back on a 48kHz
device played fast and sharp. Steps the cursor by the file/engine rate
ratio instead, with linear interpolation between the two nearest
source frames since the cursor is now generally non-integral.
Also fixes PositionSeconds(), which divided the (now file-rate-based)
frame counter by the engine's sample rate rather than the file's -
would have shown an incorrect elapsed-time/progress-bar reading
whenever the two rates differ, even after the speed fix above.

parsed_message.title: Fix use-after-free crash: gate retired-node teardown on audio thread progress
parsed_message.description: Fix use-after-free crash: gate retired-node teardown on audio thread progress
parsed_message.body:
Undo (Cmd+Z) retires every node into gRetiredNodes and destroys them
unconditionally at the top of the next video frame - a delay sized only
for a GL-texture hazard, with no relationship to whether the real-time
audio thread has actually finished a block against the topology that
referenced them. Under load (e.g. synchronous sample decode during an
undo restore) the audio thread could still be mid-ProcessBlock on a
freed node, producing a SIGBUS wild-pointer crash inside
SpecBlurKernel::ProcessBlock.
AudioEngine now stamps each published topology with a monotonically
increasing generation and records the generation the audio thread has
actually finished processing. Retired nodes record the last generation
that could still reach them, and gRetiredNodes only drains an entry once
the audio thread confirms it has moved past that generation (or the
engine isn't running at all).
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

referenced them. Under load (e.g. synchronous sample decode during an
undo restore) the audio thread could still be mid-ProcessBlock on a
freed node, producing a SIGBUS wild-pointer crash inside

parsed_message.title: Stop the macOS recorder from silently dropping padded frames
parsed_message.description: Stop the macOS recorder from silently dropping padded frames
parsed_message.body:
Constant-frame-rate padding hands the encoder bursts of frames, and the
AVAssetWriter adaptor's pixel buffer pool only recycles as the encoder
drains it - so a burst could exhaust the pool, CVPixelBufferPoolCreate
PixelBuffer would fail, and AppendPixelsToWriter returned false.
The worker's response to that was to abandon every remaining repeat of
the frame and break, without touching droppedCount. The movie came out
short of what the caller had been told was accepted, nothing reported
it, and the missing frames showed up as sync drift in the back half of
the take - intermittently, since it depended on encoder timing.
Wait for a pool buffer instead of treating exhaustion as a lost frame,
and count whatever still has to be abandoned so this can never be
silent again. INFINITE_RECEXPORTTEST now asserts the invariant
directly: every frame the recorder accepts is written or dropped.

parsed_message.title: Measure A/V sync on a real exported movie, and fix the crash it found
parsed_message.description: Measure A/V sync on a real exported movie, and fix the crash it found
parsed_message.body:
RECSYNCTEST only exercises the pacing arithmetic in isolation, which is not
evidence that an actual written file is in sync - the distinction this repo
already learned the hard way with PortableFft::Inverse, which returned
time-reversed audio while its test printed OK on the real Windows runner.
INFINITE_RECEXPORTTEST marks a take with five simultaneous tone/flash pairs
decided by the same boolean, writes it through the real platform recorder
while rendering at a rate deliberately mismatched to the target, then reopens
the file with the app's own decoders and measures how far apart the two
tracks landed. It reports drift and constant offset as separate verdicts:
drift is the bug that shipped, while a fixed lead/lag is an encoder-priming
or capture-tap question with a different cause and a looser tolerance.
Verified it catches the original bug rather than merely passing: with the
pacing reverted it reports 120 frames instead of 180 and an offset growing
325 -> 1658ms across the take, which is exactly the 20-into-30fps deficit.
With the fix, 180 frames and a flat +8ms - within the 8.3ms sampling
resolution of the flash detector, so no measurable AAC priming offset on the
AVFoundation path. Deterministic across eight consecutive runs.
Writing that test immediately crashed the app, which is the more serious
find. -[AVAssetWriterInput appendSampleBuffer:] raises an ObjC exception when
readyForMoreMediaData is NO rather than returning NO, and the live-audio path
appended without ever checking it - the video path spin-waits on the encoder
queue and the file-audio path returns to retry next frame, but live audio had
neither. A stalled AAC encoder was therefore an uncaught NSException that
terminates the app and loses the whole take, on the exact path a live-audio
recording uses. RecorderAppendAudio runs on the render thread and so cannot
spin waiting for readiness; it now parks samples in a backlog and retries on
the next drain, with RecorderStop flushing the tail before the worker marks
the audio input finished.
Headless, so it runs on the Windows CI runner too - the only machine evidence
anywhere that Media Foundation's muxing keeps the two tracks together. That
takes P8 from grade C to B.

parsed_message.title: Latch record fps for the take, and skip readbacks that would be decimated
parsed_message.description: Latch record fps for the take, and skip readbacks that would be decimated
parsed_message.body:
Two things the pacing fix got wrong about a user changing settings mid-take.
The recorder fixes its video PTS denominator at RecorderStart and never
re-reads it, but the fps slider in the Output node's UI stayed live during a
recording and PacedRepeatCount read it straight off the node. Dragging
30 -> 60 mid-take would have made the pacer emit frames twice as fast as the
encoder stamps them, stretching the video to double length against real
audio - a worse desync than the one being fixed. Latch fps at StartRecording
alongside the dimensions, which are already locked for exactly this reason,
and disable the slider (and "include audio", inert mid-take for the same
reason) while recording so the UI stops implying otherwise.
Vsync needs no such handling - it only moves the render rate, which is what
the pacing already absorbs - but with it off the render loop can run many
times the target rate, and every one of those frames was costing a
full-resolution glReadPixels whose result the pacing then discarded. Count
what the readback pipeline already holds and skip issuing one we are certain
to decimate. If that guess leaves us short later the padding path covers it,
so it can only cost a slightly staler frame, never sync.
Adds a 240fps -> 30fps case to RECSYNCTEST for the uncapped-render path.

parsed_message.title: Fix exported video drifting out of sync with live audio
parsed_message.description: Fix exported video drifting out of sync with live audio
bullets: rendered* frame, so the file came out with a video duration of
parsed_message.body:
A live-audio recording has two independent clocks. The video track's PTS is
a plain frame counter over recordFps on both platforms - frameIndex/fps via
AVAssetWriter on macOS, FrameNumberToHns(frameCount, fps) via Media
Foundation on Windows - while live audio is stamped from the real captured
sample count. OutputNode::CaptureFrame emitted exactly one video frame per
renderedFrames/recordFps against an audio duration of real elapsed time.
Unless the render loop happened to hold exactly recordFps, the two walked
apart linearly across the take: 30s of audio recorded while rendering at
20fps produced 20s of video. Playback while monitoring is real-time either
way, which is why it looked fine in the app and only broke in the export.
Pace the video against the same sample count the muxer stamps the audio
with, using RecorderAppend's repeatCount - which both recorders already
honour and nothing had ever passed anything but 1 to. Rendering faster than
the target decimates, slower pads with a repeat, and the final drain takes
the whole remainder so the tail reaches the audio's full length. Deriving
the target from the audio sample count rather than a wall clock also keeps
it immune to the audio device clock drifting from the system clock, which
is its own source of desync over a long take.
Only the live path needs this: with an audio file source the recorders
slave audio to the video's synthetic clock instead, so that path is in sync
by construction and still keeps every rendered frame.
Also surface capture-ring overflow in the recording status - dropped audio
samples shift everything after the gap earlier in the file, so a stall that
costs audio is a sync bug, not just a glitch.
Add INFINITE_RECSYNCTEST, which simulates whole takes at render rates
above, below and equal to the target and asserts the video timeline tracks
the audio timeline to within a frame throughout. It is pure arithmetic over
the pacing both recorders' PTS depend on, so it runs in the hygiene gate and
on the Windows CI runner - the one place the Media Foundation half of this
can be executed by machine at all.

Fix eight Windows/parity defects and un-blind the hygiene gate

The pillar-parity audit surfaced two test-harness holes and confirmed six
still-open defects from docs/WINDOWS_VERIFICATION.md against current source.

Test harness:

- driver.sh matched only FAIL|BUG$, but 56 fixture failure branches in
  main.cpp print a bare SUSPECT / MISMATCH / DID NOT MOVE / TONE MISSING.
  Every one of those failed silently with the gate reporting green. Widen the
  marker and, separately, require a positive verdict at all, so a fixture that
  dies before asserting can no longer pass by staying quiet. audit.sh gets the
  same two rules so the gates agree.

- Two failures the old gate was hiding, both found by the above:
  MACROTEST asserted the Macro XY pad against a size-x range of 0.01..0.50
  while the slider has been 0.01..1.0, so the pad - a core performance
  control - had been unverified for as long as the range has been wider.
  GEOTEST asserted LastUploads() == 0 on a steady frame, but that counter is
  reset inside Render3DNode's draw and the cache's ideal outcome is skipping
  the pass entirely, leaving the previous render's count in place. It read
  SUSPECT on a perfectly-behaving cache. Assert the frame-to-frame delta,
  which is the invariant actually meant.

Windows defects (1.3-1.8), all confirmed live before fixing:

- 1.3 MIDI clock sync never worked. HandleShortMessage masked status & 0xF0
  and then switched on 0xF8/0xFA/0xFC, which that mask cannot produce, so
  Pulse()/Reset() were dead code and MidiClockIsPresent() was permanently
  false. macOS tests the raw status first and syncs fine. Dispatch System
  Real-Time before masking.

- 1.6 Audio Analyze drove visuals wrongly. low/mid/high came from fixed band
  indices (~20-106 / ~106-373 / ~1982-4571 Hz vs macOS's 20-250 / 250-2000 /
  2000-16000), with low's weights summing to 1.5. Three further divergences
  found while fixing: bands[] used a linear clamp(v*4) against macOS's
  compressive sqrt(12v), the ladder stopped at 16 kHz where macOS runs to
  nyquist, and rms/peak/low/mid/high were never smoothed. Both paths run the
  same 1024-point FFT with the same normalisation, so all formulas are now
  transcribed from Platform.mm and agree by construction.

- 1.8 Dropped notes with 2+ controllers. MidiStart opens every device with
  CALLBACK_FUNCTION, so the "single-producer" note ring had one producer per
  device racing the same index. Serialise on a dedicated ringMutex - not
  gState.mutex, which the Note Off path already holds when it publishes.

- 1.4 All Windows text rendered at the wrong size. The cap-height pass passed
  GGO_GLYPH_INDEX while asking for L'H', measuring glyph 72 instead of the
  letter. Also fixes letter spacing (applied in em units, then divided by cap
  height) and quadratic tessellation that never reached t=1.0, notching every
  on-curve point.

- 1.7 Camera frames sheared at unaligned widths. The file-decode path was
  fixed to read MF_MT_DEFAULT_STRIDE; the camera path still assumed w*4.
  Thread the negotiated stride through, and re-read it on resolution change.

- 1.5 Upgrading macOS users silently lost their theme and recents when these
  moved under AppSupportDir(). Migrate once on load instead of reverting.

Autosave could fail on every frame in silence: EnsureDir returned true
unconditionally (contradicting its own doc comment) so an unwritable settings
directory was invisible, and PollAutosave discarded WriteAutosaveNow's result.
The user found out only after a crash, with nothing to recover. EnsureDir now
reports whether the directory exists afterwards, AppSupportDir returns empty
rather than a path that swallows writes, and a failing autosave is logged once
and flagged in the Autosave menu.

Hygiene suite 60/60 green under the stricter gate; static lane 11/11.
Windows fixes remain unfalsified on Windows hardware - see the status note
added to Part 1 of docs/WINDOWS_VERIFICATION.md.
