parsed_message.title: Add pillar-parity-audit skill: per-pillar, per-platform coverage map
parsed_message.description: Add pillar-parity-audit skill: per-pillar, per-platform coverage map
parsed_message.body:
run-infinite-hygiene answers "did I break something"; it cannot answer
"which pillar is verified, and on which OS". This skill does.
15 pillars: the ten obvious ones (nodes, shortcuts, settings, rendering,
panels, modulation, the four content engines, I/O, performance, save and
recovery) plus five properties that don't map to a feature and are where
this repo's real cross-platform defects came from - the platform-layer
contract, distribution integrity, dual-path numeric equivalence, glyph
metrics, and UI/UX conformance.
static-checks.sh: 131 Platform:: declarations checked for both
implementations, no _WIN32 under src/nodes, every win/*.cpp in the build,
kShortcuts[] cross-referenced against live handlers, Ctrl||Cmd modifier

parsed_message.title: Fix vertically mirrored Windows video export, and raise encode quality
parsed_message.description: Fix vertically mirrored Windows video export, and raise encode quality
parsed_message.body:
Two separate defects behind the same user report ("garbled, compressed,
upside down and flipped").
1. Every movie recorded on Windows came out vertically mirrored.
Media Foundation's RGB32 input format defaults to bottom-up
orientation - the GDI BITMAPINFOHEADER convention, signalled by a
negative MF_MT_DEFAULT_STRIDE. ConfigureRecorderVideo never set that
attribute, while RgbaBottomUpToBgraTopDown was already flipping GL's
bottom-up readback into top-down rows, so the sink writer read a
top-down buffer as bottom-up and mirrored the whole take. Set the
attribute explicitly to a positive width * 4.
docs/WINDOWS_VERIFICATION.md 1.7 covers stride on the decode side;
the encode side was never checked. macOS is unaffected - AVFoundation
takes a CVPixelBuffer with no orientation ambiguity.
2. The bitrate ladder was 0.08 bits per pixel per frame - roughly 5 Mbps
at 1080p30 - and no H.264 profile was requested, so an MFT was free to
pick Baseline (no CABAC, no 8x8 transform). Media Foundation's encoder
is weaker than VideoToolbox at equal bitrate, and this app's output is
its worst case: hard-edged pixel art, flat colour fields, dithering,
fine generative detail. Raised to 0.30 bpp (cap 80 Mbps) and set High
profile, best-effort so a refusing encoder still works.
Platform.mm was running on bare AVFoundation defaults with the same
problem, less severely; it now uses the identical ladder plus High
profile, so the two platforms agree by construction.
Not fixed here, and worth its own change: recording is a real-time
capture, not a render. CaptureFrame() runs once per rendered frame from
CookIfNeeded, and recordFps only stamps timestamps - it paces nothing -
so file duration is frameCount/recordFps regardless of how long those
frames took. The encoder queue is 4 deep and silently drops past that.
INFINITE_AUDIORECTEST already works around this, checking duration
against the real frame count rather than wall-clock elapsed time.
Verified: macOS hygiene suite 59 passed / 0 failed; INFINITE_VIDEOAUDIOTEST
round-trips and ffprobe reports profile=High. Frame drops in that fixture
are 37/18 both before and after, so the higher bitrate did not worsen
pacing.
Per windows-parity section 4, Windows CI cannot reach the recorder - it
proves the change links, nothing more. Both fixes need a real Windows
confirmation before being reported as verified.

parsed_message.title: Fix a use-after-free on the Windows audio thread, and a per-restart handle leak
parsed_message.description: Fix a use-after-free on the Windows audio thread, and a per-restart handle leak
parsed_message.body:
Both were open items under docs/WINDOWS_VERIFICATION.md 1.9.
AudioInputCaptureRead runs on the audio render thread and was gated on
`running && sampleRate > 0.0`, but CaptureTapEngine::OnFormat wrote
sampleRate BEFORE ring.Init() - so between those two statements the render
thread could pass the gate and index ring.buffers while assign() was
reallocating it. The window reopened on every input-engine restart, which
PollAudioRecovery triggers on any device change. Readiness is now a single
atomic set only after the ring is allocated, and that is what the read path
gates on.
ThreadMain's bufferEvent was a local inside the SUCCEEDED(Initialize)
block and was never closed on any path out, leaking one event handle per
capture start/stop cycle - on both capture engines, since they share
ThreadMain. It now lives with the other locals and is closed by cleanup().
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

parsed_message.title: Fix app-wide hang from duplicate pin ids, and guard against it recurring
parsed_message.description: Fix app-wide hang from duplicate pin ids, and guard against it recurring
bullets: DiscreteSlotScope (main.cpp) gives a repeated sub-panel its own discrete
NodeBuilder::BeginPin refuses to relink an id already emitted this frame,
PINDUPTEST spawns every registered node type with both param sections
parsed_message.body:
The Wavetable node froze the app. Its two engine columns draw the same
control labels, and a discrete param's pin id comes from a hash of its
label alone (ImGui::PushID scopes widget ids, not these), so both engines
landed on one pin id. imgui-node-editor links a node's pins into a list as
they're emitted, so emitting one id twice in a frame made that list
circular - and every walk of it (the hit-test pass, the bounds pass, the
drag scan) is a plain `for (p = last; p; p = p->m_PreviousPin)`. The app
didn't crash, glitch or draw wrong: it spun at 100% CPU inside one frame,
forever, as soon as the cursor was over the canvas. Users saw only a
system "hang" report.
Three changes, at three depths:
namespace, so engine B's controls get their own slots. Engine 0 keeps the
unscoped hash, so bindings in already-saved patches still resolve. This
also fixes the user-visible half of the same collision: modulating engine
A's filter was driving engine B's too.
turning any future collision into a warning instead of a freeze. Stamped
with the ImGui frame index rather than m_IsLive, which Object's ctor sets
true and so cannot distinguish a first emission from a repeat.
forced open and asserts zero duplicates. Verified against a negative
control (it catches all 6 colliding Wavetable labels); 267 types clean
with the fix. ROUNDTRIPTEST covers every type too but draws them
collapsed, which is exactly why it never saw this.
Also: test runs (INFINITE_EXITAFTER) now create their window hidden and
unfocused. They were stealing focus mid-suite, and a slow frame in a
foreground window is what tripped WindowServer's 10-second watchdog into
writing the hang spindumps in the first place.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
parsed_message.raw:
Fix app-wide hang from duplicate pin ids, and guard against it recurring

The Wavetable node froze the app. Its two engine columns draw the same
control labels, and a discrete param's pin id comes from a hash of its
label alone (ImGui::PushID scopes widget ids, not these), so both engines
landed on one pin id. imgui-node-editor links a node's pins into a list as
they're emitted, so emitting one id twice in a frame made that list
circular - and every walk of it (the hit-test pass, the bounds pass, the
drag scan) is a plain `for (p = last; p; p = p->m_PreviousPin)`. The app
didn't crash, glitch or draw wrong: it spun at 100% CPU inside one frame,
forever, as soon as the cursor was over the canvas. Users saw only a
system "hang" report.

Three changes, at three depths:

- DiscreteSlotScope (main.cpp) gives a repeated sub-panel its own discrete
  namespace, so engine B's controls get their own slots. Engine 0 keeps the
  unscoped hash, so bindings in already-saved patches still resolve. This
  also fixes the user-visible half of the same collision: modulating engine
  A's filter was driving engine B's too.

- NodeBuilder::BeginPin refuses to relink an id already emitted this frame,
  turning any future collision into a warning instead of a freeze. Stamped
  with the ImGui frame index rather than m_IsLive, which Object's ctor sets
  true and so cannot distinguish a first emission from a repeat.

- PINDUPTEST spawns every registered node type with both param sections
  forced open and asserts zero duplicates. Verified against a negative
  control (it catches all 6 colliding Wavetable labels); 267 types clean
  with the fix. ROUNDTRIPTEST covers every type too but draws them
  collapsed, which is exactly why it never saw this.

Also: test runs (INFINITE_EXITAFTER) now create their window hidden and
unfocused. They were stealing focus mid-suite, and a slow frame in a
foreground window is what tripped WindowServer's 10-second watchdog into
writing the hang spindumps in the first place.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

parsed_message.title: Keep modulation live on a node with its params collapsed
parsed_message.description: Keep modulation live on a node with its params collapsed
parsed_message.body:
A parameter only existed, as far as the apply pass was concerned, for the
frames it drew in: ModSlider/ModKnob/ColorSwatch hand out a raw float*
through RegisterParam, and the pass writes through exactly the pointers
registered that frame. Closing a node's eye stopped its params drawing, so
every modulator, expression and palette binding patched into it silently
froze - the cable was still there, the "mod" tag was still there, the matrix
still listed it, and nothing moved.
A collapsed node that actually has something driving it now still runs its
whole params dispatch, with the UI suppressed three ways: gParamRegisterOnly
makes each Mod* widget register its ParamRef and return before it draws or
declares a pin (a collapsed node's pins come from CollapsedBindingPins, and
ed::BeginPin twice on one id in a frame is undefined), SkipItems makes every
plain ImGui widget a no-op so the node's size and layout are untouched, and
an empty clip rect swallows any raw draw-list work around them. Gated on
there being a binding at all, so the common collapsed node costs what it did
before.
HIDETEST now stamps a sentinel outside the binding's range while the node is
collapsed and checks the apply pass puts it back. MODMATRIXTEST's test 2 was
asserting the old behaviour (registered nothing while collapsed); it now
requires the opposite, alongside the KnownParam stickiness it was really
about.

parsed_message.body:

Ctrl+N silently did nothing there. Gate on KeySuper || KeyCtrl instead,
matching the cmdOrCtrl helper the undo/redo/duplicate/add-node bindings
already use.

on Windows. Add a MODKEY macro ("Ctrl" on _WIN32, "Cmd" elsewhere) and use
it in the File and Edit menus, the shortcuts reference window, the help
text, and the Group node's description.

parsed_message.title: Fix Sampler position dropped on copy/paste; baseline new sweep params
parsed_message.description: Fix Sampler position dropped on copy/paste; baseline new sweep params
parsed_message.body:
SamplerNode::ReloadFromPath re-clamped the restored position against
start/end. CopyParams runs ReloadDerivedState -> ReloadFromPath, so
pasting a Sampler could silently move its playback start; ROUNDTRIPTEST
caught it as 'copy/paste dropped values: Sampler'. Restore position
verbatim like start/end - CookIfNeeded already clamps it every frame.
The new 'position' and 'decay' params also tripped AUDIOPARAMSWEEPTEST's
check B, the same documented blind spot every other Sampler param is
baselined for: the sweep's bare rig loads no file, and an unloaded
Sampler is silent by design, so no param can move the rendered signature.
Also repoints last-release-sha.txt at 106ea54 (the v0.2.1 release commit)
so the changelog covers exactly what shipped after v0.2.1.

parsed_message.title: Fix VST3/AU plugin note input being silently dropped
parsed_message.description: Fix VST3/AU plugin note input being silently dropped
parsed_message.body:
AudioNode's slot-aware SetNoteInbox(slot, inbox, cursor) default only
forwarded slot 0 to the single-slot overload. Nodes whose slot 0 is an
audio input put their note pin at slot 1 - AudioPluginNode,
WaveTerrainNode, ImageSpectralSynthNode - so the topology builder's call
was dropped on the floor: mNoteInbox stayed nullptr and the node was mute
no matter what note source was wired in. Forward every slot instead; the
builder only calls slots the node actually exposes, and Note Merge (the
one real multi-input consumer) overrides this anyway.
PLUGINSCANTEST and the audio param sweep both wired their inboxes by
calling the two-arg overload directly, bypassing the very dispatch that
was broken - which is how this shipped past them. Both now wire through
the slot-aware overload at the node's real slot; with the fix reverted,
PLUGINSCANTEST reports note-on peak=0.00000 FAIL.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

parsed_message.description: Fix output windows vanishing behind editor on multi-monitor setups
parsed_message.body:
Projector windows ("Open in new window") had no way to go borderless/
topmost/fullscreen or target a specific display, so on Windows (no
OS-level app fullscreen) the output window drops behind the editor as
soon as focus returns to it. Adds F11 fullscreen (borderless +
GLFW_FLOATING on macOS, borderless + HWND_TOPMOST via new
Platform::ConfigureOutputWindow/ReassertOutputWindowTopmost on
Windows) and a per-window Display submenu to move between monitors,
deliberately avoiding exclusive GLFW fullscreen which is what
auto-iconifies across displays. Also fixes the projector context
inheriting a default swap interval instead of vsync 0, and opens new
windows at a scaled-down positioning size instead of native resolution.
Reimplemented from scratch against current main per
local-prompts/output-window-multimonitor.md; not ported from any fork.

parsed_message.title: Windows: implement Syphon In/Out via Spout2 (SpoutGL)
parsed_message.description: Windows: implement Syphon In/Out via Spout2 (SpoutGL)
parsed_message.body:
Fills in the Windows half of the existing Platform::Syphon* facade, backed
by Spout2's minimal SpoutGL library, per local-prompts/11-spout-windows.md.
SyphonInNode/SyphonOutNode are unchanged - the GL_TEXTURE_2D (Spout) vs
GL_TEXTURE_RECTANGLE (Syphon/node contract) mismatch is resolved by blitting
into an internally-owned rectangle target (SpoutGLBridge), and (appName,
serverName, uuid) maps onto Spout's single sender-name string via
serverName.
SpoutGL is vendored as plain source under external/spout2 (not vcpkg),
guarded by if(WIN32), split into its own translation unit
(PlatformWinSyphon.cpp) so the GL/DirectX-heavy code and its headers never
reach PlatformWin.cpp - which is also compiled into the GL/DX-free
infinite-vst3-scanner helper target. SetAutoShare(false)/SetCPUshare(false)
make Send/Receive fail closed rather than falling back to a slow CPU path
when WGL_NV_DX_interop2 is unavailable.
Adds INFINITE_SPOUTLOOPTEST: an in-process server+client loopback that
publishes a synthetic texture and checks the pixel/orientation round-trip,
skipping cleanly on macOS and on Windows machines without GL/DX interop.
Windows-only change; macOS's existing Syphon implementation (Platform.mm)
is untouched. Windows side is CI-built only - not yet verified on real
hardware.

parsed_message.title: Windows: enable Video Processor MFT so video files actually open
parsed_message.description: Windows: enable Video Processor MFT so video files actually open
parsed_message.body:
VideoOpen created its IMFSourceReader with no attributes, so the reader
could only hand out whatever subtype the raw decoder produced (e.g. NV12
for H.264). ConfigureVideoOutputType then asked for MFVideoFormat_RGB32,
which failed on nearly any normal video since there was no MFT to do the
conversion. Set MF_SOURCE_READER_ENABLE_ADVANCED_VIDEO_PROCESSING on the
reader attributes at both the file-open and camera-open call sites to pull
the Video Processor MFT into the pipeline.
Also stopped ReadNextVideoFrame from assuming the negotiated RGB32 buffer
is tightly packed at width * 4: now reads MF_MT_DEFAULT_STRIDE off the
negotiated media type and handles a negative (bottom-up) stride.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
parsed_message.raw:
Windows: enable Video Processor MFT so video files actually open

VideoOpen created its IMFSourceReader with no attributes, so the reader
could only hand out whatever subtype the raw decoder produced (e.g. NV12
for H.264). ConfigureVideoOutputType then asked for MFVideoFormat_RGB32,
which failed on nearly any normal video since there was no MFT to do the
conversion. Set MF_SOURCE_READER_ENABLE_ADVANCED_VIDEO_PROCESSING on the
reader attributes at both the file-open and camera-open call sites to pull
the Video Processor MFT into the pipeline.

Also stopped ReadNextVideoFrame from assuming the negotiated RGB32 buffer
is tightly packed at width * 4: now reads MF_MT_DEFAULT_STRIDE off the
negotiated media type and handles a negative (bottom-up) stride.

parsed_message.title: Windows: implement RemoveBgNode background removal via ONNX Runtime + DirectML
parsed_message.description: Windows: implement RemoveBgNode background removal via ONNX Runtime + DirectML
parsed_message.body:
Platform::SubjectMask on Windows was a stub that always returned false.
Implements it using the bundled u2netp salient-object model (Apache-2.0,
assets/models/u2netp.onnx) run through ONNX Runtime with the DirectML
execution provider, falling back to ORT's CPU EP if DML registration or
inference fails - there is no Vision equivalent on Windows to lean on
instead. Person mode maps to the same general-purpose model rather than
returning false, since a dedicated person-segmentation model isn't worth
the extra machinery for this feature.
ONNX Runtime + DirectML are fetched at configure time as NuGet package
zips (Microsoft.ML.OnnxRuntime.DirectML for the DML-enabled
onnxruntime.dll/headers, Microsoft.AI.DirectML for the DirectML.dll
redistributable it dynamically loads) rather than built from source or
taken from the plain GitHub release zip, which lacks DirectML support.
package.ps1 and the CI workflow now stage both DLLs and the model file
next to Infinite.exe, and the Windows headless CI run now also exercises
INFINITE_REMOVEBGTEST end-to-end (CPU EP only, since the runners have no
GPU) as a real check that the bundled model loads and infers correctly,
not just that the code compiles.

parsed_message.title: RemoveBgNode: move mask computation to a worker thread
parsed_message.description: RemoveBgNode: move mask computation to a worker thread
parsed_message.body:
Segmentation is far too slow to run on the render thread, and the Windows
ONNX path landing next will be materially slower than Vision - synchronous
computation would freeze the UI for hundreds of ms per mask.
Adds a latest-only request queue (one pending FrameRequest slot, not a
deque) on a lazily-started worker std::thread, mirroring SampleScanner's
"main-thread-owned background work" shape. A completed result carries the
mask paired with a copy of the source pixels it was computed from (matched
by a monotonic serial), and CookIfNeeded composites the mask exclusively
against that paired frame rather than the live current one, so a moving
subject never tears against a mask computed several frames ago.
Also adds INFINITE_REMOVEBGTEST: a headless fixture (exits before
glfwInit, like PLUGINSCANTEST) that feeds a synthetic shaded blob through
Platform::SubjectMask directly and checks the mask lands on the right side
of the midpoint inside vs. outside the shape - weak by design, catches an
inverted/transposed mask without asserting model quality. Wired into
run-infinite-hygiene's driver.sh.

parsed_message.description: Add shared sort+filter strip to all four browser panel modes
parsed_message.body:
Replaces the four hand-rolled search-only boxes (Modules, Samples, Media,
Plugins) with a shared DrawBrowserFilterStrip: search + sort dropdown +
ascending/descending toggle + type filter, each mode keeping its own
BrowserFilterState so switching tabs preserves in-progress query/sort/filter
per mode.
Sorting and filtering happen inside each mode's existing cache
(LibraryFilterCache extended with sort/filter keys, new PluginFilterCache)
so ImGuiListClipper keeps getting a stable, pre-sorted row list rather than
re-filtering thousands of entries every frame. FilterAndSortSampleEntries
and FilterAndSortPluginEntries are factored out as standalone functions so
the new INFINITE_BROWSERSORTTEST fixture exercises the same logic the UI
calls, not a reimplementation.
State persists across restarts via a flat Infinite.browserfilters file,
mirroring CategoryColors's theme persistence.

parsed_message.title: Replace glReadPixels with async triple-buffered PBO readback
parsed_message.description: Replace glReadPixels with async triple-buffered PBO readback
parsed_message.body:
CaptureFrame's glReadPixels was a full GPU pipeline stall on every
recorded frame - the driver blocks the render thread until pending
work drains before pixels are readable. Swapped it for a ring of
three pixel pack buffers: glReadPixels into a PBO (client memory
untouched, so this issues async) with a fence, and a separate
non-blocking (zero-timeout) poll each frame that maps and consumes
whichever earlier PBO's fence has signaled, handing that frame to the
encoder queue. StopRecording flush-drains remaining in-flight PBOs
with a bounded wait rather than dropping them.
Also adds INFINITE_RECTEARDOWNTEST, exercising both teardown paths
(deleting the Output node mid-recording, and window-close/destructor
mid-recording) to confirm neither crashes/hangs on the encoder join
nor leaks a PBO.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

parsed_message.title: Move video encoding off the render thread onto a worker queue
parsed_message.description: Move video encoding off the render thread onto a worker queue
parsed_message.body:
AVAssetWriter/Media Foundation appends were happening synchronously on
the render thread inside CaptureFrame, stalling every recorded frame
on encoder throughput. RecorderStart now spawns a dedicated worker
thread per platform that drains a bounded, pooled append queue;
RecorderAppend hands off (dropping under backpressure rather than
blocking), and RecorderStop drains and joins that worker before
reporting final frame/dropped counts - reading counts before the join
raced the worker's last writes, so RecorderStop now returns them
directly via out-params instead of callers sampling them separately.
Pending/dropped counts are surfaced in the recording UI.
Also fixes InspectMovie's frame counting on macOS, which used
AVAssetReader passthrough (compressed NALUs) instead of forcing
decode - passthrough buffers don't map 1:1 onto displayed H.264
frames, so the reported count drifted from what ffprobe/actual
playback shows.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

parsed_message.title: Add instance-domain selection (Select/Delete/Transform on scattered instances)
parsed_message.description: Add instance-domain selection (Select/Delete/Transform on scattered instances)
parsed_message.body:
Full slice per local-prompts/instance-selection.md Part 1, steps 1-5:
1. IGeometrySource gains InstanceSelection()/InstanceSelectionRevision()/
InstanceTransformOverride(), forwarded by every node overriding
PassthroughSource() (GeometryOpNode, DisplacementNode, SetColorNode,
WrapNode, MergeByDistanceNode, Null3DNode, MaterialNode, Switcher3DNode -
the 8 confirmed by both grep and geometry-transform-sweep's own
"Instancing passthrough sweep" list).
2. GeometryOpNode::GetMesh()'s kSelect case, when WrapsInstancer(input),
leaves the stamp mesh untouched and masks instance placements instead -
all six modes (All/Index/Axis/Normal/Random/Radius) mirrored from
MeshOps::Select, substituting instance translation/local-Y for face
centre/normal. selectInvert/selectAppend/selectSeed behave the same.
3. kDelete and kTransform, with selectionOnly on and WrapsInstancer(input),
publish an edited transform list via InstanceTransformOverride() instead
of touching the stamp. GetInstanceGroupMatrix() backs off to the upstream
matrix unchanged when selectionOnly is on, so a Transform's move isn't
applied twice (once per masked instance, once to the whole group) -
documented at its call site in GeometryOpNodes.cpp.
4. Draw-path consumers (Geometry3DNodes.cpp's instanced upload + scene
signature, NodeViewport.cpp's instanced draw + reframing) now resolve the
first non-null InstanceTransformOverride() along the chain instead of
reading the raw instancer directly, via a small ResolveInstanceTransforms/
ResolveInstanceSelection helper added in each file (not lifted into a
shared header - the two draw paths' surrounding state differs enough that
a shared helper would need an awkward extra parameter or a virtual hook
for no real gain). Cache-invalidation gates: GeometryOpNode's own
MeshRevision() already bumps on every instance-domain rebuild
(GetMesh() stamps NextMeshRevision() unconditionally), so it alone gates
BuildSceneSignature's meshRev; the two GPU-upload sites additionally gate
on that same revision (Geometry3DNodes.h's GpuMesh::instanceOverrideRevision,
NodeViewport.h's mInstanceOverrideRevision) since their own instanceRevision/
instanceGroupMatrix comparisons don't otherwise know an override changed.
GeometryOpNode::Signature also gained upstreamInstanceRevision (the raw
instancer's InstanceRevision()) so a Select/Delete/Transform sitting on
an instancer correctly rebuilds when the scatter itself changes -
InstanceOnPointsNode::MeshRevision() only reflects the stamp shape, not
mInstanceRevision, which upstreamRevision alone would have missed.
5. Selection overlay fallback in NodeViewport.cpp: when mesh.faceMask is
empty but InstanceSelection() has a mask, mSelIbo holds the *whole* stamp
(not a faceMask-filtered subset) and is drawn instanced over only the
selected instances' transforms, filtered into a new mSelInstanceOverrideVbo
each redraw - whole instances tint, not per-face. Chose this over the
per-instance aSelected-attribute route: no shader changes, reuses Part 0's
instanced-selection plumbing directly, and this whole block only runs on
an actual redraw already, so rebuilding the filtered buffer every entry
costs nothing extra.
Added INFINITE_INSTANCESELECTTEST: scatters a cube stamp over a sphere's
vertices, Select-by-radius centred on a point on the sphere's surface (an
icosphere's own centre would make every vertex equidistant, so it can't
produce a genuine partial split), and asserts the mask is nonempty, strictly
between 0 and the instance count, byte-stable across an unrelated re-cook,
and that the stamp mesh itself stays untouched (faceMask still empty).
Registered in run-infinite-hygiene's driver.sh as INSTANCESELECTTEST:10.
Verified: geometry-transform-sweep and run-infinite-hygiene (full build,
not --skip-build) both pass, including PHASE4TEST (unaffected - it only
exercises the mesh/face-domain selectionOnly path) and the new
INSTANCESELECTTEST. HIDETEST remains the sole pre-existing failure
(unrelated link-loss bug found and separately tracked before this work -
see task_2b3340fb / the Part 0 commit).
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

parsed_message.title: Fix instancing collapsing behind passthrough nodes, and dropped group matrix
parsed_message.description: Fix instancing collapsing behind passthrough nodes, and dropped group matrix
bullets: Null3D, Displacement and Wrap forwarded every other side-channel but not
Material, Set Color, Merge by Distance and Switcher 3D implemented
parsed_message.body:
InstanceOnPointsNode returns the single stamp mesh from GetMesh() and carries
its N placements separately, so consumers walk PassthroughSource() to find the
instancer and read GetInstanceGroupMatrix() to pick up a wrapping Transform's
rigid move. Two halves of that contract were being dropped:
PassthroughSource(), so patching any of them after an Instance on Points
drew one stamp instead of N instances, with no error anywhere. Null 3D is
the clearest case - a node whose whole job is to be a no-op passthrough was
destroying the instancing it passed through.
PassthroughSource() without GetInstanceGroupMatrix(), so
Instance on Points -> Transform -> Material -> Render 3D found the instancer
but read an identity group matrix and drew the scatter back at the origin.
Both accessors now travel together on all seven nodes; Wrap forwards from
sourceInput (the stamp being wrapped), Switcher 3D from the same Active() slot
its PassthroughSource() returns so the two can't disagree.
Adds INSTANCESWEEPTEST, a fifth generic sweep in geometry-transform-sweep, so
this stays enforced as new geometry nodes are added rather than re-checked by
hand. Verified it fails on each of the two dropped overrides before the fix.
No revision plumbing needed: both consumers already compare the group matrix
directly (Geometry3DNodes.cpp, NodeViewport.cpp).

  drew one stamp instead of N instances, with no error anywhere. Null 3D is
  the clearest case - a node whose whole job is to be a no-op passthrough was
  destroying the instancing it passed through.
- Material, Set Color, Merge by Distance and Switcher 3D implemented
  PassthroughSource() without GetInstanceGroupMatrix(), so
  Instance on Points -> Transform -> Material -> Render 3D found the instancer
  but read an identity group matrix and drew the scatter back at the origin.

Both accessors now travel together on all seven nodes; Wrap forwards from
sourceInput (the stamp being wrapped), Switcher 3D from the same Active() slot
its PassthroughSource() returns so the two can't disagree.

Adds INSTANCESWEEPTEST, a fifth generic sweep in geometry-transform-sweep, so
this stays enforced as new geometry nodes are added rather than re-checked by
hand. Verified it fails on each of the two dropped overrides before the fix.
No revision plumbing needed: both consumers already compare the group matrix
directly (Geometry3DNodes.cpp, NodeViewport.cpp).

parsed_message.title: Fix reverse video playback frame-rate collapse
parsed_message.description: Fix reverse video playback frame-rate collapse
parsed_message.body:
mPosition was never wrapped/clamped for negative speed, so it walked
past 0 forever — on macOS that meant tearing down and rebuilding the
AVAssetReader every frame while producing only frame 0; on Windows the
reader just stopped updating once position went negative.
Now mPosition wraps (loop) or clamps (no loop) on both sides. On
macOS, backward seeks target the requested time instead of always
restarting the reader at t=0, and the last few dozen decoded frames
are kept in a byte-capped cache so steady reverse playback pays for a
reader rebuild roughly once per cache window instead of once per
frame. Windows already seeks to the target rather than zero, so it's
left as-is.

parsed_message.title: Fix Geometry Table grid pins: only the last-drawn cell was draggable
parsed_message.description: Fix Geometry Table grid pins: only the last-drawn cell was draggable
parsed_message.body:
ed::BeginPin()/EndPin() derive a pin's hit bounds from the enclosing
ImGui group's bounding box, anchored at the cursor position from before
BeginPin() and grown via the window's monotonic CursorMaxPos. The grid
jumps the cursor to each cell's absolute position via SetCursorScreenPos
without ever advancing the real layout cursor, so each successive pin's
group-derived bounds ballooned to include every prior cell - only the
last cell (bottom-right) ended up with bounds covering the whole grid,
so every drag started from it regardless of which cell was clicked.
Use ed::PinRect() to set each pin's bounds explicitly instead.

imgui-node-editor's group hit-region list is narrowed from the 8 edge/
corner regions + Header to just Header + Center, which removes the
resize handles/cursor (auto-fit would overwrite a manual resize the
next frame anyway) and makes the box's empty interior draggable, so the
whole group moves from anywhere inside it, not just the header.
Fixes #11.

parsed_message.description: Preserve connections through copy/paste and duplicate (Cmd/Ctrl+D)
parsed_message.body:
Cmd+C/Cmd+V and Shift+D previously copied nodes and params but dropped
every cable. Captures plain input-slot links (from gLinks), modulator
bindings (from Modulation::Instance().Links()), and palette bindings
(from PaletteBinding::Instance().Links()) for the copied cluster at
copy/duplicate time, then rewires them onto the fresh copies: internal
links reconnect copy-to-copy, external inbound sources stay wired to
the copy, and outbound-only links are left alone. Also binds Cmd/Ctrl+D
as a duplicate alias alongside Shift+D.
Fixes #13.

parsed_message.title: Bound modulation writes to a per-binding lo/hi range
parsed_message.description: Bound modulation writes to a per-binding lo/hi range
parsed_message.body:
Adds Modulation::Source::lo/hi, SetRange(), and ResolvedSourceFor() so a
binding writes into an explicit range in the destination's own units
instead of always overriding the full span. Legacy polarity/depth/centre
bindings convert to an equivalent lo/hi lazily, the first time their
destination param actually draws a frame (EnsureRange can't run at load
time since the destination's declared min/max aren't known yet).
Persists lo/hi through both the text and JSON patch formats, appended as
trailing optional tokens so older patches still decode correctly.

parsed_message.title: Schedule the WASAPI render thread with MMCSS
parsed_message.description: Schedule the WASAPI render thread with MMCSS
parsed_message.body:
RenderThreadMain ran as a plain std::thread at ordinary priority, so the
Windows scheduler was free to preempt it in favour of anything else on the
machine - including our own UI thread compiling a shader, or a plugin scan.
Every preemption outlasting the buffer deadline is an audible click, since
WASAPI plays whatever is in the buffer whether we filled it or not.
macOS has never needed an equivalent because CoreAudio calls the render
callback on its own HAL I/O thread, which the kernel has already granted
time-constraint scheduling. On Windows that guarantee is opt-in, and nothing
was opting in.

lifetime, via RAII - the function has an early return on setup failure as
well as its normal exit, so a paired call would leak the registration on the
failure path. Falls back to "Audio", then to doing nothing: MMCSS is a
service and can be disabled, and unprioritised audio still plays.
Not verifiable in CI - the runners have no audio device - so this is
compile-checked only. The glitch-under-load improvement needs a real Windows
machine to confirm.

parsed_message.title: Give main()'s frame loop its own function to clear the x64 codegen ICE
parsed_message.description: Give main()'s frame loop its own function to clear the x64 codegen ICE
parsed_message.body:
The internal compiler error was never about flags. main() is ~12k lines and
its GLFW frame loop accounts for ~10.1k of them, so MSVC's x64 backend was
being asked to generate code for one enormous function body. That is why
/Ob1 changed nothing - the size is intrinsic, not from inlining - and why
ARM64, with a different backend, compiled the identical source.
The loop body is now a lambda invoked by the loop, which gives it its own
function without editing a line inside it: everything main() declared above
is captured by reference. Safe to do mechanically here because the body has
no top-level continue/break, and all 51 of its `return`s belong to nested
lambdas rather than exiting main - both checked before the change.
This replaces the per-file /Od workaround, which would have shipped Windows
users an unoptimised UI frame loop. Optimisation stays on everywhere.

parsed_message.title: Disable MSVC compile batching to dodge the x64 codegen ICE
parsed_message.description: Disable MSVC compile batching to dodge the x64 codegen ICE
parsed_message.body:
The Visual Studio generator batches every source in a target into one
cl.exe call, ending in a combined "Generating Code..." pass. On x64 that
pass died with an internal compiler error - no C1001, no source line,
just RaiseException frames - so it was neither fixable nor attributable.
ARM64 compiled the identical sources fine, and forcing a serial build
(/maxcpucount:1) ruled out memory pressure: it's a genuine ICE.
CMAKE_VS_NO_COMPILE_BATCHING gives one cl.exe per translation unit. That
removes the batched codegen pass the ICE lives in, and if anything does
crash in future it now names its own .cpp.

parsed_message.title: Replace NetCompat's close() macro with NetClose(), fixing an MSVC ICE
parsed_message.description: Replace NetCompat's close() macro with NetClose(), fixing an MSVC ICE
parsed_message.body:
`#define close(fd) closesocket(fd)` in a header is an unscoped macro named
close, and RemoteControl.cpp includes NetCompat.h (line 3) then <fstream>
(line 7). The macro therefore rewrites basic_filebuf::close()'s declarations
in that one TU while every other TU in the same MSVC codegen batch sees the
real ones.
Symptom on the x64 runner: twelve C4003 "not enough arguments for
function-like macro invocation 'close'" warnings pointed at <fstream> and
__msvc_filebuf.hpp, then
Generating Code...
CL!RaiseException()+0x6c
CL!InvokeCompilerPassW()+0x12548b
error MSB6006: "CL.exe" exited with code -529706956.
i.e. an internal compiler error in the optimizer, not a diagnosable error in
our code. macOS never saw it: the POSIX branch of the header has no macro.
Replaced with an inline NetCompat::NetClose() alongside the existing
NetRecv/NetSend/NetSendTo/NetSetSockOpt shims, and updated all six call
sites (three in RemoteControl.cpp, three in OscNodes.cpp). SHUT_RDWR stays a
macro - it is a constant, not a name anything else declares.
This was already filed as 1.10.6 in docs/WINDOWS_VERIFICATION.md, noted as
compiling "today" but a landmine for the first TU to touch an fstream. It
turned out that TU already existed.
macOS: build clean, DSPTEST OK exit 0.

parsed_message.raw:
Windows: stop a failed audio-device open from calling std::terminate()

RenderState::Stop() decided whether to join the render thread from the
`running` flag, but the render thread clears that flag itself when WASAPI
setup fails (non-float mix format, >8 channels, an endpoint another app holds
in exclusive mode, any Activate/Initialize failure). Stop() then took its
early-return branch, closed the two event handles and returned WITHOUT
joining - leaving a joinable std::thread.

From there the process died two ways, both silent:
  - picking another device: `gRender.thread = std::thread(...)` move-assigns
    over a joinable thread, which calls std::terminate()
  - quitting: ~RenderState() -> Stop() -> same early return -> ~thread on a
    joinable thread, same result

So one failed device open was enough to abort on quit, and a second attempt
aborted immediately. No dialog, no log.

Stop() is now a single unconditional path with the join gated only on
joinable() - the shape CaptureEngineBase::Stop() in the same file always had.

Two related fixes on the same path:
  - the open poll loop guarded on !thread.joinable() to detect "the thread
    died", which can never be true (joinable() stays true until join or
    detach), so every failed open stalled the caller for the full 4000 ms.
    Replaced with a setupDone atomic the render thread latches on both the
    success and failure paths.
  - dropped the dead `|| !SUCCEEDED(0)` (always false) and the redundant
    re-test of the same null pointer inside its body.

Documented as 1.2 in docs/WINDOWS_VERIFICATION.md. Windows-only code, so CI
is the compiler.

parsed_message.title: Fix PortableFft::Inverse, port Molder off Accelerate, Windows icon and .infinite
parsed_message.description: Fix PortableFft::Inverse, port Molder off Accelerate, Windows icon and .infinite
bullets: RunCore built its twiddles at a negative angle and used them
Inverse passed mRe/mIm as RunCore's own input while RunCore writes them
Scaling was also wrong in a way the class comment documented backwards.
parsed_message.body:
Four things, all needed before a Windows build can ship anything current.
PortableFft::Inverse was not the inverse of Forward (two defects):
unconditionally, so Inverse ran the FORWARD kernel over a Hermitian-
mirrored spectrum and returned the input TIME-REVERSED. Now takes an
`inverse` flag that conjugates the twiddles.
through a non-identity permutation, corrupting the data. Now stages into
mStageRe/mStageIm, sized in Prepare() so the class stays allocation-free
on the audio thread.
PaulStretchNode's normScale = 1/(N*1.5) is SHARED by both backends, so
Inverse has to match vDSP_fft_zrip(FFT_INVERSE) exactly: unnormalised,
yielding N*x. Dropped the stray 0.5 and the 1/N, and corrected the
contract comment.
Verified against Accelerate at N = 32..16384: forward and inverse now both
match vDSP to 2.1e-07 worst relative error.
Added RunPortableFftFixture to RunDspTest (INFINITE_DSPTEST, exit-code gated,
runs headless in CI on BOTH platforms so macOS gates the Windows backend).
It asserts Forward's x2 zrip packing via a DC probe and the N*x round trip,
and names the time-reversal case explicitly. Confirmed it fails (exit 1) when
the twiddle bug is reintroduced - a regression test that cannot see the
regression is worthless.
MolderDsp.cpp arrived from main with an unfenced <Accelerate/Accelerate.h> in
the SHARED source list, so it could not compile on Windows at all - and it
needs a working inverse transform, which is why the above had to come first.
All vDSP use was confined to FftContext; PortableFft's Forward/Inverse are
drop-ins for those exact ctoz/zrip/ztoc pairs, so the surrounding maths is
untouched and the Apple path is byte-identical.
Patches now save as .infinite on Windows. ".inf" is RESERVED there for Setup
Information files, so a saved patch showed up as "Setup Information", took the

parsed_message.raw:
Fix PortableFft::Inverse, port Molder off Accelerate, Windows icon and .infinite

Four things, all needed before a Windows build can ship anything current.

PortableFft::Inverse was not the inverse of Forward (two defects):
  - RunCore built its twiddles at a negative angle and used them
    unconditionally, so Inverse ran the FORWARD kernel over a Hermitian-
    mirrored spectrum and returned the input TIME-REVERSED. Now takes an
    `inverse` flag that conjugates the twiddles.
  - Inverse passed mRe/mIm as RunCore's own input while RunCore writes them
    through a non-identity permutation, corrupting the data. Now stages into
    mStageRe/mStageIm, sized in Prepare() so the class stays allocation-free
    on the audio thread.
  - Scaling was also wrong in a way the class comment documented backwards.
    PaulStretchNode's normScale = 1/(N*1.5) is SHARED by both backends, so
    Inverse has to match vDSP_fft_zrip(FFT_INVERSE) exactly: unnormalised,
    yielding N*x. Dropped the stray 0.5 and the 1/N, and corrected the
    contract comment.

Verified against Accelerate at N = 32..16384: forward and inverse now both
match vDSP to 2.1e-07 worst relative error.

Added RunPortableFftFixture to RunDspTest (INFINITE_DSPTEST, exit-code gated,
runs headless in CI on BOTH platforms so macOS gates the Windows backend).
It asserts Forward's x2 zrip packing via a DC probe and the N*x round trip,
and names the time-reversal case explicitly. Confirmed it fails (exit 1) when
the twiddle bug is reintroduced - a regression test that cannot see the
regression is worthless.

MolderDsp.cpp arrived from main with an unfenced <Accelerate/Accelerate.h> in
the SHARED source list, so it could not compile on Windows at all - and it
needs a working inverse transform, which is why the above had to come first.
All vDSP use was confined to FftContext; PortableFft's Forward/Inverse are
drop-ins for those exact ctoz/zrip/ztoc pairs, so the surrounding maths is
untouched and the Apple path is byte-identical.

Patches now save as .infinite on Windows. ".inf" is RESERVED there for Setup
Information files, so a saved patch showed up as "Setup Information", took the
OS setup icon, and double-clicking handed it to the installer machinery. That
association belongs to the system and must not be hijacked. Both extensions
are still accepted when opening, so patches stay portable both ways; only the
default for new saves differs. Also fixed the basename split to accept
backslashes.

Added src/platform/win/Infinite.rc: app icon (generated from the existing
assets/Infinite.iconset, all seven Explorer sizes down to 16px so list views
are not badly downscaled) plus a VERSIONINFO block, since an unsigned exe with
no version info looks maximally anonymous to SmartScreen.

macOS verified unchanged: DSPTEST OK exit 0, and AUDIOPARAMSWEEPTEST's failure
set is byte-identical to origin/main's (359 lines both, empty diff both ways).

parsed_message.title: Link the MSVC runtime statically so Infinite.exe runs on a clean Windows
parsed_message.description: Link the MSVC runtime statically so Infinite.exe runs on a clean Windows
parsed_message.body:
The Windows artifact failed at launch on a stock Windows image with
The code execution cannot proceed because MSVCP140.dll was not found.
MSVC defaults to the dynamic CRT, so the exe imported MSVCP140.dll and
VCRUNTIME140.dll from the Visual C++ redistributable. package.ps1's header
and the README both already claimed the build was self-contained; it wasn't.
Set CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY to MultiThreaded before the FetchContent
calls, so glfw, libFLAC and Infinite all agree on the static CRT - they have
to agree or the link fails on mismatched RuntimeLibrary.
The build and every headless test passed with the old linkage, because the
CI runner has Visual Studio installed and therefore has the DLLs. So add a
gate that scans the shipped exe's import table for MSVCP140/VCRUNTIME140 and
fails the job if they reappear. Byte-scanning the PE avoids needing a dev
shell and works on both architectures.
Documented as 1.11, and corrected the Part 2 instructions, which repeated the
same false self-containment claim.

parsed_message.raw:
Windows handoff: eight more defects, drop the manual checklist

Second review pass over src/platform/win. New confirmed defects, all found
by reading and none visible to a build:

  - a failed audio-device open leaves a joinable std::thread that Stop()
    never joins, so reopening or quitting calls std::terminate()
  - HandleShortMessage switches on (status & 0xF0), so the 0xF8/0xFA/0xFC
    MIDI clock cases are unreachable - clock sync never works
  - the text cap-height probe passes GGO_GLYPH_INDEX with L'H', measuring
    glyph 72 rather than the letter, so all text is mis-scaled
  - the analyser's low/mid/high use band indices that resolve to different
    Hz ranges than Platform.mm's, and skip its shaping/smoothing
  - Media Foundation stride is hardcoded to width*4 in the decoder and the
    camera; MF_MT_DEFAULT_STRIDE is never read
  - the MIDI note ring is single-producer but MidiStart opens every device,
    and WinMM gives each one its own callback thread
  - a function-local static vector is shared by both capture threads, and
    CaptureTapEngine::OnFormat publishes readiness before it allocates the
    ring the audio thread reads

Plus smaller items: positional (unstable) audio device ids, the unscoped
close() macro in NetCompat.h, HOME-before-USERPROFILE in AppPaths, and the
STA/MTA apartment disagreement between the win TUs.

Also proposes a second headless fixture: GetTextOutlines needs no GL
context, so a cap-height assertion can gate 1.4 in CI the way the FFT
round-trip assertion gates 1.1.

Dropped Part 2's manual hardware checklist - that is the contributor's call
on their own machine, not something to script for them. Parallels notes
renumbered to Part 2.

parsed_message.raw:
Port the whole app to Windows (WASAPI/WinMM/Media Foundation/GDI+)

Every Apple framework is now swapped for a Windows equivalent behind the
same src/platform/Platform.h facade, so both platforms compile from one
source tree selected by CMake:

- Audio: WASAPI shared-mode render/capture + WinMM MIDI replace
  CoreAudio/CoreMIDI; analyser, input tap, and config-change recovery
  reimplemented against MMDevice notifications.
- Media: Media Foundation replaces AVFoundation - source-reader video
  decode with seek, camera capture on a pump thread, and H.264+AAC MP4
  recording via sink writer.
- Decode: stb_image/tinyexr (+ vendored miniz), dr_wav/dr_mp3/dr_flac
  and a hand-rolled AIFF parser replace ImageIO and the audio asset
  pipeline; OBJ/PLY/STL importers replace ModelIO.
- Text: GDI+ GraphicsPath rasterization matches the CoreText fill /
  stroke / stroke-only triad; font enumeration via EnumFontFamilies.
- Plugins/Syphon/Vision: AU hosting reports unavailable (VST3 stays an
  Apple-only opt-in), Syphon and Remove Background nodes degrade
  gracefully like the rest of the stub surface.
- vDSP: two FFT nodes move to a shared PortableFft fallback.
- Build: CMakeLists restructured for per-platform source sets, glad GL
  loader for non-Apple contexts, libFLAC fetched for FLAC writing
  (dr_libs is decode-only); package.ps1 stages a Windows dist folder.

Verified on Windows 11 / MSVC: clean Release build, INFINITE_DSPTEST and
INFINITE_AUDIOPDCTEST pass, app launches with a live window.

parsed_message.title: Fix modulator cables being dropped by undo, redo and patch load
parsed_message.description: Fix modulator cables being dropped by undo, redo and patch load
bullets: one undo anywhere on the canvas detached the cable, and the same hole
parsed_message.body:
Modulator-into-modulator connections (Random -> Range to Range's `in`,
and every other node exposing a ModulatorInputSlot) are raw IModulator*
pointers rather than ImageCables, so restoring them goes through
ConnectGeometrySlot. That function only knew how to re-seat MathNode's
two pins, so every other modulator input cable was written into the
snapshot by BuildPatchData and then silently dropped on the way back in
hit redo and opening a saved patch.
Replaces the MathNode special case with the generic
ModulatorInputSlot() accessor the live drag-to-connect path already
uses, and threads the source output index through: BuildPatchData knew
which output of a multi-output modulator was wired but discarded it, so
even MathNode's restored cables snapped back to output 0.
Affects 11 node types: Math, Compare, Range to Range, Smoothing,
Invert, Mod Depth, Mod Curve, CV to Pitch, Null Modulator, Envelope,
OSC Send.
INFINITE_UNDOTEST grows a registry-wide sweep rather than a
hand-written fixture, so a new modulator-input node cannot quietly
reintroduce the hole: 11 types swept, 0 lost with the fix, 11 lost
without it.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
parsed_message.raw:
Fix modulator cables being dropped by undo, redo and patch load

Modulator-into-modulator connections (Random -> Range to Range's `in`,
and every other node exposing a ModulatorInputSlot) are raw IModulator*
pointers rather than ImageCables, so restoring them goes through
ConnectGeometrySlot. That function only knew how to re-seat MathNode's
two pins, so every other modulator input cable was written into the
snapshot by BuildPatchData and then silently dropped on the way back in
- one undo anywhere on the canvas detached the cable, and the same hole
hit redo and opening a saved patch.

Replaces the MathNode special case with the generic
ModulatorInputSlot() accessor the live drag-to-connect path already
uses, and threads the source output index through: BuildPatchData knew
which output of a multi-output modulator was wired but discarded it, so
even MathNode's restored cables snapped back to output 0.

Affects 11 node types: Math, Compare, Range to Range, Smoothing,
Invert, Mod Depth, Mod Curve, CV to Pitch, Null Modulator, Envelope,
OSC Send.

INFINITE_UNDOTEST grows a registry-wide sweep rather than a
hand-written fixture, so a new modulator-input node cannot quietly
reintroduce the hole: 11 types swept, 0 lost with the fix, 11 lost
without it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

parsed_message.title: Add tempo sync and mute-dry to Note Echo
parsed_message.description: Add tempo sync and mute-dry to Note Echo
parsed_message.body:
Note Echo's spacing was a flat millisecond knob with no way to lock
to tempo, unlike every other rhythmic note node (Arpeggiator, Note
Sequencer, Random Note Generator) and unlike Ableton's own Max for
Live Note Echo device, which syncs its delay to a beat division by
default. Add the same rateMode/rateBeats/rateSeconds split those
nodes already use, defaulting to free mode so existing patches sound
unchanged. Also add muteDry, matching Ableton's Input Thru/Mute
switch, so the dry note can be swallowed without a downstream mute
node. Tightened the node body to a narrow 2-knob-per-row layout.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

parsed_message.title: Guard New/Open/Open Recent/drag-drop behind unsaved-changes modal
parsed_message.description: Guard New/Open/Open Recent/drag-drop behind unsaved-changes modal
parsed_message.body:
Save/Save As and window close already checked gPatchDirty before
discarding the current patch, but New, Open, Open Recent, and dropping
an .inf file on the canvas called NewPatch()/LoadPatchFrom() directly,
silently destroying unsaved work with no undo escape hatch afterward.
Generalizes the close-only guard into GuardUnsavedChanges(action), which
runs the action immediately on a clean patch or defers it behind the
existing "Unsaved Changes" modal (Save/Don't Save/Cancel) otherwise, and
routes all five call sites (menu + Cmd+N/Cmd+O shortcuts + Open Recent +
drag-drop) through it.
Fixes #6.

parsed_message.title: Add real CoreAudio processor-overload listener for xrun detection
parsed_message.description: Add real CoreAudio processor-overload listener for xrun detection
parsed_message.body:
AudioEngine::Process's xrun count was purely a wall-clock heuristic
(AVAudioSourceNode gives no direct xrun signal). AudioDeviceOpen already
resolves the real output AudioObjectID but discarded it. Retain it on
AudioDeviceHandle and register a kAudioDeviceProcessorOverload property
listener that feeds genuine overload notifications into the same
mXrunCount the heuristic uses, removed before teardown with the same
lifecycle discipline as configChangeObserver. Kept alongside, not instead
of, the heuristic - each catches dropout classes the other can miss.
Fixes #3

snapped to Transport's key/scale, unlike every other useGlobalScale

is already diatonic to Transport's C-major default, so snapping is a

parsed_message.description: Fix PHASEFTEST's stale ShapeNode.size usage
parsed_message.body:
aa0462a split ShapeNode's single `size` field into sizeX/sizeY (uSize
is now a vec2 in the shader) and `size` itself became dead - read
nowhere in CookIfNeeded any more. PHASEFTEST's image-to-points fixture
still set only `circle.size = 0.25f`, so the circle actually rendered
at the sizeX/sizeY defaults (0.35 radius, ~38.5% coverage) instead of
the intended 0.25 (19.6%), producing the reported 35.1%-vs-19.6%
mismatch. The shape/point-sampling code never regressed; only the
fixture's setup was stale. Sets sizeX/sizeY directly instead.

parsed_message.title: Suppress Dock icon in VST3 scan child process, sync AU init
parsed_message.description: Suppress Dock icon in VST3 scan child process, sync AU init
parsed_message.body:
Each --vst3-scan-bundle re-exec previously let AppKit lazily create a
default-policy shared application as soon as a scanned plugin's Cocoa
editor classes touched NSApplication during static init, so the child
showed up as its own visible Infinite instance in the Dock - hitting
this for every bundle in a large VST3 folder is what produces dozens
of stray icons during a Rescan. SuppressAppUIForScanChild() claims the
shared-application singleton with a Prohibited activation policy
before any plugin code runs, so the child never becomes visible.
Also switches AU instantiation from the async completion-handler API
to the synchronous initializer, since the async variant's "arbitrary
queue" callback let some plugins' Qt-based init code run off the main
thread (observed: Native Instruments Massive X/Pigments hitting a
dispatch_assert_queue trap).
WIP: written but not yet built/tested on this machine.

parsed_message.title: Marshal VST3 processor<->controller messages onto the main thread
parsed_message.description: Marshal VST3 processor<->controller messages onto the main thread
parsed_message.body:
compCP/ctrlCP were wired directly together, so a notify() sent by the
processor (e.g. pushing state to its own GUI mid-process()) landed on the
edit controller on whichever thread sent it - the audio thread, in that
case.
Adds a hand-written connection proxy (HostConnectionProxy) inserted between
the two real IConnectionPoints each way, so notify() calls get marshaled
onto the main thread via dispatch_async before reaching the real peer.
This is deliberately not the SDK's public.sdk/source/vst/hosting/
connectionproxy.cpp compiled in as-is: its ConnectionProxy::notify() only
compares the calling thread against whichever thread constructed the proxy
(via ThreadChecker) and silently drops the message on a mismatch - it does
not queue or hop threads by itself, which is exactly the missing piece
here. A thin wrapper wouldn't have been meaningfully simpler than writing
the real thing, so this hand-rolls the same interface with an actual
dispatch hop, matching how the rest of this file's host-side objects
(HostApplication, MemoryStream, HostEventList) are already implemented.
Separate commit from the prior fix (message passing / IPlugFrame / editor
teardown) because this one changes threading behavior; those did not.

parsed_message.title: Fix VST3 host-side spec violations: message passing, resizable GUIs, editor teardown
parsed_message.description: Fix VST3 host-side spec violations: message passing, resizable GUIs, editor teardown
bullets: IHostApplication::createInstance was a stub returning kNoInterface
IPlugFrame was never implemented and plugView->setFrame() was never
The editor's plugView->removed() was only ever called from
parsed_message.body:
Serum2/Pigments crash Infinite as VST3 but not AU because three host-side
spec requirements were unmet:
unconditionally, so ComponentBase::allocateMessage() always returned null.
This is the only channel for processor<->controller messaging beyond plain
parameters (wavetable/spectrum displays, voice counts, sample loading);
parameter-only effects never hit this path, which is why only big synths
broke. Implements IMessage/IAttributeList by hand, matching the reference
hostclasses.cpp semantics.
called, so a plugin with a resizable GUI (Serum2) had no host object to
ask for a resize.
PluginVST3Destroy, and even there it ran after the window had already
closed. A closed-but-not-removed editor leaves the plugin's GUI timer
armed against a view Infinite no longer considers open - the crash
report that started this investigation is a CFRunLoopTimer callback with
zero Infinite frames on the stack, exactly this shape. removed() now runs
first, while the container view is still alive, on the attached()-failure
path, on PluginVST3CloseEditor, and on PluginVST3Destroy; CloseEditor now
fully detaches instead of merely hiding the window.
IPlugFrame::iid and IPlugView::iid are defined in the SDK's
public.sdk/source/common/commoniids.cpp, now added to the VST3 source list.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
parsed_message.raw:
Fix VST3 host-side spec violations: message passing, resizable GUIs, editor teardown

Serum2/Pigments crash Infinite as VST3 but not AU because three host-side
spec requirements were unmet:

- IHostApplication::createInstance was a stub returning kNoInterface
  unconditionally, so ComponentBase::allocateMessage() always returned null.
  This is the only channel for processor<->controller messaging beyond plain
  parameters (wavetable/spectrum displays, voice counts, sample loading);
  parameter-only effects never hit this path, which is why only big synths
  broke. Implements IMessage/IAttributeList by hand, matching the reference
  hostclasses.cpp semantics.

- IPlugFrame was never implemented and plugView->setFrame() was never
  called, so a plugin with a resizable GUI (Serum2) had no host object to
  ask for a resize.

- The editor's plugView->removed() was only ever called from
  PluginVST3Destroy, and even there it ran after the window had already
  closed. A closed-but-not-removed editor leaves the plugin's GUI timer
  armed against a view Infinite no longer considers open - the crash
  report that started this investigation is a CFRunLoopTimer callback with
  zero Infinite frames on the stack, exactly this shape. removed() now runs
  first, while the container view is still alive, on the attached()-failure
  path, on PluginVST3CloseEditor, and on PluginVST3Destroy; CloseEditor now
  fully detaches instead of merely hiding the window.

IPlugFrame::iid and IPlugView::iid are defined in the SDK's
public.sdk/source/common/commoniids.cpp, now added to the VST3 source list.

Connection-point proxying (item 4 of the same investigation, which changes
threading behavior) is a separate commit.

parsed_message.description: Move Audio File playback into the real-time DSP graph
parsed_message.body:
Audio File was a plain INode with its own private AVAudioEngine, so its
cable could be dragged onto any audio-input pin (Audio Displacement, Mixer,
effects, Audio Out) and read as permanent silence there, while still being
audible through its own engine independent of the main audio engine's
start/stop state. Made AudioFileNode a real IAudioSource backed by a new

falling through to the generic v3 audio-node shell once it became an
IAudioSource (added the same IsAudioBodyNode carve-out AudioTextureNode already
has, so it keeps its own file-picker/transport/level UI).

parsed_message.title: Fix Finder double-click failing to open .inf patches
parsed_message.description: Fix Finder double-click failing to open .inf patches
parsed_message.body:
glfwInit() runs [NSApp run] internally, which drains the launch odoc
Apple Event and installs AppKit's own kAEOpenDocuments handler before
our document-open plumbing ever ran. Split InitDocumentHandling into a
pre-glfwInit step that injects the NSApplicationDelegate methods (so
AppKit's cached _delegateFlags are correct the first time) and a
post-glfwInit step that reinstalls the Apple Event handler AppKit
clobbered. Dedupe pending opens so a file isn't loaded twice if both
handlers fire for one launch, and fix the document icon key in
Info.plist.in to point at InfinitePatch.icns instead of the app icon.
Also includes pending WAV recording helpers, new color presets, and
node editor tweaks already in the working tree.

AppKit's cached _delegateFlags are correct the first time) and a
post-glfwInit step that reinstalls the Apple Event handler AppKit
clobbered. Dedupe pending opens so a file isn't loaded twice if both
handlers fire for one launch, and fix the document icon key in
Info.plist.in to point at InfinitePatch.icns instead of the app icon.

Also includes pending WAV recording helpers, new color presets, and
node editor tweaks already in the working tree.

parsed_message.raw:
Fix mobile CTA button sizing, clean up showcase window chrome, and rebuild tree-branch growth animation

- Shrink btn-lg padding/font on mobile so hero and download CTAs no longer read oversized
- Remove redundant title/FPS chip from the showcase window header
- Fix tree-branch animation getting stuck invisible on mobile: resize/ResizeObserver was
  firing repeatedly during scroll (address bar collapse etc) and resetting growth to 0%
  every time; now only rebuilds when size actually changes
- Redraw branches as directed paths with twig offshoots instead of a runaway recursive
  fork, so the shape reads as branches rather than a tangle
- Replace the particle-cloud capability animation with a draped-cloth grid simulation
- Rename "3D Worlds & Cloth Physics" capability to "3D Work & Particle Systems"

parsed_message.body:

parsed_message.raw:
Fix Sampler playback bugs, make Pitch Bend a live modulator, per-folder sample rescans

- Sampler: fix reverse/loop toggles not taking effect on already-playing
  voices, clamp range drags to voices mid-flight, add explicit Play/Stop,
  draggable start/end grips plus numeric fields, and per-folder Refresh
  so rescanning one library folder no longer wipes the others' index
- Pitch Bend: convert from a note-chain semitone-shift node (which could
  only snap new notes, never bend one already sounding) into a live
  IModulator wired into a synth's own pitch input, matching a real wheel
- Wavetable: add a "bend" knob wired to the same continuous pitch path
- Add NullModulatorNode as a junction/probe point for modulator chains
- MeterRing::ReadLatest() drains the ring instead of reading one sample
  per frame, fixing meter lag against a producer writing once per block
- crude_json: accept/round-trip UTF-8 bytes instead of truncating on
  non-ASCII characters (was silently blanking sample index entries with
  accented filenames)
- Consolidate old FilterDefs color-grading nodes into "color adjustments"
- Transient Shaper visualizer now traces the actual shaped envelope
  instead of a fixed decay curve, with a dim unshaped reference line

  per-vertex colour the same way Render3DNode's GpuMesh already does,
  so a Set Color node's output actually looks tinted in its own

  either pin actually switches Set Color into that mode instead of
  just filling the field.

- Link redraw (rebuilding ed::Link visuals from live wiring state) now
  covers Set Color's paletteInput, so a palette connection shows up as
  a link on canvas again after whatever triggers this rebuild.

Shared viewport camera, link-drag-to-search, and safer NewPatch teardown

- SharedViewportCamera: a node's inline mini-viewport and its
  viewport-panel card now agree on orbit rotation (shared per node
  index via gNodeCameras), and the panel card gains its own
  drag-to-orbit/scroll-to-zoom, matching the inline preview. Render3D
  keeps its own separate camera, untouched by any of this.
- Link-drag-to-search: dropping a cable on empty canvas now opens the
  node search with compatible types suggested first, and wires the
  connection automatically once one is picked. The pin-compatibility
  and wiring logic used by both plain link creation and this new path
  is unified into IsInputSlotCompatible/WireInputSlot.
- NewPatch retires nodes/viewports instead of destroying them
  synchronously, since it can now run mid-frame from ApplyPatchData
  (Undo/Redo) after this frame's draw list already queued AddImage()
  calls against their GL textures - freeing those names immediately
  risked a one-frame flash of reused/garbage texture content.
- Updated INFINITE_UNDOTEST to re-resolve its GeometryNode pointer
  after each Undo()/Redo(): ApplyPatchData respawns a genuinely new
  node object every time now, so a pointer held across the call is
  stale afterward (previously this coincidentally worked only because
  the old node was freed synchronously and the allocator reused its
  address for the respawned one).

parsed_message.title: Phase 4: selection as an input, not four operators
parsed_message.description: Phase 4: selection as an input, not four operators
parsed_message.body:
Adds GeometryOpNode::selectionOnly (and DisplacementNode's own copy for
Twist/Displace's per-vertex case): when set and the incoming mesh
carries a face selection, Delete/Transform/Extrude/Solidify/Wireframe/
Triangulate/Normals/Explode/Twist restrict to the selected faces and
pass the rest through untouched. Off (the default) is unchanged from
before this field existed.
kDeleteSelected/kTransformSelected/kExtrudeSelected are kept at their
saved-patch enum indices as deprecated aliases - MigrateDeprecatedOp,
called from ApplyPatchData right after a node's params load, rewrites
them in place to (kDelete/kTransform/kExtrude, selectionOnly=true) so
an old patch keeps meaning what it did. They stay registered with
NodeFactory (old patches and internal fixtures still resolve them by
name) but are filtered out of the interactive spawn popup, the search
panel and the operation dropdown by name/IsSpawnable.
Migration is deliberately not hooked into ReloadDerivedState (shared
with copy/paste): once ApplyPatchData migrates a live node it stays
migrated, so copy/paste of it never needs to re-normalize, and the
round-trip self-test's generic param fuzzer (which can otherwise drive
a plain Select node's `op` field into the deprecated range) doesn't
mistake the normalization for dropped values.
Adds INFINITE_PHASE4TEST covering both this phase's "done means" risk
points directly: selectionOnly on/off behavior for Transform/Delete/
Extrude, and a simulated pre-phase-4 save (no selectionOnly key at all)
loading to the same geometry after migration.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Phase 2b: generic geometry connect/disconnect/rebuild via GeometryInputSlot

Adds INode::GeometryInputSlot(slot), returning the address of the pointer
field backing a node's geometry input at that slot (or nullptr if it has
none). ~15 geometry-consuming node classes implement it with a one-to-five
line override.

The four hand-maintained per-node-class dynamic_cast ladders collapse into
generic loops over this accessor:
  - ConnectGeometrySlot: one `*node->GeometryInputSlot(slot) = geo` instead
    of a case per class.
  - QueryNewLink: validation and the duplicate assignment block both
    collapse to a single check/assignment through the accessor - one path
    instead of two that had to agree.
  - DisconnectAllTo: one loop over every node x every geometry slot nulling
    matches against the dying source. This is where the use-after-free risk
    goes away - a new node type can't forget to register here.
  - The patch-save and node-editor link-rebuild passes both walk the same
    accessor instead of duplicating the per-class list a third and fourth
    time.

Render3DNode, MaterialNode and DisplacementNode keep small special cases
(camera/light pins; a texture map slot alongside geometry) since those pins
aren't plain geometry inputs.

Extends PATCHTEST's fixture and round-trip assertions to cover a second
Render 3D geometry slot, all three Instance on Points pins, Metaballs' cloud
and Path's curve pin - the exact links this refactor touches, since
CableRecord carries no type info and a slot-numbering slip would load
silently wrong. Adds DELETECRASHTEST: one source feeds Render 3D, every
Instance on Points pin, Metaballs and Path at once, gets deleted, and every
consumer cooks without crashing on the freed pointer.

Full hygiene suite (37/37) and all three geometry-transform-sweep checks
pass. `grep -rn "IPointCloudSource\|ICurveSource" src/` returns nothing.

parsed_message.title: Phase 2a: collapse IGeometrySource/IPointCloudSource/ICurveSource into one interface
parsed_message.description: Phase 2a: collapse IGeometrySource/IPointCloudSource/ICurveSource into one interface
parsed_message.body:
IPointCloudSource and ICurveSource are gone. IGeometrySource gains optional
GetPointCloud()/PointCloudRevision()/GetCurve()/CurveStamp() accessors that
default to "I don't have one" - a plain mesh source needs no changes, and
ParticleSystemNode/ImageToPointsNode/MeshToPointsNode/CurveNode now expose
their points or curve through the same interface everything else uses.
Consumer fields (InstanceOnPointsNode::cloudSource, MetaBallNode::cloudSource,
PathNode::curveSource) are retyped to IGeometrySource*, and the 21 call sites
that used to dynamic_cast to whichever of the three interfaces applied now
cast to IGeometrySource alone. Render3DNode's parallel clouds[kSlots] array
(Phase 1 scaffolding) is deleted - geometry[] carries everything now, and
BuildSceneSignature folds MeshRevision()/PointCloudRevision()/CurveStamp()
together so an animated cloud with a constant mesh revision still invalidates
the draw cache.
A plain mesh can now be dragged into a curve/cloud-only pin (PathNode's curve
slot, MetaBallNode's cloud slot) - it validates and the node just no-ops,
matching Blender's behavior of ignoring a component a source doesn't have,
rather than refusing the connection outright.
Full hygiene suite (36/36) and the geometry-transform-sweep checks pass.

parsed_message.description: Weld coincident vertices and dissolve triangulation diagonals in ToPoints
parsed_message.body:

vertex/edge sampling over-counted them. Weld first, then use adjacent
face-normal angle to tell a real edge from a triangulation diagonal.
